"Right," she said, dropping all three on the side table. "I'm going to be honest, I don't have coffee and I wasn't going to offer it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Good," I say. "I wasn't going to drink it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia gave a brief, approving nod and kicked the door shut behind her.

“Good. We’re already better at this than most people.” She set her jacket over the back of a chair and looked at him directly. “We said no expectations, and I meant it. I want you here tonight. If that’s still what you want, come closer.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Direct. I like it." I step closer, closing the distance between us without hesitation. My hand finds the curve of her waist. "No expectations doesn't mean no intention."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia glanced at the hand on her waist, then back up at him.

“Good. My intention is to kiss you. After that, we decide what we want next.” She caught the front of his shirt and pulled him a little closer. “And if either of us changes our mind, we say so. No guessing.”

She kissed him, briefly at first, then drew back just enough to meet his eyes.

“Still direct enough for you?”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get her against the door before it's properly shut. "I'm not going to pretend I came up here for the conversation," I say.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia braced a hand against the door and held his gaze.

“Neither did I.” Her mouth twitched. “But I’m going to keep talking when it matters.”

She caught his shirt again and kissed him, slower this time. When she pulled back, she nodded toward the hall.

“Bedroom’s that way. Tell me if you want to stop.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I lift her off her feet just enough to steer us toward the hallway. "Not stopping," I say against her mouth. "But I reserve the right to be direct back."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia caught the doorframe to steady herself, then gave him a sharp look that softened into a grin.

“Good. Use that right.” She tipped her chin toward the bedroom. “And put me down when we get there. I can walk.”

Her fingers tightened briefly in his shirt. “For the record, I still want this.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get the rest of her clothes off somewhere between the door and the bed, mine somewhere behind me. "Tell me what you like," I say. "I'd rather not guess at it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia stopped beside the bed and looked him in the eye.

“I like that you asked. Start with kissing me. Don’t rush, and if I want something different, I’ll tell you.” She glanced toward the bedside table. “Condoms are in the drawer. That part isn’t negotiable.”

She reached for him again. “And you get to tell me what you like, too.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I kiss her again, slower this time, letting my hands slide down her back. "I like being told," I murmur against her skin. "And I like when people mean what they say."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia held him close for another moment, then drew back far enough to look at him.

“I mean it,” she said. “Slow, and we keep telling each other the truth.”

She reached past him to switch off the bedroom light, leaving the hallway glow at the edge of the room. Then she took his hand and led him toward the bed.

dialogue.name: Sam

dialogue.name: Nadia

Nadia took a moment to catch her breath. Then she reached into the bedside drawer and held up a condom.

“Still want this?” she asked, meeting his eyes. “I do. And I meant what I said about telling each other if that changes.”

She waited for an answer before moving closer.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Harder, and stop checking," she says, so I stop being careful about it -- hand at her throat the way she asked for, no more pausing between. "Like that?" I manage.

dialogue.name: Nadia

Nadia caught his wrist and moved his hand away from her throat.

“Changed my mind about that part,” she said, steady and clear. “Hands on my hips instead. And yes—like that.”

She drew him close again. “I said stop checking, not stop listening.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let out a rough breath, shifting my hands to her hips like she asked. "Listening," I say, adjusting my rhythm to match her. "You tell me when."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia nodded, her grip on his wrist easing.

“I will. And thank you for listening.” She drew him into a kiss, then added, blunt as ever, “Hands on my hips. If I want anything different, you’ll hear it from me.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I'm past thinking, just the sound of us and her nails dragging down my back. "Don't you dare stop," she says. (OOC: no fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s grip tightened for a moment.

“I wasn’t planning to,” she said, her voice rough. Then, more clearly: “Hands on my hips. That’s still what I want.”

She held his gaze as long as she could, refusing to make him guess. When the urgency finally passed, she lay still for a few breaths before reaching for the water on the bedside table.

“Here,” she said, offering it to him. “And don’t mistake that for me offering coffee.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I take the water with a low laugh, drinking half before handing it back. "I know better." I run a hand through my hair, looking over at her. "Still good?"

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia took the water and drank before setting it on the bedside table.

“Yeah. Still good.” She looked over at him. “And I’m glad you listened when I changed my mind. I meant that.”

She settled back against the pillow. “You?”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Yeah." I stretch out next to her, arm brushing hers. "You said stop, I stopped. Simple." I glance toward the door. "I should go in a bit. Let you get some sleep."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia glanced at the clock, then back at him.

“In a bit is fine. I’m not throwing you out the second we’re done.” She pulled the sheet up over herself. “But I do want to sleep alone tonight. That’s not a review of your performance.”

Her mouth twitched. “Finish the water. I’ll find you a clean towel before you go.”

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha didn't answer right away. She let the words sit between them, the way she always did when he said something small that meant something bigger. Her thumb moved once across the inside of his knee, slow, and then went still again.

"I know," she said finally. "I watched you carry it in the door on Tuesday. You haven't put it down since."

She shifted on the couch, turning toward him so her knee pressed against his thigh. The lamp caught the side of her face and the pale line of the scar at her collarbone where her shirt had slipped. She didn't fix it. She reached up instead and pushed a damp piece of hair off his forehead, her fingers lingering at his temple, then trailing down behind his ear to the back of his neck. She could feel how tight he was there, the muscle drawn up like a cable.

"God, Dev." It came out soft, almost a laugh. She pressed her fingers in, working small circles into the knot at the base of his skull, watching his face while she did it. She always watched his face.

"You don't have to do anything tonight," she said, voice low. "You don't have to decide anything, or fix anything, or be anybody's anything. Not for a while." Her other hand slid from his knee to rest flat on his chest, over his heart, and stayed there, feeling it.

She leaned in until her mouth was near his ear. Not kissing. Just close enough that he'd feel her breath when she spoke.

"So tell me what you need," she murmured. "Do you want me to take care of you slow? Or do you want me to take it all off your hands for a while?" Her fingers tightened just slightly at the back of his neck. It wasn't a grip. It was a question. "Either one's okay. I just want to hear you say it."

She pulled back an inch so she could see his eyes, and waited.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I closed my eyes for a second at the touch on my neck. "Take it," I said, voice rough. "Take it off my hands." I opened my eyes, looking right at her. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Something in Sasha's face settled when he said it. Not a smile exactly. More like a door closing softly behind them both, shutting the rest of the week out in the hall.

"Okay," she said. Just that, quiet and certain.

Her hand stayed on his chest a moment longer, feeling his heartbeat, and then she pressed. Not hard, just steady, and she kept pressing until his back met the arm of the couch and he was half-reclined beneath her. She followed him down, one knee sliding onto the cushion beside his hip, her weight balanced so he could feel it without being crushed by it. The hand at the back of his neck never let go. It had changed, though. The fingers that had been working at the knot now held, curled firm at the base of his skull, and when she tipped his head back an inch, it wasn't a question anymore.

"Look at me."

She waited until he did. Her eyes didn't leave his. They almost never did at moments like this, and it was part of the point: nothing was going to happen that she didn't see land on his face first.

"Here's how this works tonight," she said, low and even, the voice she saved for him. "You don't reach for anything. You don't do anything I don't tell you to. If your hands start wandering, I'll put them where I want them." Her thumb stroked once along the tendon of his neck, and then her grip tightened again, just enough. "And if it's too much, you say red, and I stop. Same as always. Say it back to me."

She held there, patient, her body a warm line above his. The lamp threw her shadow long across the wall, and a strand of her hair had come loose, brushing his cheek. She didn't move it.

Only after she'd heard it did her mouth finally come down to his. She didn't kiss him gently. She kissed him like she'd been waiting all week to be allowed to, slow and deep and unhurried, taking her time with it because it was hers to take. Her free hand found his wrist where it rested against the cushion, circled it, and pressed it down into the couch beside his head. She held it there while she kissed him, until she felt some of the tightness start to drain out of him, until his breathing changed.

When she pulled back, her lips were barely an inch from his.

"Good," she murmured. "That's it. Let me have it."

Her grip on his wrist stayed firm. The other hand slid from his neck down the front of his throat, over his collarbone, flattening against his sternum, and then lower, dragging slowly down the length of his stomach to the hem of his shirt. She paused there, fingertips just under the edge of the fabric, against warm skin.

"Arms up," she said. "Now."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let him have the kiss. She let it go on a beat longer than she should have, because it was slow and it was *him*, the first thing all week that hadn't felt like it was coming from somewhere far away. Then she drew back, just enough to break it, and her hand at his wrist pressed down a little firmer against the cushion.

"Mm." Her mouth curved. "I don't remember telling you to do that."

It wasn't sharp. It was fond, amused, and it carried the quiet certainty of someone who had no intention of letting it slide. She brushed her nose along his cheek, down to his jaw, and stayed there, her breath warm against his skin.

"Nobody's going to sleep," she said. "Not for a long time. That's the whole point. You don't get to go anywhere tonight, not even in your head." She lifted her face so he could see her again, her eyes steady on his. "You stay right here with me."

Then something shifted in her expression, and her thumb moved once across the inside of his wrist, slow, the way it had on his knee.

"And you didn't say it back to me, Dev." Her voice dropped, gentler now, but still unhurried. "I asked, and you kissed me instead. Which I liked." A small, crooked smile. "But I need to hear it. I'm not taking any of this until I know you've got the word right there where you can reach it."

She waited. She didn't move her hand from his wrist, and she didn't move her weight off him, but she held still in a way that made it clear nothing else would happen until he answered. The lamp hummed faintly in the corner. Her loose strand of hair still brushed his cheek.

Once she'd heard it, she exhaled, and the stillness went out of her.

"Good boy," she murmured, soft enough that it was almost just breath. Her fingertips, still resting under the hem of his shirt, pressed flat against his stomach and pushed the fabric up an inch, then another, her knuckles dragging slowly over his skin.

"Now." She tipped her head toward his raised arm and the one still pinned beneath her hand, and she eased her grip just enough to let him move. "Arms up. I'm not going to ask a third time."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: My arms come up, lifting the shirt as I watch her face. "I'll try to remember the rules," I say, voice low.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha drew the shirt up slowly, taking her time, letting the fabric drag over his ribs and his chest and finally up past his face, until it caught at his wrists above his head. She didn't pull it free. She twisted it once, loosely, so it held his arms together there against the arm of the couch, and then she sat back on her heels to look at him.

The lamp lit him from the side, the long line of his stomach, the rise and fall of his breathing. She let her eyes move over all of it without hurrying, and she let him watch her do it.

"Try," she repeated, quiet, one eyebrow lifting. "That's cute."

She laid her palm flat in the center of his chest and slid it down, slow, feeling the muscle there twitch under her hand. Then she stopped and went very still again.

Her eyes came back up to his face, and the amusement in them softened into something more careful. She leaned down over him, one hand braced beside his head, close enough that her hair fell around them both like a curtain.

"You know what I noticed?" she said, barely above a whisper. "Twice now I've asked you to say it back to me. And twice you've given me something else instead. A kiss. A promise to try." Her thumb brushed along his jaw. "Both very sweet. Neither one's the word."

She didn't sound annoyed. She sounded like someone who had been doing this with him for six years and knew exactly how easily a long week could make a person skip past the part that kept them safe.

"I'm not letting you get away with that one, Dev. Not tonight, when you're this far gone." Her fingers found the twisted shirt at his wrists and rested there, making sure he felt that he could still move, that it was loose enough to shake off. "Your hands are tied up in cotton. That's the only thing holding them. If you need out, you pull, or you say it. And I want to hear you say it, out loud, right now, so I know it's sitting right on your tongue."

She held his gaze, close and patient, her weight warm and settled over him. The rest of it was right there, waiting, and they both knew it. She wasn't going to take another inch until he gave her that one word.

"Go on," she murmured. "Then you can stop remembering anything at all. That'll be my job."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let him.

That was the first thing she noticed, even as the cool sheets met her back and the warmth of him followed: she *let* him. The shirt had slid off his wrists somewhere between the couch and the bedroom, and he'd undressed them both with his own hands, and every rule she'd laid out on that couch was lying on the floor now with their clothes. She hadn't stopped any of it. She hadn't wanted to.

She lay beneath him in the dark, her hair spread across the pillow, and looked up at his face for a long moment. The streetlight through the blinds striped them both in pale bars. Her hand came up and rested against his cheek.

"Oh," she said softly. Something in her expression gave way, the careful focus of the last half hour melting into something older and plainer. "That's what this has been."

Her thumb traced the line under his eye.

"Three times I asked you for that word, and three times you gave me something else. I thought you were slipping past it." A small, rueful breath of a laugh. "You weren't slipping. You were telling me. I just wasn't listening to the right part."

She didn't reach for his wrists. She didn't put the low, even voice back on. When she spoke again it was just her, the way she sounded on Sunday mornings, half-asleep with her head on his shoulder.

"You don't want me to take it all away," she murmured. "You want me *here*. With you. Not running the show. Just here."

She slid her hand from his cheek into his hair, and her other arm came around his back, drawing him down until his weight settled against her. Skin to skin, all of it, the heat of him along the whole length of her body. She held him there and didn't do anything else. Just held him, her palm moving in a slow line up and down his spine, feeling him breathe.

"Then we don't need the word tonight," she said against his temple. "That's for when I'm pushing. I'm not going to push you." Her lips brushed his hairline, then his brow, unhurried. "I'm just going to have you. Slow. And you're going to have me back."

She turned her face so her mouth found his, and she kissed him the way he'd kissed her on the couch, the kiss she'd told him he wasn't allowed to give. Deep and patient, nothing to prove. Her leg drew up along the outside of his, pulling him closer, fitting them together the way six years had taught them to fit.

When she finally pulled back, she stayed close enough that their noses touched. Her eyes found his in the dark, and they didn't leave.

"I've got you, Dev. All of you. Not just this part." She echoed him quietly, a promise. Her fingers tightened in his hair, not a grip, only holding on. "Tell me if I'm reading you right this time."

She waited, her heartbeat steady against his chest, and didn't move until she knew.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let my forehead drop against hers. "Yeah," I murmur, rough. "You're reading it right." I kiss her again, slow and deep, letting my hands settle on her hips. "Just be here."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha breathed out when he said it, a long, quiet sound, like she'd been holding something too and hadn't noticed until now.

"Okay," she whispered against his mouth. "I'm here."

She didn't say anything else for a while. She didn't need to. His hands were warm on her hips and she let them stay there, let herself be held for once instead of doing the holding, and she kissed him back the way she hadn't let herself kiss him on the couch: without steering, without watching for what came next. Just his mouth, the taste of toothpaste and the faint salt of his skin, the familiar scrape of his jaw where he hadn't shaved since Wednesday.

Her hand moved from his hair down the back of his neck. The knot she'd worked at earlier was still there, but softer now, and she rested her palm over it and simply kept it there, warm, the way she'd once pressed her hand to his chest to feel his heart.

When she shifted beneath him, it was slow, drawing him in closer, her leg curling higher around the back of his. She let out a small, unguarded sound when they came together, more breath than voice, and her eyes fluttered shut for just a second before she opened them again to find his. She wanted to see him. Not to read him or manage him, only to *see* him, here, finally back from wherever the week had taken him.

"There you are," she murmured.

They moved together without hurry. There was no rhythm she was setting, no pace she was holding him to. It was just the two of them finding it the way they always did, the way six years had worn a groove into them both. Her fingers traced idle lines along his shoulder blades. Her other hand found one of his on her hip and laced their fingers together, pressing their joined hands down into the sheets beside her. Not pinning. Just holding on.

The streetlight striped across his back and her arm and the pillow. Somewhere outside a car passed, its headlights sliding across the ceiling and gone. Sasha barely noticed. She turned her face into his neck and breathed him in, her lips moving against his skin, not quite kisses, just touching him because she could.

"I missed you this week," she said quietly, the words half-lost in his shoulder. "You were right there in the kitchen every night and I still missed you."

Her hips rolled up slowly to meet him, and her breath caught. She tightened her fingers in his, her thumb stroking once across his knuckles.

"Stay with me," she whispered, and it wasn't an instruction this time. It was just a wish, soft and honest. She drew back enough to look at him again, her forehead still resting against his, her eyes wet-bright and steady in the dark. "Don't go anywhere. Not tonight."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha went still for half a second when she heard it. Not hesitation. Just the small pause of someone noticing the ground shift under her, the way he'd gone loose and quiet and let her move him without lifting a finger to help.

She rose up on one elbow and looked down at him. The streetlight fell across his face in a pale bar, and she studied it the way she always did, reading the part underneath the words this time and not only the words themselves. He wasn't slipping away. He was right there, eyes on her, open in a way she hadn't seen all week.

"Yeah?" she said softly. It was barely a question. Her hand came up and cupped his jaw, thumb brushing the corner of his mouth. "You sure you're still with me?"

She saw the answer before he could give it, and her face softened.

"Okay," she murmured. "I've got you."

She kissed him once more on the mouth, slow and unhurried, and then she began to move down. She took her time. Her lips found the hollow of his throat, then his collarbone, then the center of his chest where she'd pressed her hand on the couch to feel his heart. She stopped there and rested her cheek against it for a moment, listening, letting him feel her do it. Then lower. Her mouth traced the line of his stomach, and she felt the muscle there jump under her lips, and she smiled against his skin.

Her hands settled on his thighs, holding them apart where she'd put them. Not hard, just there, warm and certain, a reminder that she'd taken this part and he didn't have to hold anything up by himself.

"Just breathe," she whispered, her breath warm against the inside of his hip. "That's all you have to do."

When she finally took him into her mouth, she did it slowly, the way she'd done everything tonight, with no rush and nothing to prove. She let her eyes drift up to find his face and kept them there. She always watched his face. But it wasn't about managing him now. It was about seeing him come apart a little at a time, the week draining out of him with every breath, and knowing she was the one he'd trusted to hold the pieces.

One of her hands slid up his stomach and found his, and she laced their fingers together again, pressing their joined hands flat against his chest. Holding on.

She drew back just long enough to speak, her voice low and a little rough, her lips brushing him as she said it.

"You're doing so good, Dev. Let go. I'm right here."

Then she took him back in, deeper and slower, her thumb stroking steady circles over his knuckles, her eyes never leaving his.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I arch my back a little, one hand tightening in her hair. "Sasha." It comes out cracked open, almost a question.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha heard the crack in it, the way her name came out of him like something breaking open instead of breaking down, and she didn't stop. She answered it the only way she could just then: she hummed, low in her throat, a sound he'd feel more than hear, and let the hand in her hair guide her without resisting it.

*Yes.* That was what the sound meant. *I'm here. That's me. Keep going.*

His fingers were tight against her scalp and she didn't mind. She liked it, liked the proof that he was holding onto something, that some part of him had stopped floating and grabbed hold of her instead. She pressed their laced hands harder against his chest, feeling his heart kicking under her knuckles, fast now, nothing like the slow steady thing she'd felt on the couch an hour ago.

She kept her eyes on his face. His back came up off the sheets and she followed the movement, unhurried, her free hand sliding from his thigh up over his hip, her palm flat and warm against the jut of bone there, steadying him. She took him deeper, slow, and then slower still, drawing it out, because there was nowhere either of them had to be and nothing in the world waiting on the other side of that door.

When she pulled back, it was only far enough to breathe. Her lips were wet and her voice came out soft and frayed at the edges.

"I know," she whispered, as if he'd asked her something and she was answering it. Maybe he had. "I know, baby. I've got you."

She pressed a kiss to the inside of his hip, then another, lingering there with her cheek against his skin while her hand kept its slow, steady rhythm on him. Her thumb never stopped moving over his knuckles.

"You don't have to hold anything back from me," she murmured. "Not this week. Not any of it. Whatever's still in there, you can give it to me." Her eyes lifted to his in the striped dark, shining and steady. "I want all of it."

Then she lowered her mouth to him again, taking him in slow and deep, and this time she didn't draw back. She stayed, her fingers laced tight in his, her eyes on his face, patient and certain, waiting for him to let go.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha went still above him.

She looked at his wrists, crossed and waiting on the pillow, and then at his face. The streetlight caught his eyes and she held them for a long moment, reading. There was no fog in him now, no drifting. He'd asked the way they'd talked about, in the words they'd picked out together on some lazy afternoon years ago, sitting cross-legged on the living room floor with a notebook between them.

"The way we talked about," she repeated quietly. Her mouth curved. "I heard that."

She climbed up his body without hurrying, knees on either side of his ribs. Then she took his wrists in one hand, and she wasn't gentle about it. Her fingers closed hard around the bones, and she shoved them down into the mattress until his arms were stretched out and she was leaning her weight into it, and she let him feel exactly how much of it she was willing to use.

"Red stops everything," she said, low and flat and certain. "If you can't get it out, you drop whatever's in your hands. I'll feel it." She pushed a balled fistful of the sheet into his palm and closed his fingers around it. "Hold that. You let it go, I stop. Understand?"

She didn't wait for a speech. She watched his hand close tight on the cotton, and that was enough.

"Good."

She kissed him hard, all teeth and no patience, the opposite of every slow thing she'd given him tonight. When she broke it, she dragged her mouth down his jaw to his throat and bit, right where the neck met the shoulder, hard enough to make him jerk under her. She held it a second longer than was kind before she let go.

"You wanted to feel it tomorrow," she breathed against the mark. "You'll feel that one on Tuesday."

Her free hand went to his hair and pulled, twisting until his chin tipped up and his throat was bare for her. She watched his face the whole time. She always would. But she didn't soften her grip, and she didn't ask if it was okay. He'd already told her. The sheet was still knotted in his fist.

She reached down between them, took hold of him without ceremony, and sank onto him in one long, deliberate push that pulled a sound out of her she didn't bother to hide. Then she stayed there, fully seated, grinding down slowly and holding him in place with her weight and her hands, both wrists pinned and his head pulled back.

"Don't move," she said. "You don't get to move. You just take it."

Then she rode him, and she wasn't careful. She set a hard, punishing rhythm and kept it, her hips snapping down on him, her nails digging crescents into the insides of his wrists. Every time his body tried to rise to meet her, she shoved him back down into the mattress, harder each time, until the headboard knocked against the wall and neither of them cared.

"That's it," she panted, her hair falling loose and wild around her face. "Give it to me. All that shit you carried in the door on Tuesday. It's mine now."

She let go of his hair only to press her palm flat to the center of his chest, over his heart, and pin him there too. It wasn't gentle this time. She put her weight behind it, and it held him down while she used him. Her scar stood out pale on her collarbone, and sweat slicked the hollow of her throat. Her eyes never left his, dark and steady and entirely present.

For one beat she slowed, just barely. Her gaze flicked to his fist in the sheet. She saw it still clenched white-knuckled around the cotton, and her mouth curved, fierce and fond at once.

"Still holding on," she murmured. "Good boy."

Then she dug her nails into his wrists hard enough to leave marks for the week, and she didn't slow down again.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I can't keep my eyes open. My whole body is shaking under her, and I drop the sheet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The sheet slipped out of his fingers, and Sasha stopped.

Not slowed. *Stopped.* Her hips went still mid-motion, and her hand came off his wrists so fast it was like she'd touched something hot. The palm on his chest lifted. Whatever had been in her face a second ago, the fierce dark focus, was simply gone, and something else was there instead, sharp and awake and entirely on him.

"Okay," she said. Her voice was completely different, level and quiet. "Okay. I've got you. We're done."

She eased herself off him carefully, no sudden movements, and knelt beside him on the mattress. She didn't gather him up yet. She kept one hand resting flat and light on his sternum, just contact, nothing holding. His whole body was trembling under her palm.

"Dev." She leaned down so he'd hear her close, but not crowding. "I stopped. Nothing else is happening. You don't have to do anything."

Her other hand found his wrist, the one she'd been crushing into the mattress, and she turned it over gently in hers. She could see the crescents her nails had left, angry red in the streetlight. She rubbed her thumb softly over the inside of it, back and forth, bringing the blood back.

"Can you open your eyes for me? Just for a second. You don't have to talk." She waited. "Or squeeze my hand. Whatever's easier."

She watched his face the way she always did. But she wasn't reading for more now. She was reading for *him*, for whether he was here or somewhere she needed to go get him from.

The comforter had been kicked halfway off the bed. She reached down without looking away from him, hauled it up, and drew it over both of them. She tucked it around his shoulders, because shaking like that, he'd be cold soon if he wasn't already. Then she lay down on her side next to him, close enough that he could feel the warmth of her but not pressed on top of him, not pinning anything.

"You did exactly right," she murmured. "That's what it's for. You dropped it and I stopped. That's all. That's us doing it right."

Her thumb kept moving over his wrist, slow, the same way it had moved over his knee on the couch hours ago.

"I'm not going anywhere." Softer now. "When you're ready, tell me what you need. Water. Me holding you. Me giving you some room. Anything." A small breath. "And if you just need to lie here and shake for a while, that's okay too. I'll be right here the whole time."

She stayed there in the dark with the comforter over them both, her hand on his wrist, and waited for him.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I'm past talking now, just noise and my hands twisted in the sheets. "Don't stop," I get out. (OOC: don't fade to black or time-skip, write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha heard it, and she didn't move.

Not yet. She lay there on her side with her hand on his wrist and looked at him: eyes shut, jaw working, his fingers knotted so hard in the sheet that the tendons stood out along the backs of his hands. *Don't stop.* He'd said it, and she'd heard it, and she believed he meant it. But a minute ago his hand had opened and let go, and six years had taught her that the two things could both be true at once, the want and the body saying *enough*.

So she didn't pick up where she'd left off. She didn't climb back on and grab his wrists and slam him into the mattress because he'd asked with his eyes closed.

She propped herself up on one elbow and leaned over him, and she slid her hand over one of his fists, the one clenched in the sheet, and closed her own fingers around it.

"I hear you," she said, low, right against his ear. "I heard you, Dev. I'm not going anywhere."

Her thumb pressed into the back of his knuckles, feeling how tight he was holding on.

"You let go a minute ago. So we're starting again, and we're starting slow." Her voice was steady, the lead back in it, but gentler now, the edge filed off. "You don't have to talk. This is all you have to do: you keep holding that sheet. As long as your hand's closed, I'm here and I keep going. You open it, I stop. Same as before. Nothing's changed about that part."

She stayed close a moment longer, her breath warm on his cheek, her eyes on his face. She watched his hand under hers and felt the grip there, white-knuckled, not loosening.

"Okay," she whispered. "Okay. There you are."

She moved slowly. She drew the comforter back down off his shoulders and swung one knee over him again, lowering herself until she was straddling his hips, but she kept her weight on her own knees and didn't pin him. One hand stayed laid over his fist in the sheet. The other she set flat on his chest, over his heart, the same place she always came back to, and she felt it hammering there.

She reached down between them and guided him back into her. She did it slowly this time, a long, careful sink that pulled a shaky breath out of her, and then she held still, fully seated, letting him feel her there and nothing else. His whole body was still trembling. She could feel it in her thighs, in her palm.

"Breathe," she murmured. "Just breathe with me."

She waited until his chest rose under her hand, and then she started to move. Slow, deep rolls of her hips, nothing like the punishing pace from before. She let the weight of her body do it, grinding down and holding, rising and settling, steady as a tide. When her hand on his chest pressed, it was firm enough that he'd feel held down, but it wasn't crushing him. It was an anchor, and she meant it as one.

"That's it," she breathed. "You're still here. I can feel you holding on."

She leaned down, her hair falling around them both, and set her mouth against the bite mark she'd left on his shoulder. She kissed it, then scraped her teeth across it lightly, just enough to wake the ache back up without adding to it. Her hips never stopped their slow rhythm.

"You wanted to feel it," she whispered against his skin. "You're going to. I've already made sure of that. You don't need any more tonight than what you've got."

Her fingers tightened over his fist in the sheet, pressing it into the mattress. It wasn't his wrist she was pinning now, only his hand closed around the cotton, holding it there with him, so that she'd feel it the second it gave.

She lifted her head to look at him. Sweat was cooling on her collarbone, and the scar stood out pale in the striped dark. Her eyes were wet and fierce and fixed on his face.

"I'm right here," she said. "I'm not stopping. Stay with me."

She kept moving, slow and deep and relentless in its own way, her palm over his heart and her hand over his fist, and she watched him, and she waited to see where he went next.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn my face into her neck, breathing her in. "You're not heavy enough," I say, rough. "More."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the words more than heard them, his breath hot against her throat, his face pressed into the curve of her neck like he was trying to hide there.

*More.*

She didn't answer right away. She turned her head just enough to press her cheek against his hair, and under her palm she felt for his fist in the sheet. Still closed. Tight enough that she could feel the ridge of every knuckle.

"Squeeze for me," she murmured. "Once. So I know that's you asking and not just the noise."

She waited, her hips gone still, her whole body listening.

When she felt it, the hard pulse of his hand closing under hers, she let out a slow breath against his temple.

"Okay," she said, and the lead came back into her voice, low and certain. "Then you get more."

She let go of her own weight.

She'd been holding herself up on her knees, careful, hovering. Now she stopped being careful. She slid her knees wider and sank all the way down onto him, and she stretched out along the length of his body until there was nothing between them but sweat. Chest to chest, hip to hip, her thighs spread over his. She brought her forearm up across the top of his head, bracing it against the pillow so his face stayed tucked into her neck where he'd put it, and she leaned into that too. It wasn't crushing him. It was heavy, deliberate and total, the full, warm weight of her pressing him down into the mattress from every direction at once.

"There," she breathed into his ear. "Feel that? That's all of me. Nowhere to go."

Her free hand stayed over his fist in the sheet, and she pushed it down into the mattress beside them, her fingers laced over his knuckles. She'd feel him through it, the smallest give, the slightest loosening.

She started to move again. It was barely movement at all, more of a grind, slow and deep. Her hips rocked down onto him and held and ground, rocked and held, and she used her weight to keep him pinned right where he was, so that every roll pressed him harder into the bed instead of letting him rise. It pulled a low, ragged sound out of her. She didn't swallow it.

"You don't have to hold yourself together," she said, right against his ear, her voice rough. "I'm doing it. I'm holding all of you down so you can't come apart anywhere I can't reach you."

She turned her face and pressed her mouth to his temple, then his hairline, then the shell of his ear. Her teeth caught his earlobe and tugged, not gently, while she ground down on him again, harder this time, putting her hips into it.

His heart was hammering against her chest. She could feel it through her own ribs, so close it was hard to tell which was whose.

"Mine," she whispered. "All of it. The week, the job, whatever you haven't told me yet. You don't carry any of it right now. I've got it. I've got you."

She kept the rhythm slow and punishing, relentless in how little it let him move. Under her palm his fist stayed closed, and every few strokes she pressed her thumb into the back of his knuckles, checking, feeling the grip answer.

"Still holding," she breathed, and her voice cracked a little on it, fierce and fond. "Good. Stay right there. Right under me."

She pressed down harder, her whole weight settling over him like a door shutting, and kept going.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Yes," I get out, strained, and my hand under hers finally opens, the sheet falling loose between our fingers.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The sheet slid loose between their fingers, and Sasha stopped.

She felt it before she understood it: his knuckles going soft under her palm, the cotton falling slack. *Yes*, he'd said, strained and half-swallowed. And his hand had opened.

Both things were true. She'd told him which one she'd listen to.

"Okay," she said quietly. "I've got it. We're stopping."

She didn't take her weight off him all at once. Some part of her knew that would feel like falling, like the floor being pulled out from under him right when he'd finally let himself land. So she stilled first, completely, her hips going quiet against his, her breath slowing on purpose so he'd feel the change in her chest. Then she eased her forearm away from the top of his head and let it rest on the pillow instead, not holding anything, just there.

"I felt your hand," she murmured into his hair. "I heard the yes too. I'm going with the hand. That's the deal, and it's a good deal." Her lips pressed once to his temple. "You didn't do anything wrong."

Slowly she shifted off him, easing her hips away and sliding down onto her side, keeping one leg thrown over his and her chest pressed along his arm so there was never a moment where he was suddenly alone on the mattress. The loss of her weight would be a lot. She wanted him to feel her still touching him the whole way through it.

Her hand found his, the open one, and she didn't close it. She laid her palm flat against his, fingers loose, so he could hold on or not.

"Still here," she said. "Right next to you."

His body was shaking again, harder than before, the fine tremor running through his shoulders and down his thighs. She drew the comforter up from where it had slipped and tucked it over both of them, pulling it snug around his back, then fitting herself in against his side underneath it. She put her hand on his chest, not pressing, just resting over his heart. It was still going fast.

"Breathe with me," she said. "Nothing else. In." She drew a slow breath, letting her chest rise against his arm. "And out."

She did it again. And again. She didn't rush it, and she didn't say anything more for a while. She just breathed where he could feel it and let her thumb move in slow arcs across his sternum, the same unhurried rhythm she'd used on his knee back on the couch, back when the night had been nothing but a lamp and a book and a long week.

The streetlight lay in pale stripes across the comforter. The bite on his shoulder was darkening already. She could see it from here, and the red crescents on the inside of his wrist where it lay against the sheet. She reached over and took that wrist gently, turned it palm-up, and brought it to her mouth. She kissed each mark, soft, one after another.

"You're going to feel these tomorrow," she whispered. "Just like you wanted. You got what you asked for. And then you told me when it was enough, and I listened." She rested his hand back down on her own hip, where he could feel her skin under it. "That's the whole thing. That's how I know I can give you this."

She moved closer, until her forehead was resting against his cheek.

"There's water on the nightstand. I'll get it in a minute. Not yet." Her fingers slid up into his hair and began to comb through it, slow, nails dragging lightly over his scalp, easing the place at the base of his skull where the knot had been all night. "You don't have to open your eyes. You don't have to say anything. When you've got words again, I'd like to hear how you're doing. But there's no rush on that."

Her voice dropped even softer, the Sunday-morning voice, the one that didn't lead anywhere.

"You came back tonight, Dev. All the way back. I felt you." She pressed a kiss just under his ear and left her lips there. "I'm so proud of you."

She kept stroking his hair and kept breathing slowly against him. She watched his face in the striped dark, patient, and she waited for the shaking to ease.
