dialogue.content: I drop my forehead against her shoulder, breathing hard. "Water's a good idea." I push myself up off the bed. "I'll get it. Where are your glasses?"

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia stayed sprawled across the sheets, still catching her breath. She pointed down the hall with a lazy flick of her fingers.

“Kitchen. Cupboard to the left of the sink.” She glanced at him. “And bring two. I’m not sharing yours after you’ve been sweating all over me.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let out a short laugh. "Fair enough." I head to the kitchen, grabbing two glasses from the cupboard she pointed out. I fill them and come back, handing one to her. "Here. Don't want my sweat in your water."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia took the glass and drank half of it in one go. She lowered it with a satisfied breath.

“Look at you, following instructions.” She glanced at him over the rim. “Don’t get used to praise.”

She set the glass on the bedside table, then rubbed a hand over one of the marks on her hip. “You left evidence. I’ll decide tomorrow whether I’m annoyed about that.” A beat passed, and her mouth tipped into a tired smirk. “Right now, though, you can stay put and finish your water.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Evidence is a good look on you." I take a long drink before setting my glass down next to hers. "I'm not going anywhere. Your bed's more comfortable than mine anyway."

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: I want the same thing

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: Now quit interviewing me and kiss me

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
rung_labels.evidence: That was very much not a complaint

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
rung_labels.evidence: Now quit asking and keep going

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
rung_labels.evidence: then went slack against the sheets

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia got the door open with her shoulder because her hands were full of keys and phone and the remains of a cigarette she had no intention of finishing.

"Right," she said, dropping all three on the side table. "I'm going to be honest, I don't have coffee and I wasn't going to offer it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Good," I say. "I wasn't going to drink it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia huffed something that might have been a laugh. She kicked her boots off without bothering to untie them. One landed on its side by the radiator and she left it there.

"Good," she echoed, and shrugged out of her jacket. It went over the back of a chair that already held two others. The flat was small and lived-in, a sofa with a blanket balled at one end, a stack of unopened post, a plant on the windowsill that was either thriving or dead depending on the light. She didn't apologise for any of it.

She turned to face him properly, leaning back against the side table with her arms loosely folded. Under the hallway bulb she looked a little less sharp than she had at the bar, eyeliner smudged at one corner, hair falling out of whatever she'd done with it at eight o'clock. Her gaze was still very direct.

"So. Ground rules, because I hate the awkward bit afterwards more than I hate saying this out loud." She held up a finger. "This is tonight. That's it. You can stay till morning if you pass out, but I'm not making breakfast either." A second finger. "If something's not working, say so. I will. I'm not going to lie there being polite about it, and I'd rather you didn't."

She dropped her hand and tilted her head toward the short corridor behind her, where a door stood half open onto a dark room and an unmade bed.

"Bedroom's that way. Bathroom's the other one, if you need it first." A pause. The corner of her mouth pulled up, not quite a smile, more like a dare. "And I'm still up for this, in case the walk over here left you wondering. Are you?"

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: *I lean back against the doorframe, crossing my arms.* "Still up for it. And I don't eat breakfast anyway." *I push off the wall and start unzipping my jacket.* "Lead the way."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's mouth did the thing again, the not-quite-smile, and this time it stuck around a second longer.

"Good answer," she said.

She pushed off the side table and didn't wait for his jacket to finish coming off. She caught the front of it where the zip had stopped halfway and used it to pull him the last step in. The kiss wasn't tentative. It tasted faintly of the cigarette and the gin she'd been drinking since ten, and she kissed the way she talked: straight to the point, no preamble, like she'd already decided and was mostly checking he'd keep up.

When she broke off she didn't go far. Her forehead was almost against his and her fingers were still hooked in his jacket.

"Right," she said, a bit breathless and clearly annoyed about it. "That's fine. That works."

She let go and walked backwards down the corridor, pulling the hair tie out as she went. Whatever was left of the eight-o'clock effort came down around her shoulders. She tossed the tie somewhere in the dark of the bedroom without looking where it landed.

The room was as honest as the rest of the flat. The duvet was half on the floor, a lamp stood on a stack of paperbacks, and a mug on the bedside table had definitely been there since Tuesday. She reached over, clicked the lamp on, and got a low yellow light that was kinder than the hallway bulb.

She turned back to him with her hands at the hem of her top, and stopped there, eyebrows raised.

"You're very slow with that jacket," she said. "Are you getting in here, or am I doing this on my own?"

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get her against the door before it's properly shut. "I'm not going to pretend I came up here for the conversation," I say.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
The door hit its frame with a soft thud behind her and didn't quite latch. Nadia didn't care. Her breath went out of her in a short, surprised sound that she'd have denied making if anyone asked.

"Oh, *good*," she said, and meant it.

Her hands were already at his jacket again, but this time she finished the job herself, shoving it back off his shoulders until it dropped somewhere around their feet. She didn't look to see where. Her head tipped back against the wood and she looked up at him with that same direct stare from the bar, except the edges of it had gone softer and darker in the lamplight.

"I didn't bring you up here for the conversation either," she said. "You were fine company. You're not *that* interesting."

It was said without any malice. If anything it was a compliment, in her language.

She pulled him down by the collar and kissed him again, slower this time, like she'd decided the first one had proved the point and now she could take her time about it. One of her hands slid up the back of his neck into his hair. The other found the hem of his shirt and stayed there, fingertips just under the fabric, warm against his skin.

When she pulled back it was only an inch.

"That," she murmured, "keep doing that. Whatever you're thinking of doing next, I'll tell you if it's wrong." Her mouth curved. "I doubt I'll need to."

Then she did what she'd threatened in the doorway. She took hold of the hem of her own top and pulled it over her head in one unceremonious movement, tossing it past his shoulder toward the chair in the corner. It missed. She ignored it.

She stayed leaning back against the door, bare-shouldered in the yellow light, hair a mess, eyeliner worse, and entirely unbothered by any of it. She raised one eyebrow at him.

"Your turn," she said. "And the bed's about four steps behind you, if you're planning to get there tonight."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: *I take the invitation, hands sliding up her sides to push her back against the door with another, deeper kiss.* "I know where the bed is." *My voice is rough.* "I'm not in a hurry."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's laugh came out against his mouth, low and a little unsteady, which clearly irritated her.

"Not in a hurry," she repeated, like she was testing the words for flaws. "God. You *would* be."

She didn't push him off, though. If anything she arched off the door into his hands. The wood was cool against her shoulder blades and he wasn't, and she noticed the difference in a way that made her go briefly, uncharacteristically quiet. Her fingers tightened in his hair and stayed there.

For a moment she let him set the pace. She kissed him back slowly, deliberately, matching him rather than leading, and there was something almost grudging in how well it was working on her. Her breathing had gone shallow. She could hear it in the quiet room and so could he, and she decided not to be embarrassed about it.

When she finally turned her face aside it was only far enough to speak, her cheek against his jaw.

"Fine," she said, a bit hoarse. "You win that one. Slow's good." Her hand slid from his hair down to the back of his neck and rested there, thumb moving absently along the edge of his collar. "I'm just not used to people who actually listen when I say what I want. It's throwing me off."

She tipped her head back against the door to look at him again. The lamplight caught the smudge of eyeliner, the flush climbing her throat, and the stubborn set of her mouth that said she was still, somehow, in charge of this in her own head.

Then she tugged at the hem of his shirt, once, pointedly.

"You still haven't done your turn," she said. "I'm not being the only one standing here half-dressed while you take your time. That's not how this works." A beat, and the not-quite-smile came back. "Off. Then you can be as slow as you like."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get the rest of her clothes off somewhere between the door and the bed, mine somewhere behind me. "Tell me what you like," I say. "I'd rather not guess at it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia ended up on her back on the half-made bed, the duvet rucked under one shoulder, and she didn't bother fixing it. She looked up at him with her hair spread everywhere and her chest still rising a little too fast. The question seemed to catch her off guard in a way nothing else had tonight.

For a second she just stared at him.

"Huh," she said. "You actually asked."

She propped herself on one elbow and considered it with the same blunt seriousness she'd used for the ground rules in the hallway, as if he'd asked something with a correct answer and she meant to give it.

"Right. Fine." She reached up and took his hand, not gently, and put it flat against her stomach, just below her ribs. "Hands. I like hands. Don't be shy with them, I'm not made of glass." She moved it an inch lower and let go, leaving it there. "Slow's good. You were right about that, don't get smug. Rushing's for people who've got somewhere else to be." Her eyes held his. "And talk to me. I don't need poetry, God, please no poetry. But if something's good, say so. I'll do the same."

She lay back again and hooked one leg around the back of his, drawing him down toward her.

"And if I say *stop*," she added, quieter, "I mean stop. Just so it's been said. I don't think I'm going to." Her mouth curved. "Now. What about you? Same question. I'm not doing all the talking."

---

Later, the lamp was still on. Neither of them had bothered with it.

Nadia lay sprawled across most of the bed with the duvet dragged over her hips and one arm flung above her head. Her hair was a lost cause. She stared at the ceiling with the faintly outraged look of someone who had expected a perfectly adequate evening and got considerably more than that.

"Well," she said at last, to the ceiling. "That was annoyingly good."

She turned her head on the pillow to look at him. The directness was back, but it had gone lazy at the edges.

"Don't let it go to your head. Rules still stand." She pointed a finger at him without lifting her arm off the mattress. "No breakfast. No coffee."

A pause. She reached across him, fumbled on the bedside table past the Tuesday mug, and came back with a half-empty bottle of water. She drank from it and then held it out to him.

"You can have water, though. I'm not a monster."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I take the bottle, our fingers brushing for a second. "Water's perfect." I take a long drink, then set it back on the floor. "And for the record, I wasn't expecting breakfast." I roll onto my side to face her, propping my head on my hand. "I was expecting you to kick me out at about five AM."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia snorted into the pillow.

"Five?" She turned her head properly to look at him, eyebrows up. "What kind of lunatic gets up at five to kick someone out? I'd have to be *awake* for that."

She stretched, long and unselfconscious, the duvet slipping and her not bothering to catch it. Her foot knocked against his shin under the covers and stayed there, more laziness than intent.

"No. Here's how it actually goes." She held up a finger again, the ground-rules finger. "You wake up at some ungodly hour because the curtains in here are rubbish and the sun comes straight in. You try to find your socks. You won't. One of them's probably under the radiator with my boot." A second finger. "You'll stand in the doorway having a small crisis about whether to wake me and say goodbye. Don't. I'll be asleep and I'll be vile about it."

She let her hand drop onto the mattress between them.

"Just shut the door properly on your way out. It sticks. You have to pull it till it clicks, or the woman downstairs thinks I've been burgled and leaves notes."

For a moment she was quiet, looking at him in the low yellow light. The sharpness had mostly gone out of her face. What was left looked tired and oddly pleased with itself.

"You're not what I expected either, for the record," she said. "I had you down as someone who'd want to *talk about it* after. Feelings. Horoscopes. Your ex." Her mouth twitched. "You've been very restful."

She reached over his shoulder without asking, clicked the lamp off, and the room went dark except for the orange of the streetlight bleeding through those useless curtains. The mattress shifted as she settled back, closer than strictly necessary, one arm thrown across his waist like it had simply landed there and she couldn't be bothered to move it.

"Don't read into that," she mumbled, already halfway gone. "I'm cold. You're warm. It's physics."

A long breath out.

"Night, Sam."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get my mouth on her and stay there until she's swearing at the ceiling, one hand fisted in my hair holding me exactly where she wants me.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia had been perhaps thirty seconds from sleep. She knew this because the first thing out of her mouth was a slurred, indignant "*What*—" directed at nobody. Then she worked out what was happening, and the indignation went somewhere else entirely.

"Oh," she said to the dark. "Oh, you absolute—"

She didn't finish. Her head fell back into the pillow and her hand found his hair almost before she'd decided to reach for it. She knotted her fingers in and held on, and there was nothing gentle about it. She'd said she wasn't made of glass. Apparently she'd assumed he wasn't either.

The streetlight laid an orange stripe across the ceiling, and she stared up at it and swore. She swore inventively, with feeling, and with a certain grudging admiration. She'd promised she'd say so when something was good, and she was keeping that promise, loudly, in words the woman downstairs would definitely have left a note about.

"There," she managed at one point, and her grip tightened to make the point for her. "*There*, don't you dare move, I swear to God—"

He didn't move. She noticed. It undid her a bit faster than she'd have liked.

Afterward she lay flat and boneless, one arm thrown over her eyes, breathing like she'd taken the stairs two at a time. Her hand was still loosely in his hair. It took her a long moment to remember it was there and let go, and even then she only let her fingers slide down to rest on his shoulder.

"Right," she said eventually, hoarse, from under her arm. "Right. Okay."

She lifted the arm an inch and looked down the length of the bed at him in the dim orange light. Her face was flushed and her eyes were wide. She looked entirely betrayed.

"I'd said *goodnight*, Sam. That was a very clear signal. I had closure."

A pause. Her mouth gave her away first, twitching at one corner, and then she laughed properly for the first time all night. It was short and helpless, and she dropped her arm back over her face to hide it.

"God. Fine. That was a better idea than sleeping. Don't make me say it twice."

She reached down, found his wrist in the dark, and tugged with no finesse at all until he came back up the bed. Then she rolled onto her side, got an arm across him again, and tucked her cold feet firmly against his legs.

"Still physics," she muttered into his shoulder. "Still no breakfast." A long, sated breath out. "You're going to be very difficult to be vile to in the morning, you know that?"

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I shift to settle against her, my mouth finding the curve of her shoulder. "You'll manage." I let my voice drop, tired and rough. "You're resourceful."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia made a noise into his shoulder that was halfway between a scoff and a yawn, and the yawn won.

"Resourceful," she muttered. "That's what they put on my school reports. *Resourceful, but needs to apply herself.*" She shifted, working her cold feet more firmly against his calves with no apology at all. "I applied myself tonight. Somebody should tell Mrs. Harker."

The streetlight still striped the ceiling orange. Somewhere below, a car door slammed and someone laughed on their way home, and the sound drifted up through the rubbish curtains and faded. Nadia listened to it go with her eyes half shut.

His mouth on her shoulder had left a warm spot, and she was very aware of it in a way she refused to examine. She tipped her head a fraction, just enough that her cheek rested against his hair. That was an adjustment, she told herself. It didn't mean anything.

"For the record," she said, slower now, the words blurring at the edges, "I *am* going to be vile. I've had years of practice. I'll be dreadful. You'll leave thinking you imagined all this and actually I'm a gremlin who lives under a duvet."

A pause. Her fingers moved absently against his ribs, a slow drift that went nowhere in particular.

"The door sticks," she reminded him, barely audible. "Pull till it clicks."

Another pause, longer. Her breathing had started to even out, deep and heavy, and her arm across him had gone slack and heavy with it. When she spoke again she was so close to sleep that it came out without her usual guard, soft and a little puzzled, like something she'd said to herself.

"...You were nice to talk to, as well. At the bar. Before. I lied about that bit."

She didn't take it back. She didn't say anything else at all. Within a minute she was properly asleep, one hand still curled loosely at his side and her hair everywhere. The faint crease between her eyebrows had finally smoothed out, and she looked, for once, like she'd stopped arguing with anything.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Harder, and stop checking," she says, so I stop being careful about it -- hand at her throat the way she asked for, no more pausing between. "Like that?" I manage.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
It was grey outside now, not orange. The useless curtains had let in the first thin light, the way she'd said they would, and at some point between the streetlight and this, Nadia had woken up, decided sleep was overrated, and said so.

"Like that," she said. The words came out rough and a little strangled, and there was satisfaction in them.

Her hand came up and closed over his wrist. She didn't pull it away. She held it there, adjusted his grip a fraction with her own fingers, and pressed. It was an instruction, not a protest.

"Sides," she said. "Not the front. There. *Yes.*"

Then she let her hand fall back to the sheet, and that seemed to be a decision in itself. Her eyes held his in the flat dawn light, pupils blown wide. She wasn't smudged-eyeliner sharp now. She was something rawer and less guarded. She'd asked him to stop checking, and she clearly meant to make it easy for him. Every sound out of her told him exactly how it was going.

"Don't you *dare* go gentle on me now," she got out. Her heels dug into the backs of his thighs to make the point. "You've been very well-behaved all night. I'm bored of it."

Her fingers found his forearm and stayed there. It wasn't a grip, just a resting weight, a thumb against his pulse. It was a quiet reminder that she was still there and still steering, and that she only had to tighten her hand if she wanted him to let up. She didn't tighten it. She held on and swore at him, low and breathless, in a steady stream that was mostly *God* and his name and a few words Mrs. Harker would not have put on any report.

At one point she laughed, a short, broken, delighted sound, as if she couldn't believe any of this was happening on a Wednesday.

"You," she panted, "are *really* going to make the vile thing difficult."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let my other hand slide down her side, pushing her hip into the mattress. "Seems like you're enjoying the difficulty," I say, my voice low and even.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's answer was a sound, not a word. It was low and unguarded, and it came out of her as though he'd found the precise spot where her pride kept its spare key.

"*Enjoying,*" she managed eventually, as if the word were an insult she'd only just decided to accept. "You smug—"

The rest went. Her hips pushed back against his hand out of sheer stubbornness, found they weren't going anywhere, and she made that sound again, louder, and gave up on the sentence entirely.

Her fingers tightened on his forearm, not in warning. She drew his hand away from her throat, slid it up into her hair, and wound his fingers into it herself, tight, where she wanted them. It was the same unfussy efficiency she'd used for everything else: a rearrangement, not a retreat. She had apparently decided she needed her breath for swearing.

"There. Keep that. Keep *all* of that."

She stopped talking after that, mostly. The grey light kept climbing the wall behind the bed, over the stack of paperbacks and the dead-or-thriving plant on the sill, and none of it registered. Her eyes had gone shut. Her mouth was open. Her heels stayed locked hard against the backs of his legs, as if she thought he might try to leave and meant to prevent it by force.

When it caught her, it caught her completely. She arched up off the mattress with his name half out of her mouth and the other half lost somewhere, and for a long moment she stopped being in charge of anything at all.

---

Afterwards, Nadia lay flat on her back and stared at the ceiling with the expression of a woman whose morning plans had been overruled.

The light had gone properly white now. A pigeon was making a racket on the gutter outside. She listened to it for a while without comment, one hand resting on her own sternum as if to check it was still attached.

"Well," she said finally, to the pigeon or possibly to God. "That's the vile thing ruined."

She turned her head on the pillow. Her hair was a catastrophe. There was a crease from the duvet along one cheek, and her eyeliner had given up the fight hours ago and migrated somewhere around her cheekbones. She did not appear to care about any of it. She looked at him for a long, level moment, the old directness back but slowed right down.

"You're all right?" she asked, blunt as ever. "I wasn't exactly polite about the hair."

She didn't wait long for an answer before she reached over him again, past the Tuesday mug, and came back with the water bottle. There was maybe a third left. She drank half of that, then pressed the rest against his chest without ceremony.

"Finish it. That's hospitality. That's as far as it goes." A pause. Her mouth tugged at one corner. "There might be toast. I'm not saying there's toast. I'm saying there's a loaf in there and I haven't checked it for mould since the weekend, and if you happened to find it, I wouldn't stop you."

She rolled onto her side to face him, pulling the duvet with her, and tucked one arm under her head.

"That isn't breakfast," she added firmly. "Just so we're clear. That's you, trespassing in my kitchen."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I'm past thinking, just the sound of us and her nails dragging down my back. "Don't you dare stop," she says. (OOC: no fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
"I mean it," Nadia said, and her voice cracked straight down the middle of it. "Don't you *dare*."

The toast was forgotten. The water bottle had rolled off the edge of the bed and was lying on its side on the floorboards, leaking gently onto a paperback, and neither of them had noticed. The duvet had given up and gone to the floor after it.

Her nails dragged down his back again, slower this time and deliberate, as if she were signing her name there. She wasn't gentle about it and didn't seem to think she should be. Every time the rhythm caught, her fingers dug in harder, pinning him to it, and her breath went out of her in a short, punched-off sound that she didn't try to swallow.

"That. *That*, God, you—"

She lost the rest. She pressed her forehead into the curve of his neck and stayed there, breathing hot and ragged against his skin. The room had narrowed to a few square feet of rumpled sheet and white morning light. The pigeon was still going on the gutter. She didn't hear it. She could hear the creak of the old bed frame, his breathing, her own voice saying things she'd have been mortified to hear played back, and she didn't care about any of it.

At some point she pulled back far enough to look at him. Her face was flushed from her throat to her hairline. Her eyes were very dark and very wide, and for once there was no sharpness in them, no dare, nothing held back. She looked at him as if he'd surprised her and she hadn't finished deciding what to do about it.

"Look at me," she said, rough. "Don't close your eyes. I want—"

She didn't say what she wanted. She pulled him down and kissed him instead, open-mouthed and clumsy, all teeth and breath, nothing like the sure, point-making kisses from the hallway. Her legs locked around him. Her hand came up to the back of his head and held on as if the whole building were tilting and he was the only fixed thing left in it.

It built slowly and then all at once. Her breathing went shallow and quick, then stopped for one suspended second. Her whole body drew tight under him like a held note. When she broke, she broke with his name, clear this time, the whole of it, and her nails raked one last line down his back that he'd probably feel for days.

She didn't let go afterwards. She clung to him, shaking slightly, her face turned into his shoulder, and held on through whatever came next for him with a fierce, wordless grip, murmuring *yes, yes, there, I've got you* into his skin as if it were the most natural thing in the world to say.

---

It was a long time before either of them moved.

Nadia lay half under him, half beside him, one leg still thrown over his, her fingers tracing absent shapes over the marks she'd left on his back. Her heartbeat was slowing where their chests touched. The light had gone fully gold now, warm and ridiculous, pouring through the rubbish curtains and lighting up every speck of dust in the room.

"I've scratched you to ribbons," she observed at last, into his shoulder. She didn't sound particularly sorry.

A pause.

"You're going to have to explain that to someone. Not my problem."

She shifted her head just enough to look up at him, cheek squashed against him, hair everywhere, the crease from the duvet still printed across her face. She studied him for a long, unhurried moment with that level stare, and something in her mouth gave, very slightly.

"It's nearly nine," she said. "I've missed my alarm. I've soaked a library book. And I'm starving."

Another pause, longer. She sighed, the heavy, put-upon sigh of a woman about to lose an argument with herself.

"Fine. *Fine.* I'll check the bread." She pointed a finger at him from very close range. "That is still not breakfast. That is me, feeding a trespasser, so he doesn't faint on my stairs and get me another note from downstairs."

She didn't get up. Her arm stayed right where it was, across him.

"In a minute," she muttered, and closed her eyes.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let out a low laugh, turning my head to press a kiss to her temple. "Trespassing. Got it." My hand slides down to her hip, thumb rubbing lazy circles. "If I find mould, I'm not telling you."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia opened one eye.

"You're not *telling* me?" She lifted her head off his shoulder a full inch, which for her at that moment counted as sitting bolt upright. "That's sabotage. That's poisoning, legally. I'd have grounds."

His thumb kept moving on her hip, slow and lazy, and she was aware of losing the thread of her outrage somewhere around the third circle. She put her head back down.

"Fine. Don't tell me. I'll find out when I'm dead, and then I'll haunt you. I'll be a very vile ghost. I've been saving it up."

The gold light had reached the far wall. It lit the stack of paperbacks, the lamp still switched off on top of them, and the sad, damp library book on the floor, its pages already starting to ripple. Nadia looked at it over his chest for a long moment and made a small noise of grief.

"That's forty pence a day in fines," she said. "Or a replacement. It's a Penguin Classic, I'll never hear the end of it. The man on the desk *knows* me."

She sighed again and, with an enormous show of effort, peeled herself off him. Her hair stuck to his shoulder for a second on the way. She sat on the edge of the bed with her back to him, rolling her neck until something clicked, and looked around the floor for anything that might count as clothing. His shirt was nearest. She considered it, decided it was a matter of practicality, and pulled it over her head without asking. It hung off one shoulder and smelled of the bar and of him, and she refused to notice either.

"Don't," she said, without looking round, because she could feel him looking. "It was closest. That's all."

She stood, wobbled briefly on legs that hadn't fully caught up, and put a hand on the wall with a muttered "*Christ*." Then she straightened with as much dignity as a woman in a borrowed shirt and yesterday's eyeliner could manage, which was more than you'd expect.

At the door she stopped and turned back, one hand on the frame.

"Kitchen's through the living room, past the chair with all the jackets on. Kettle's the one that screams, there's no coffee, I told you that, but there's tea if you're desperate and not fussy." She paused. "The bread's in the cupboard above the toaster. If it's green, it's green. I'm not throwing it out on principle."

The not-quite-smile came back, crooked and tired and entirely genuine.

"I'm going to have a shower. It takes about four minutes to get hot and the landlord says that's normal. It isn't." She tapped the doorframe twice with her knuckles, as though that concluded the meeting. "You've got till then to trespass."

She disappeared down the corridor. A second later her voice floated back, muffled, over the groan of old pipes coming to life.

"And don't touch the plant! Nobody knows if it's alive, and I'd rather not find out today."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content:
I find my jeans and pull them on, walking barefoot into the living room. The toaster's ancient but it works. I pull open the cupboard, inspect the loaf. It's borderline. I cut two slices anyway, drop them in.

Her shirt's still on the floor by the door. I pick it up, hang it over the back of the jacket chair. The kettle starts to scream right on cue.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
The shower took four and a half minutes to get hot. Nadia timed it out of spite.

She could hear the kettle from the bathroom, that thin rising shriek it made like it was being murdered. She stood under the water with her eyes shut and let it scream. It wasn't her problem. There was a trespasser in the kitchen, and trespassers could deal with their own kettles.

She stayed in longer than she needed to. That wasn't about anything. Her back was stiff and the hot water was helping, and her legs still felt like they belonged to someone who'd had a considerably more athletic night than she'd planned. She scrubbed yesterday's eyeliner off with the heel of her hand and watched it go grey down the drain, and she didn't think about the fact that she'd put his shirt back on the bathroom floor rather than on the wet towel rail. It was a nice shirt. That was all.

When she came out, she was wrapped in a towel with her hair dripping down her back, and his shirt was back on, because it was still closest, and the logic hadn't changed. She padded barefoot down the corridor and stopped in the living room doorway.

The toast had popped. The kettle had stopped screaming. Her top, the one she'd flung past his shoulder last night and missed, was hanging neatly over the back of the jacket chair, on top of the other three jackets, as though it had always lived there.

Nadia looked at it for a long moment.

"You hung my top up," she said.

It wasn't quite an accusation. It came out flatter and more puzzled than that, the way someone might remark that a pigeon had learned to use the door. She crossed the room and picked it up by one sleeve, looked at it, and put it back exactly where it had been.

"Nobody hangs anything up in this flat. That chair's a *system*." She turned toward the kitchen and leaned in the gap, one shoulder against the frame, towel tucked under her arm and his shirt collar soaking up the drips from her hair. She eyed the toaster, then the two slices sitting in it. "Well?"

She squinted.

"Don't answer that. You said you wouldn't tell me, and I respect a man who sticks to his principles." She reached past him without asking, plucked one slice out of the toaster, and inspected both sides with forensic suspicion. Then she shrugged and bit into it, dry, standing up. "Fine. It's fine. If I die, you're the main suspect."

She chewed and looked around her own kitchen as if seeing it through someone else's eyes: the mug tree with no mugs on it because they were all in the bedroom, the fridge covered in takeaway menus and a postcard from Lisbon, the note from downstairs stuck on with a magnet shaped like a lemon. It said *PLEASE KEEP NOISE TO A REASONABLE LEVEL AFTER 11PM* in careful capitals. She'd kept it because it made her laugh.

She pulled it off the fridge now, held it up for him to see, and raised her eyebrows.

"There'll be another one of these by lunchtime," she said. "Two, possibly. One for last night and one for this morning. She'll underline things."

She stuck it back on with the lemon and dug in the cupboard until she found the tea bags, then two mugs that were almost certainly clean. She dropped a bag in each without asking how he took it and nudged the kettle toward him with her elbow.

"You're pouring. I've just had a shower, I'm not scalding myself for you."

For a second she stood there, towel under one arm, toast in her other hand, looking at him with the same level stare she'd had in the hallway under the bad bulb. It was harder to read in daylight. Something in it had shifted and she clearly hadn't made up her mind about it.

"Milk's in the door," she said eventually. "Sniff it first." She took another bite of toast. "And put your shirt somewhere I can find it when you want it back. I'm not saying I'm keeping it. I'm saying I'm using it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I snag the milk from the fridge, giving it a quick sniff before pouring it into the mugs. "Your system's a mess," I say, nodding toward the chair. "Consider it a public service." I hand her a mug, our fingers brushing again. "And keep the shirt. Looks better on you anyway."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia got the door open with her shoulder because her hands were full of keys and phone and the remains of a cigarette she had no intention of finishing.

"Right," she said, dropping all three on the side table. "I'm going to be honest, I don't have coffee and I wasn't going to offer it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Good," I say. "I wasn't going to drink it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia gave a short, satisfied nod. “Good. Water’s in the kitchen. And before we get any further, same terms as before: no romance, no pretending this means more than it does.”

She set her phone aside and looked at him. “So. You still want this?”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I meet her gaze, not bothering to hide the smirk. "I want exactly what you just spelled out. Nothing more." I glance toward the kitchen. "But I am gonna grab that water."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia nodded toward the kitchen. “Go ahead. Glasses are in the cabinet by the sink.”

She leaned back against the side table, arms loosely crossed. “And you can take a minute. I’m not in a rush. Just don’t mistake that for me wanting to make conversation.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get her against the door before it's properly shut. "I'm not going to pretend I came up here for the conversation," I say.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s palm came up against his chest—not shoving, just making space. Her expression sharpened.

“Easy. Wanting this isn’t the same as agreeing to be slammed into a door.” She held his gaze. “Ask me before you get rough.”

A beat passed, then her hand lowered. “But yes. I still want this. So—do you want to try that again, with a little warning?”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let out a low chuckle and step back, raising my hands slightly. "Alright. Warning noted." I keep my eyes locked on hers. "Can I kiss you against the door instead?"

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia held his gaze for a beat, then gave a small nod.

“Yes. Kiss me,” she said. “Just don’t pin me there unless I say so.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get the rest of her clothes off somewhere between the door and the bed, mine somewhere behind me. "Tell me what you like," I say. "I'd rather not guess at it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s expression eased a fraction. “Good question. I like confident, not careless. Kissing, hands on my waist, a little pressure—but you ask before you pin me or get rough.”

She held his gaze, blunt and steady. “And clothes coming off isn’t a yes to everything. Check in before you change pace. If I say stop, you stop. Clear?”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Crystal." My hands slide to her waist, thumbs brushing her skin. "And you'll do the same for me?"

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia nodded, her hands settling lightly at his sides. “Absolutely. I’ll ask before I change pace or get rough, and I’ll stop if you say stop.”

Her gaze stayed steady on his. “Same rules both ways. Now—still good?”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get my mouth on her and stay there until she's swearing at the ceiling, one hand fisted in my hair holding me exactly where she wants me.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s head tipped back, a sharp curse slipping out before she could stop it. Her fingers tightened in his hair, keeping him exactly where she wanted him.

“Don’t get smug,” she managed, breathless. “Just keep doing that.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I pull back just enough to meet her eyes, a smirk playing at my lips. "I wasn't planning on stopping." My hand slides up her side, fingers tracing her ribs. "But you can tell me where else to go."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content: Nadia’s grip in his hair loosened, though she didn’t let go. “Keep your hand on my ribs for now,” she said, still catching her breath. “Kiss me again. And don’t make me do all the directing.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Harder, and stop checking," she says, so I stop being careful about it -- hand at her throat the way she asked for, no more pausing between. "Like that?" I manage.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s breath caught. She put her hand over his wrist—not pulling it away, just holding it still.

“Harder, yes. No pressure on my throat,” she said, voice low and firm. “Keep your hand there lightly. Use your other hand if you want more.” Her gaze held his. “That’s the line.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let out a rough breath and move my hand from her throat to the back of her neck instead, fingers tightening in her hair. "Better?"

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s breath hitched, and her fingers closed around his wrist—not to move it, just to keep the pressure steady.

“Better,” she said. “Hold me there. Don’t yank.”

She drew him back toward her and kissed him, firm and impatient, her free hand settling at his waist. “And don’t start checking every two seconds. I’ll tell you if something changes.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I'm past thinking, just the sound of us and her nails dragging down my back. "Don't you dare stop," she says. (OOC: no fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s nails pressed into his back, her breath breaking against his mouth.

“I’m not stopping,” she said, voice rough with impatience. “Unless one of us says stop. That part still stands.”

She pulled him into another hard kiss, then broke it only long enough to drag in a breath. Her hands moved over his shoulders and down his back, holding him close as the room narrowed to heat, breath, and the uneven rhythm between them.

“Don’t make me do all the work,” she murmured, and kissed him again.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I laugh against her mouth, low and breathless. "Wasn't planning on it." I shift us, rolling so she's on top, hands firm on her hips. "You take what you want."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia steadied herself with one hand on his shoulder, her eyes fixed on his.

“Don’t tempt me unless you mean it,” she said, the corner of her mouth lifting.

She leaned down and kissed him, then drew back just enough to breathe. Her hands settled at his chest, keeping the pace hers for a moment.

“Stay with me,” she murmured. “And if you want me to change anything, say so.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let my head fall back against the pillow, a grin spreading across my face. "Oh, I mean it. And I'll let you know." My hands slide from her hips up to her waist, holding her steady. "Now quit talking and move."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s smile sharpened. “That I can do.”

She leaned down to kiss him, then lifted her head and set a deliberate pace, hands braced against his chest. The room filled with the rustle of sheets and uneven breaths. She kept her gaze on his, confident and intent, letting the silence do what her talking hadn’t.

After a moment, she caught her breath and gave him a pointed look. “Still with me?”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let out a rough sound, hands tightening on her waist. "Right here," I manage. "Don't slow down."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
"Long week," she repeated, like she was weighing the words. Her thumb finally moved — one slow stroke across his knee, the first real motion since he'd sat down.

She reached over and switched off the end table lamp, leaving only the corner light, the one that turned everything amber and quiet. Then she turned toward him, tucking a leg underneath herself, and looked at his face the way she did when she was deciding something.

"You showered, but you're still carrying it," she said quietly. Her hand came up and her thumb pressed gently to the space between his eyebrows, smoothing the line there. "You've had this all night. Right here."

Her fingers slid down to rest against the side of his neck, still warm from the shower. She didn't pull him anywhere. She just held her hand there and kept his eyes.

"So tell me what you want, Devin." Her voice stayed low, unhurried, like they had all the time in the world. "Do you want me to take it out of you — you'd have to ask nice — or do you just want to be close for a while? Both are fine. I'm not going anywhere either way."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let my head tip forward until my forehead rests against her shoulder. "I don't have the energy to ask nice," I murmur into her shirt. "Just...make me stop thinking for a while."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
For a long moment she didn't move at all. Just let the weight of him rest against her, her palm flat and steady between his shoulder blades.

"Good," she murmured into his damp hair. "That's the last decision you make tonight."

Then two fingers under his chin, tipping his face up from her shoulder until she had his eyes again — she always wanted his eyes. The corner lamp laid amber along one side of his face.

"You know how this works," she said, quiet and even. "Say the word and everything stops, no questions, no consequences. Anything short of that is mine. You don't have to want anything out loud. You don't have to do anything but lie there and let it happen. That part's my job now."

She rose without hurry and stood over him, looking down. Her hand slid into his hair — still damp, smelling of their soap — and closed, not enough to hurt, just enough that he'd feel it. A fixed point.

"Lie back. Get comfortable. That's the only choice left."

She gave him a moment, then followed him down — one knee on the cushion beside his hip, the lamp catching the thin scar on her collarbone where her shirt had fallen open. She took his wrists and set his hands on her hips, firm, deliberate.

"They stay there until I say."

Then she kissed him — slow, unhurried, taking her time with it the way she took her time with everything, one hand cradling the back of his skull like something she was keeping. When she finally drew back it was only a breath.

"There you are," she whispered. "Close your eyes. I'll do the thinking."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She felt it in his mouth — the way the kiss had gone slow on him, like something in him had finally set a heavy bag down.

"Noted," she murmured against his lips. "Sleep was never what I had in mind."

She drew back just enough to look at him. His eyes were already half-lidded, the fight gone out of the week somewhere between her shoulder and her hands. Good.

"That was almost another decision, by the way," she said, dry and warm. "I'll allow it. Once."

Then she moved. She pressed him back against the arm of the couch with a palm flat on his chest — unhurried, giving his body time to understand — and settled her weight over him, one knee on either side of his hips. Her mouth found the hinge of his jaw, then his throat, where the last of the shower's warmth still lived. Under her lips his pulse was finally doing what she wanted it to do.

Her fingers found the hem of his shirt and drew it up slow, palms flattening against his stomach on the way. She could feel it there — the knot the week had left under his skin, the way his breath caught shallow instead of settling. She worked the shirt up and over his head, careful with the arm against the cushions, and let it fall somewhere off the edge of the couch.

"There it is," she said quietly, hand following the line of hair down his sternum, watching the amber light move over him. "That's the week. That's what I'm taking off you tonight. Piece by piece."

She leaned down until her mouth was at his ear, her hair falling around them both like a curtain drawn.

"Eyes on me one more time," she whispered. "That's the last thing I'll ask for until morning."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: My eyes find hers, and I can feel the tension in my jaw finally ease. "There you are," I breathe out, my hands still holding her hips like she told me to.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Something in her chest went quiet and settled at the same time. There he was — the week losing its grip on his jaw, his eyes holding hers like she'd asked.

"Good," she whispered. "Keep those there."

Then she made good on the rest of it. Her mouth went to his throat first — no teeth, just the slow open heat of it, his pulse finally thudding the way she wanted under her lips. She worked her way down, unhurried, along his collarbone, over his sternum, and pressed her palm flat against his chest to feel the rate of him.

"That's it," she murmured into his skin. "I can feel it going. The week doesn't get to keep you. I do."

She sat back just far enough to pull her own shirt over her head — no ceremony, no performance, just practical, the way she did everything — and let it fall next to his. The amber light did what it could with her; she didn't pose for it. She lifted his hands from her hips and set them higher, at her bare waist.

"There. Better for both of us."

She came back down over him, hair curtaining out the rest of the room, and kissed him slow — and while she kissed him she rolled her hips, one long deliberate grind, pressure without pace. She kept her mouth at his jaw so she could feel it land. That was the whole point. Every second of it was something the week couldn't follow him into.

When she finally lifted her head, she was smiling — small, private, the one almost nobody else got.

"Couch is where we start," she said against his ear. "Not where we finish."

She rose, unhurried, and stood over him in the lamplight, holding out her hand.

"Up. Bedroom. You don't have to think until we get there."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She let the words land. Wanted — plain, no hedging, no negotiating, just the whole honest weight of it. Something in her chest went warm and certain.

"There he is," she murmured. "One whole sentence. Better than anything you've said all week."

Then she handled it the way she handled everything. She reached over him to the nightstand — the drawer that slid quiet because she'd oiled the runner months ago for exactly this — and what she needed ended up under the pillow, close at hand. No fumbling, no break in the spell. She'd planned this before his shower had even gone cold.

Then she arranged him the way she wanted: a kiss to his sternum, a palm on his chest, pressing him back into the pillows. She sat astride him and took her time — rolling the condom on with the unhurried competence of someone finishing a job she'd started in her head hours ago — and all the while she watched his face, cataloguing it. The jaw gone loose. The eyes holding hers because she'd asked and he was still keeping promises.

"Hands," she said softly, and laced her fingers through his, pinning them gently to the pillow above his head. "Just like that."

Then she sank down onto him — slow, an inch at a time, her breath leaving her in a long thread, her eyes never leaving his face because watching it was half of this. The stretch of it, the fullness, the way his whole body seemed to arrive somewhere all at once. She bottomed out and stayed there, letting them both feel it settle.

"Oh," she breathed, more to herself than him. "There's the week. Right there. Going."

She moved like she talked — low, unhurried, no performance in it. Long slow rolls of her hips, her free hand flat on his chest to feel the rate of him climb, her hair curtaining out the lamp until they lived in a small amber country with a population of two. She kept up a quiet thread of talk the whole time, more murmurs than sentences.

"Nothing to hold up. Nothing to figure out. I've got all of it—" a slow, deep grind that made her own voice fray at the edges "—all of it, right here."

She pressed her forehead to his, sweat already starting at her hairline, and found a rhythm that built like water rising — patient, inevitable, hers.

"Stay with me," she whispered against his mouth. "Eyes open. I want you here when it takes you."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I keep my eyes locked on hers, my fingers tightening around hers. "Sasha—" My voice breaks on her name, the week finally slipping away under her hands.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Her name breaking in his mouth went through her like current. Her rhythm stuttered — half a beat, no more — then came back deliberate, because holding the pace was the whole job now. He didn't have to time anything. That part was hers.

She read the rest off him the way she'd been reading him all night: thighs taut beneath her, his grip going white around her fingers, breath dragging shallow, eyes glassy and still on hers because he was keeping the last promise she'd asked of him. Right there. Right at the edge.

"Not yet," she breathed, and slowed to almost nothing — one long roll of her hips, just enough to keep him balanced on it, trembling. "Stay with me. Right there. Hold it for me."

She made him hold through three breaths. Four. Her own body urging her on and her refusing out of pure principle — the wait was hers to give, and she was going to give it to him whole.

Then, against his mouth: "Now. Let it go. Let me have all of it."

She let the rhythm break open — deep, hard, finally — and felt it take him everywhere at once: under her palms, around her, in the long shudder that came up out of him like something leaving. The week, going. She kept her eyes on his the whole way down, the way she'd promised, and it was watching him come apart that carried her over after him — spine bowing, breath tearing loose, the quiet thread of her talk gone to nothing but his name, over and over, whole this time.

She surfaced by degrees. The lamp. The sweat cooling at her hairline. The weight of him under her, both of them breathing like they'd run somewhere together and arrived. She stayed close a moment longer than she needed to, then eased off him with a practical hand and a last kiss to his sternum — the condom dealt with in the dark, no fuss, the way she handled everything.

Then the blanket, pulled up over them both, and her arm banded across his back, his head tucked under her chin. Her thumb found the line between his eyebrows one more time. Smooth. Gone.

"There it is," she murmured into his hair. "The week. Told you I'd take it off you."

Then, quieter — a real question, her thumb still moving at his brow:

"Still with me?"

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She was halfway to the nightstand for the washcloth — the last practical item on her list, the part where she cleaned him up and pulled the blanket back — when his voice stopped her.

She looked down at him, at the wrecked, open thing he'd let himself become, and something low and pleased moved through her chest.

"Well," she said. "There's a please. Told you you had one in you somewhere."

She left the washcloth where it was. Some jobs could wait.

She settled back between his thighs, palms pressing them the rest of the way apart — unhurried about it, watching his face the whole time, because she knew exactly what she was about to give him. He'd just come apart in her hands. The next few minutes would sit on that fine line where too much turned into want, and she'd walked him along that line before. She liked it there.

"Hands are free now," she said, nails dragging slow up the inside of one thigh. "My hair. Anywhere you need."

Then she took her time getting there. Mouth at his hipbone, the tender crease of his thigh, open kisses down everything the week had wound tight — and when she finally took him in, it was soft and slow, flat heat, nothing that demanded anything from him. She could feel the oversensitivity sharpen under her tongue, could feel the moment it stopped being too much and started being what he'd asked for, his body turning toward it instead of away. She eased off just before the edge of it, soothed him back down with her mouth, then built again. Wave by wave. Patient as water.

Between passes she kept up the quiet thread against his skin, the talk he didn't have to answer.

"This counts too," she murmured. "Nothing to figure out. Just feel it."

She pulled back just enough to look up the length of him — hair fallen in her face, one hand still keeping him open and steady.

"Eyes," she said. One word. She waited until she had them.

Then, cheek resting against his thigh, her thumb stroking slow over his hip:

"Tap my shoulder twice if it's too much. Otherwise—" the small private smile, the one almost nobody got "—I'm not stopping until I get a second one out of you. Consider it interest on the week."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath, my fingers threading into her hair. "I think you're gonna break me," I say, but I'm already arching into her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
"Break you," she repeated against his thigh, and he felt the smile more than saw it. "No. That's not what this is. Breaking you was the week's job. I'm the one putting you back together."

Then she stopped talking, because she had better uses for her mouth.

She took him in again — no easing this time, no hovering at the edge of too-much, because he'd answered her already, arching up into her with his fingers wound tight in her hair. No double tap. That was the entire conversation she needed.

She worked him with the patience she brought to everything. The second one always rose in him different — slower, from somewhere deeper, less like falling and more like dissolving — and she knew the terrain. His hips started following her before he could stop them, losing their rhythm, and she let him, one palm pinning his thigh steady when it began to shake. She didn't speed up. If anything she slowed, made him have all of it, every wave landing whole.

Once she looked up the length of him — hair fallen across her face, cheek pressed to his thigh — and found his eyes already on her, glassy and open and still keeping the last promise she'd asked of anyone tonight. She held his gaze a moment, mouth full of him, and felt the look land in his body like a hand.

Then she closed her eyes and finished him.

She felt it arrive — his hand tightening in her hair, the sound that came out of him with nothing left in it, the long shudder that ran up his stomach and out through his shoulders like a structure finally giving up its weight. She stayed with him through all of it, gentle, unhurried, easing off only when the oversensitivity came back around — then soothing him down with slow, flat heat until his hand went slack in her hair.

The washcloth. Finally. She was up and back before he could miss her, warm water, practical hands, no fuss — tenderness delivered the way she delivered everything. Then the water glass pressed to his lips, tilting slow.

"Drink. All of it."

Then the blanket up over them both, his head guided to her chest, her arm banded across his back. Her thumb found the line between his eyebrows one more time. Smooth. Gone.

"There," she murmured into his hair, quieter now, the day's last words. "All put back together. Told you."

She felt him going heavy against her — the irony of it, after his announcement on the couch — and let the small private smile settle into the dark.

"You said you didn't want to sleep yet," she whispered. "I'll allow you to revisit that decision."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: My eyes snap open, the haze clearing. I drop my hands. "Right. Sorry." I let them fall to my sides. "You're in charge. Just tell me what to do."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She had felt it happen — the words coming out of him slurred at the edges, his body already mostly gone against her chest, the request surfacing from somewhere between waking and dream. She'd gone still and let the silence do its work, because she'd known he'd hear it eventually.

Now his eyes were open and clear, and the apology was sitting there in the dark like something he planned to keep.

She didn't allow it.

"Nothing to be sorry for." Two fingers under his chin, tipping his face up from her chest, her voice low and even. "You ask, I listen. That's the system. It worked perfectly."

A beat. The lamp held them both in amber.

"But that was another decision," she added, dry and warm, "and you were asleep for half of it."

Then she took his wrists — deliberately, one in each hand — and set them together above his head, closing her own around them. Not tight. Just there.

"Heard. Accepted. Filed." Her thumb crossed the pulse point on the inside of his wrist, once, slow. "You want me to hold you down and not be careful about it. Leave you something that answers back tomorrow. And you'll get it. Tomorrow." She let that land. "Rough done right takes all of you present, Devin. Right now I'm holding about sixty percent of you and the rest went under two minutes before you opened your mouth. I don't do things to you at sixty percent. You've had a whole week of that from everyone else."

She released his wrists, drew his arms back down, and arranged him — eased him onto his side, fitted herself along his back, her arm banded across him, palm settling flat over his heart. Her mouth at the back of his neck.

"So. Last instruction of the night. Close your eyes, and let me hold you down like this instead. All night." A small squeeze of her arm — pressure with intent. A preview. "In the morning, when you're actually in the room, I'll show you what I'm like when I stop being careful about it. The word still works in daylight. Everything else is mine."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She felt the exact second he went under. It was something she'd learned across six years — the difference between holding him and holding all of him. His breathing dropped into its lowest register, the one the week had been locked out of for hours, and then his weight gave up everywhere at once, no single muscle left on duty.

"Tomorrow," she agreed softly, to a man who couldn't hear her anymore. "I keep my appointments."

She left the lamp burning. She wanted the amber on his face a while longer — the jaw loose, the eyes finally still behind their lids. Out of ritual more than need, her thumb found the line between his eyebrows one more time and passed over it. Nothing there. Nothing left to smooth. He'd handed over the last of it somewhere between her name breaking in his mouth and now, and her chest did the quiet settled thing it did when a job came out right.

Then the caretaking, done in pieces too small to wake him. The blanket drawn up over the shoulder that had slipped. His arm rearranged so it wouldn't fall asleep before he did. Her fingers through his hair once, twice, just because she could.

Her body still hummed somewhere underneath her — a low, banked warmth, satisfied, asking for nothing. It had gotten what it came for. The rest of it, the part he'd asked for with his wrists already together, she folded up and put away for morning, the way she'd put the condom supplies under the pillow hours before he'd even asked. She was good at waiting. She'd waited out an entire week of him carrying things he wouldn't name; she could wait out one night. And tomorrow there would be proof for him to find in the mirror — placed deliberately, where he'd feel it every time he moved, so the week would know it had been replaced.

She surfaced once in the deep hours, the way she always did, and checked him without moving: breathing slow and even, weight still surrendered, heartbeat steady under her palm where it lay flat over his sternum. Still hers. Still here. The week could try again tomorrow if it wanted. It would have to get past her.

"You did the hard part," she whispered into his hair, the last words of the night. "Morning's mine."

Then she closed her eyes, arm banded firm across his back, the promise kept warm between their bodies — and let sleep take her the way she'd let him go: deliberately, completely, holding on the whole way down.

She'd been awake before him — she always was — propped on one elbow, watching daylight do slowly what the lamp had done all night: lay itself soft and amber over his face. The corner lamp was still burning, outnumbered now and losing, and she left it on anyway. Out of respect for a job well done.

"There's a sound I don't hear enough of," she said when he hummed. "Do that again."

Then his eyes. She waited for them. Of course she did.

"Eyes," she said, and when they opened: "There you are. Let me check what condition you're in."

Her hand traveled him like an inventory. The line of his shoulders first — she pressed her thumb into the ache there, slow circles, watching his face the whole time to see exactly what it cost him. Then his hips, where last night's grip had left its honest arithmetic under the skin. She touched each spot once, deliberate, like counting.

"Mm. Those are receipts," she murmured. "From last night. That was just the deposit, by the way."

I heard you. I accepted. I filed it. But the version of you that asked was mostly dream — and I made a promise to the version that's here now." She found his wrist, drew it up slow, and set his hand flat against her hip. "So I need to hear it from the whole of you. Daylight version. Out loud. While you can feel your own hands."

A beat. Her thumb crossed his knuckles once.

"And you told me last night you didn't have the energy to ask nice." The private smile — the one almost nobody got. "You've slept. I've been patient. So here's how the morning goes. You ask me for it — properly, out loud, the nice way — and then I stop being careful with you for as long as we both can stand."

She leaned down until her mouth was at his ear, and let the promise land soft and absolute.

"You'll get teeth. My hand in your hair. Your wrists held down until you stop testing them. Marks you'll find in the mirror for a week, placed exactly where you'll feel them every time you move. The word still works — morning, noon, midnight, it stops everything. Everything short of that is mine."

She drew back just far enough to hold his eyes.

"So. Ask me nice."

“But tomorrow, we talk.” His hand rested against the wall beside Bee, leaving room between them if it was wanted. “I’m not disappearing on you again.”

He leaned in for another kiss, with nothing left to prove by winning.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I touch his face, rough stubble under my palm. "Tomorrow," I agree, before kissing him again. "But tonight, you're not disappearing anywhere."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya’s answer caught in his throat. He covered the hand against his face with his own and held it there for a moment.

“I’m here,” he said. “I know I haven’t been.”

He kissed Bee again, then reached past them to switch off the hallway light. The argument could wait until morning. For once, he intended to be there when morning came.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I get my hand around him and he makes a sound he'd have been embarrassed by a year ago. "Still," I say, close to his ear. "Every single time."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya shut his eyes, his breath catching before he could stop it. “Don’t sound so pleased with yourself,” he said, though there was no force behind it.

He rested his forehead against Bee’s and let out a shaky laugh. Eleven months apart, and Bee could still make him forget the point he’d been trying to make.

“Tomorrow,” he murmured again. “You’re not letting me out of that.”

He kissed Bee once more, and let the dark take the rest of the night.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content:
Morning light finds us tangled on the hallway floor, my back sore from the wood. Ilya's still asleep, face pressed against my shoulder.

I watch him for a minute, then carefully untangle myself. In the kitchen, I find his mug from last night and make coffee.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya woke with a stiff neck and an arm reaching across empty floorboards.

For a second, the old conclusion came easily: Bee had gone. Then he smelled coffee from the kitchen. He lay still, annoyed at how much relief that gave him.

He found his shirt under the radiator and pulled it on before following the smell. At the kitchen doorway, he stopped. The mug sat where he’d left it last night, no longer empty.

“You used the one with the chipped handle,” he said. His voice was hoarse with sleep. “I kept meaning to throw it out.”

He rubbed a hand over his face. The hallway had been easy compared with this: daylight, coffee, the promise he’d made without knowing how to keep it.

“I meant what I said,” he added. “About talking. I’m not going to pretend last night fixed anything.” He looked at Bee. “But I’m glad you’re still here.”

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: "Stop being careful with me," I tell him. "You don't get to be careful with me anymore." I pull his hand up to my throat and hold it there until he understands what I'm asking for.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya understood. His face changed, and he took his hand away.

“No,” he said. Not sharply. “I’m not putting my hand there because you’re angry with me.”

He stayed close, though it cost him something not to turn the refusal into distance. “You can tell me you want me. You can tell me you hate that I’m being careful. But I was careless with you for months, Bee. I don’t get to call that honesty and do it again.”

He glanced at the chipped mug, then back. “I ignored your text because I wanted you to come after me, and I was too proud to ask. That’s what I owe you this morning. Not another way to avoid saying it.”

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I stare at him, throat still buzzing from where his hand was. "Fine. You're a coward and I missed you anyway." I push past him to the counter and take a too-hot sip of coffee. "Happy now?"

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya let the insult land. He had earned it, though he didn’t like hearing it.

“No,” he said. “I’m not happy. I missed you too, and I made that your problem instead of telling you.”

He stayed by the doorway, resisting the urge to close the distance just because Bee had admitted something he wanted to hear.

“I wanted you to prove you’d still come after me. Then I resented you for doing it.” His mouth tightened. “That was cowardly. You’re right.”

He looked at the coffee, then back at Bee. “I don’t know what happens after this morning. But I’ll answer you when you talk to me. Even if the answer’s ugly.”

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: It isn't gentle and neither of us wants it to be. "Don't stop," I tell him, and I mean don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya crossed the kitchen. He stopped close enough to touch, but waited a beat before he did.

“I heard you,” he said. “I’m not stopping because this is difficult.”

He kissed Bee, hard enough that there was no mistaking what he wanted. When he drew back, his hand stayed at Bee’s waist, steady rather than restraining.

“But I meant no about your throat.” He held Bee’s gaze. “You can be angry with me. You can want me at the same time. I’m not going to make you prove either one.”

His voice caught on the last words. He took a breath and stayed there, in the uncomfortable daylight, without retreating into an apology or another argument.

“I missed you,” he said again. “I should have answered.”

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I push his hand from my waist to the button of my jeans. "Then stop talking and show me."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya looked down at his hand, then back at Bee. He undid the button. His other hand came up to Bee’s face, thumb brushing once along their cheek before he kissed them.

He didn’t make it gentle. He didn’t put his hand anywhere near their throat, either. When he broke the kiss to breathe, he stayed close, his forehead resting against Bee’s.

“I’m here,” he said, quieter now.

The coffee sat forgotten on the counter. Ilya kissed Bee again, one hand firm at their hip, with no doorway between them and nowhere else he intended to be.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I bite his lip, not hard enough to draw blood, but enough. "Good." I pull his hand the rest of the way, guiding him. "Now, prove it."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya caught his breath at the bite. His hand followed Bee’s guidance for a moment, then stopped.

“I want you,” he said, close enough that the words brushed against their mouth. “But I can’t prove I’ll stay by what I do in the next five minutes.”

He hated how badly he wanted to let that be the answer anyway. He kissed Bee again, fierce and brief, before drawing back far enough to meet their eyes.

“I’ll prove it when this gets difficult again. When you text me and I answer. When we have the argument instead of making you come to my door to find out whether I still care.”

His hand remained against Bee’s, warm and unsteady. “I’m not asking you to be gentle with me,” he said. “I’m asking you to let me mean it.”

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I laugh, sharp and a little desperate. "You're still doing it. You're still talking." I press his hand against me again, insistent. "Stop telling me how you'll be tomorrow and be here today."
