dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The salle had emptied an hour ago and Corvo was still there, because of course he was, rewrapping a grip that did not need rewrapping.

"Three-two," he said, without looking up. "I want it on record that the third was generous."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "It's on record that you were slow," I say, and drop my bag next to his.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's hands paused on the grip, just for a moment, the tape pulled taut between his thumb and forefinger. Then he went back to wrapping, slower now, each turn laid over the last with exaggerated care.

"Slow," he repeated, as if tasting the word and finding it overripe. "I was *baiting*. There's a difference. You'd know that if your salle taught anything past the second chapter of the manual."

He tore the tape with his teeth, pressed the end flat, and finally looked up. The overhead lights had been switched to their half-setting when the cleaners left, and the long room had gone amber and quiet, the strips on the floor faded to ghost lines. His jacket was still unbuttoned at the collar, damp at the seam where the lamé had sat against his neck for four bouts. He hadn't bothered to change. He'd been telling himself it was because he wanted to rewrap the grip.

He set the foil across his knees and leaned back on his palms against the bench, studying Reyes with the same look he used across the strip. Measuring distance. Waiting for the tell.

"Four years," he said. "Four years I've been trying to get you to drop your guard in the high line, and tonight you finally do it, and I hesitate." A short breath of a laugh, more at himself than anything. "I want to know why I hesitated. It's been bothering me for an hour."

He didn't say that he already had a theory. He didn't say that the theory involved the half-second when their masks had been close enough on the corps-à-corps that he'd heard Reyes breathing, and that he had forgotten, briefly and completely, which of them was supposed to be attacking.

Instead he tipped his chin toward the empty strip, the challenge sitting easy and dangerous in his voice.

"Best of one. No masks, no scoring box. Blades down if you like, I don't care." His mouth curved. "Or sit, and tell me I was slow again. Closer this time, so I can hear you properly."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I kick his blade lightly with the side of my boot. "You hesitated because you were waiting for applause. Always are." I unzip my bag and pull out my own foil. "Blades down. You'll need the handicap."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The foil rang faintly against the bench leg where Reyes's boot had nudged it, a thin metallic complaint that hung in the empty room longer than it should have.

Corvo looked down at it. Then up, at the second foil now in Reyes's hand, and his eyebrows climbed with slow, theatrical delight.

"Blades down," he said, "announced while drawing a blade." He clicked his tongue. "Your salle really does stop at chapter two. They never got to the part about *meaning* things."

But he was already rising. He took his own foil from his knees and stood in one easy motion. For a moment he simply held it, weighing it the way he'd weigh an argument. Then, deliberately, he bent and laid it flat on the bench behind him, tape-fresh grip toward the wall.

He straightened with empty hands.

"There," he said. "One of us has to set a good example."

He walked backward toward the strip, unhurried, his heels finding the faded en garde line without his needing to look for it. Four years of habit. The amber light caught the damp at his collar and the two undone buttons, and he made no move to fix either. At the line he stopped and turned his palms outward at his sides, the posture of a man with nothing to hide who was also plainly hiding something.

"Applause," he mused. "You think I stop to hear the crowd." A low laugh. "There's no crowd, Reyes. There hasn't been for an hour. Look around."

He let the quiet make his point. The hum of the half-lights. The distant tick of the radiator. Nothing else.

"So if I hesitate tonight, you'll have to find a new theory."

He dropped into a loose stance, knees soft, weight forward, the way he'd teach a beginner to receive an attack rather than make one. It was an invitation, and they both knew what an invitation looked like on a strip. His gaze tracked the point of Reyes's foil for exactly one beat, then lifted past it, higher, and stayed there.

"Keep it, if it makes you feel brave," he said, quieter now, the needle in his voice dulled to something closer and warmer. "I'd rather see what you do when you have to come inside my distance without it."

He didn't move. He'd decided, somewhere between the bench and the line, that this time he wasn't going to be the one who closed the gap.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I take the grip out of his hands and put it down, and I don't step back afterwards. "You've been slow all evening," I say.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo hadn't realized he was still holding anything until it was gone.

The roll of grip tape. He'd pocketed it after the rewrap and at some point, between the bench and the line, his fingers had found it again and closed around it the way they closed around a handle before a bout. Reyes's hands took it from him without ceremony, and he felt the brief, dry brush of knuckles against his palm, and then the soft tap of the roll being set down somewhere he didn't bother to look.

Reyes didn't step back.

Four years of distance. He knew it in his legs better than he knew his own address: the exact length of a lunge, the half-step that meant *I'm coming*, the full step that meant *I'm not*. There was no name in the manual for this. Too close to parry. Too close to do anything but stand there and be looked at.

"Slow," Corvo said, and his voice came out lower than he'd meant it to. "You keep saying that."

He didn't move his feet. He'd promised himself he wouldn't close the gap and, technically, there was no gap left to close, which was the kind of loophole he'd have argued with a referee about for twenty minutes. Instead, he let his head tip, just slightly, so that the amber light slid off his cheekbone and he could see Reyes's face properly without the mesh of a mask between them. There was a faint crease still pressed into Reyes's forehead from the bib. He had the absurd urge to smooth it with his thumb.

He didn't. Not yet.

"Here's the thing about slow," he went on, quietly, the needle almost gone now, only the shape of it left. "Fast is for when you don't know what the other person's going to do. You rush because you're afraid of the counter." His gaze dropped to Reyes's mouth, openly, without apology, and came back up. "I've been watching you for four years. I know all your counters."

A breath. His own, unsteady at the end, which annoyed him.

"So maybe I wasn't slow." One hand lifted from his side and stopped a few centimeters short of Reyes's jaw, hovering there, close enough to feel the warmth. It was the fencer's oldest trick: the feint that isn't quite a feint, held long enough that the opponent has to decide. "Maybe I was just waiting to see if you'd come inside."

His fingers stayed where they were. Waiting. For once, entirely willing to lose the touch.

"You did," he murmured. "So. Your point, Reyes. What do you want to do with it?"

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: My hand comes up, closing over his wrist. Not to move it away. Just to feel the quick beat of his pulse under my thumb. "You talk too much," I say, and finally step into the last inch of space between us.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
For once in his life, Corvo had no answer.

The last inch went, and with it every measurement he'd ever trusted. Reyes's thumb sat against the inside of his wrist, right on the pulse, and Corvo was abruptly, humiliatingly aware of how fast it was going. There was no hiding it. No feint that covered for a heartbeat like that. Four years of pretending the needling was all there was, undone by one thumb and a pulse that wouldn't lie for him.

His hovering hand finally finished its movement. Knuckles first, the lightest touch along Reyes's jaw, then the palm, fitting there as if it had been measured for it. His thumb found the crease the bib had left on Reyes's forehead and smoothed it, once, the absurd urge satisfied at last.

"I do talk too much," he admitted, barely above a breath. "Someone should do something about that."

He didn't wait to see who.

He kissed Reyes the way he'd never once fenced: without strategy. No bait, no second intention, nothing held in reserve for the counter. It was slower than he'd imagined it (and he had imagined it, more often than he would ever say out loud), a first press of mouth to mouth that was almost a question, and then, when the question was answered, something surer. Warmer. His free hand found the front of Reyes's jacket and curled into the fabric, not pulling, just holding on, as if the floor had tilted a degree and Reyes was the only fixed point on the strip.

Somewhere behind them the radiator ticked. The half-lights hummed. Neither foil made a sound.

When he finally drew back it was only far enough to breathe, his forehead coming to rest against Reyes's, eyes still half-closed. His pulse hadn't slowed at all under that thumb. If anything, it was worse.

"Well," he said, and his voice had gone rough and unguarded in a way he didn't recognize. A laugh caught somewhere in his chest, soft and a little stunned. "That one I'm not calling generous."

His fingers were still twisted in Reyes's jacket. He made no move to let go.

"Best of three?"

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: We get as far as the changing-room bench and not one step further. Kit goes on the floor, both of ours, and neither of us is being quiet about it.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The changing room was colder than the salle. Corvo registered this distantly, the way he registered the tile under his bare feet and the hard edge of the bench against the backs of his knees, as information that had stopped mattering.

His jacket was somewhere near the lockers. He had no idea where the plastron had gone. He'd fought with his own breeches' buckles like a novice while laughing into Reyes's shoulder, breathless and useless, and hadn't cared at all.

"Four years," he said, in the brief space between one kiss and the next, and then lost the rest of the sentence completely.

He'd always assumed that if this ever happened he'd be clever about it. That he'd find the rhythm the way he found it on the strip, read the tells, set the tempo. Instead he found he wanted everything at once and couldn't choose. His hands mapped what four years of watching had only guessed at: the long muscle of a fencer's back, the hard line of the lead thigh, the old scar he'd seen once at a regional and never dared ask about. He learned where Reyes was ticklish and filed it away with a wicked, private satisfaction. He learned what made Reyes's breath catch and did it again, slower, because he was nothing if not thorough.

And he was not quiet. He'd never once, in four years, let Reyes hear him lose his composure, not even after the worst defeats. Now it came out of him openly, low and unguarded against Reyes's throat, a sound that was half a laugh and half something he'd have been mortified by on any other night. He found he didn't care. The door was locked. The building was empty. Let the tiles hear it.

At some point he ended up with his back against the lockers, the metal cold and rattling, and he laughed outright at the noise, head tipped back, eyes bright.

"If the cleaners come back," he managed, "I'm telling them you attacked first."

His hands slid down to Reyes's hips and held on, pulling close, his mouth finding the corner of Reyes's jaw, the pulse beneath it. Returning the favor. It was going just as fast as his own had been. He felt a fierce, ridiculous triumph at that, as though he'd scored a touch.

"There," he murmured against the skin there, rough and warm. "Now we're even."

He drew back just far enough to look, flushed and dishevelled and utterly without his usual armor, and for a moment the old competitive gleam surfaced in his eyes, softened almost past recognizing.

"Tell me what you want," he said. "And don't you dare tell me I'm slow."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I press him harder into the lockers, feeling the rattle through my own chest. "You talk less when you're busy," I say against his mouth, my hand sliding down the front of his breeches.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The rattle went through Corvo's spine and into his teeth, and whatever he'd been about to say went with it.

He'd had a line ready. He always had a line ready. It dissolved somewhere between the cold press of metal at his back and the warmth of Reyes's hand moving lower, and what came out instead was a sharp, involuntary breath through his nose, his head knocking back against the locker door with a hollow *clang*.

"That's—" he started, and stopped, because it wasn't worth finishing. Reyes was right, damn it. Reyes had been right about exactly one thing all evening, and it was this.

His hands, which had been so thorough a minute ago, lost their method entirely. One stayed fisted at Reyes's hip, holding on. The other came up and slid into Reyes's hair, not guiding, just anchoring himself to something, fingers tightening each time the breath caught in his chest. He kissed back clumsily, open-mouthed, forgetting half the time to do anything but breathe against Reyes's lips while that hand did its work.

Four years of the strip had taught him to read an opponent's intent a quarter-second before the blade moved. He had absolutely no idea what Reyes was going to do next. He found, dizzily, that he loved it.

The sounds he'd been making earlier had at least been deliberate, a man letting himself be heard. These weren't. They were ragged and low and pulled out of him without permission, and when one came out louder than the rest he felt heat climb his throat and pressed his face into Reyes's shoulder to muffle it, laughing helplessly into the skin there.

"Don't," he breathed. "Don't you dare look pleased with yourself."

He could feel Reyes looking pleased anyway. He could *feel* it.

His hips moved on their own, chasing the touch, the locker rattling in rhythm behind him. A distant, still-functioning part of his brain noted that it sounded like a scoring box going off over and over, and he nearly laughed again, except that the next stroke took the laugh right out of him and turned it into something with Reyes's name in it, rough and unguarded, the first time he'd ever said it without a needle hidden inside.

He dragged his head up, forehead finding Reyes's again, eyes dark and a little wild. His grip in Reyes's hair tightened, drawing their mouths close enough to share breath.

"Fine," he got out, voice cracked down the middle. "You win this one. I'll concede. Formally. In writing."

A shudder went through him, and he swallowed hard, his hand sliding from Reyes's hip around to the small of the back, pulling Reyes flush against him, as close as the lockers would allow.

"Just," he whispered, "*don't stop.*"

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I get him flat on the bench and take my time about it with my mouth, which is the first thing all evening he hasn't had an answer for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The bench was narrow and hard and cold against his shoulder blades, and Corvo had perhaps half a second to think *this is undignified* before the thought was taken from him entirely.

He had an answer for everything. He had built a reputation on it: the remark after the touch, the needle after the handshake, the last word in the car park. Four years of last words. He opened his mouth now out of sheer habit and nothing came out but air, and then a sound that wasn't a word in any language he'd been taught.

His heels scraped on the tile, looking for purchase they'd never find. One hand went flat against the wall behind his head. The other found Reyes's hair again, and this time he didn't trust himself to hold on, so he just rested it there, fingers trembling, feeling every movement travel up through his wrist.

*Take my time*, apparently, was a thing Reyes meant literally.

Corvo, who had spent his entire adult life dictating tempo, discovered what it was to have it dictated back to him. Slow, and then slower, as if Reyes had found the exact speed at which his composure came apart and intended to sit at it for as long as it took. He tried to breathe evenly. He tried to count, the way he counted his breath before a bout. He lost the count at four and started again and lost it at two.

"*Reyes*," he got out, and it wasn't a protest, and it wasn't a plea, and it was also both.

The overhead light in the changing room buzzed, fluorescent and unflattering, and he stared up at it without seeing it. His stomach muscles jumped under his own skin. There was sweat at his temples, at the hollow of his throat, and he felt it cool and felt himself not care. At some point his free hand abandoned the wall and came down to the edge of the bench, gripping it hard enough that the wood creaked, knuckles white, because it was that or say something he'd never be able to take back.

He said it anyway. It was mostly Reyes's name, three or four times, wrecked and quiet, and something about *four years* in the middle of it that made no grammatical sense at all.

When he managed to lift his head, finally, it was only to look down, and that was a mistake. The sight of Reyes there, unhurried and utterly in command of the one bout Corvo had never known how to fence, tore a sharp, bright laugh out of him that broke halfway through into a groan. His head fell back against the bench with a soft thud.

"This is—" he gasped at the ceiling. "Grossly unfair. I'm lodging a complaint. With the—*God*—with the federation."

His fingers tightened in Reyes's hair despite himself, a helpless, involuntary pull, then loosened at once, apologetic, thumb brushing along Reyes's scalp in a clumsy caress. His thighs were shaking. He was close, closer than he wanted to be, closer than was fair after this little time, and some last competitive ember in him flared in outrage at the idea of going down this easily.

"Wait," he breathed, which was the first honest lie he'd told all evening, because he didn't want it to stop at all. "Wait. Reyes. Come up here. I want—"

He didn't finish. Couldn't. His hand slid from Reyes's hair down to the jaw, the same line he'd touched in the salle, and cupped it there, not pulling, only asking, his eyes dark and wet at the corners and, for once in four years, completely unguarded.

"I want to see your face," he said roughly, "when you win."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I look up at him, my chin resting on his hip. "Then watch," I say, and don't look away as I finish him.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
He watched.

It was the hardest thing he had ever done on any strip, in any hall, and there was no strip and no hall, only the buzzing light and the cold bench and Reyes's eyes holding his and not letting go. He'd asked for this. He'd *asked*, like a fool, and now there was nowhere to put his gaze but there, and nowhere to hide what it was doing to him.

His breath went first. It stuttered, caught, broke into short sharp pieces he couldn't string back together. Then his hand on Reyes's jaw, fingers tensing, thumb pressing without meaning to at the corner of that mouth. His free hand gave up on the edge of the bench and flailed once and found Reyes's shoulder and gripped it hard.

"Reyes," he said. "*Reyes*, I'm—"

He didn't need to say it. Reyes already knew. Reyes had known, apparently, for some time, and was simply choosing the moment, the way Corvo had chosen a thousand moments with a blade in his hand. That was the last clear thought he had: *oh, this is what it's like from the other side.*

Then it took him, and he didn't look away.

He'd have sworn later he couldn't have kept his eyes open, but he did, somehow, wide and wet and fixed on Reyes's face as his back came off the bench and his heel skidded on the tile and a sound tore out of him that echoed off every locker in the room. It went on longer than he could bear and he bore it anyway, shaking, his fingers clenched in the fabric at Reyes's shoulder and his other hand still cradling that jaw as though he were afraid Reyes might vanish if he let go.

When it finally let him down he came down all at once, boneless, his head dropping back against the wood with a soft thud. The ceiling swam. His chest heaved. For a long moment the only things in the room were the fluorescent hum and his own ragged breathing, far too loud, and he couldn't bring himself to be embarrassed about it.

His hand hadn't left Reyes's face. He noticed that eventually, distantly, and found he didn't want to move it. His thumb moved instead, slow and unsteady, tracing the cheekbone, the edge of the jaw, the corner of the mouth, clumsy as a man learning a new grip.

"Well," he said at last, to the ceiling, in a voice that sounded like it had been dragged over gravel. It took two tries. "That's. Hm."

Another breath. He lifted his head, which took real effort, and looked down the length of himself at Reyes, still resting there with that chin on his hip, and something in his chest turned over and stayed turned.

The laugh that came out of him was small and wrecked and completely without armor.

"You watched me the whole time," he said. "You absolute *bastard*."

He let his head fall back again. His legs were still trembling faintly and he made no attempt to stop them. After a moment his hand slid from Reyes's jaw into the damp hair at the nape, curling there, gentle now, a touch that wanted nothing but to stay.

"Five-two," he murmured, eyes half-closed. "I want it on record that none of them were generous."

The radiator ticked somewhere through the wall. The bench creaked under him. And Corvo, who had never in four years let anything sit without a reply, lay there in the unflattering light and simply breathed, and let the silence be Reyes's point.

Then his fingers tightened, just slightly, a small, deliberate tug upward.

"Come here," he said, softer than he'd ever said anything. "It's my turn to be slow."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Prove the point properly," he says, "or concede," so I pin his wrists to the bench and stop letting him set the pace, which is exactly what he was asking for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
"Prove the point properly," Corvo had said, lazy and loose-limbed and still half-wrecked, the old needle sliding back into his voice like a blade into a scabbard, "or concede."

He'd meant it as bait. He was always baiting. He'd expected Reyes to take it slowly, the way everything else tonight had been taken slowly, and had been lying there composing the next line in his head.

Then his wrists were against the wood.

The bench was hard under the backs of his hands, and Reyes's grip was harder, and every line he'd been composing went out of him on a single startled breath. His arms flexed once, reflexively, testing, the way he'd test an opponent's bind to see if it would hold.

It held.

Something low in his stomach turned over at that, hot and immediate and not remotely unwelcome. He stopped testing. His fingers uncurled against the bench, palms opening upward in the same posture he'd taken at the en garde line an hour and a lifetime ago: *nothing to hide.* This time he wasn't hiding anything either.

"Oh," he said, very quietly, and his voice had dropped half an octave. "Oh, I see."

He'd spent four years setting the tempo. Every bout, every argument across the car park, every needle slipped in after a handshake. Always the one choosing when to close, when to wait, when to strike. He'd told himself it was because he was better at it. He was beginning to suspect, lying pinned on a cold bench with his pulse climbing all over again, that he'd simply been waiting for someone to take it off him.

Trust Reyes to have noticed first.

"You knew," he breathed. It wasn't quite an accusation. His eyes had gone dark and bright at once, fixed on Reyes's face above him, the flush climbing his throat again, entirely without shame now. "You knew that's what I was asking for. You *read* me."

A short, disbelieving laugh escaped him, and he let his head tip back against the wood, baring his throat, and didn't bother pretending it was an accident.

"Four years," he murmured to the ceiling, "and you kept that one in reserve."

His wrists stayed exactly where they'd been put. He didn't pull against the grip again; he didn't need to. He could feel every point of pressure, the heat of Reyes's palms, the steady weight that said *here* and *mine* and *not yet*, and he found he wanted to lie very still inside it and feel all of it at once.

He brought his gaze back down, slow, and held Reyes's eyes. The competitive gleam was there again, faint, softened almost to tenderness, but underneath it something rawer and far more honest.

"All right," Corvo said, low and rough and utterly sincere. "Your tempo. I won't fight it."

A beat. The corner of his mouth lifted.

"I might *comment* on it."

And then, before Reyes could tell him again that he talked too much, he shut up of his own accord, went pliant under that grip, and waited to be shown.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I lean down and kiss him, hard, because he’s still talking. My hands stay where they are, and I don’t let him move until I feel him go slack under me.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The kiss landed like a riposte he hadn't seen coming, hard and certain, and it took the rest of his sentence clean off the end of his tongue.

Corvo made a sound into Reyes's mouth, muffled and surprised, and for one reflexive heartbeat his whole body answered the way four years had trained it to. Shoulders tensing. Wrists flexing against the grip. Chin lifting to meet the pressure and push back, to take the kiss over and set its rhythm the way he set everything.

The grip didn't give. The kiss didn't give.

And somewhere in that heartbeat, pinned under the weight of it, Corvo understood that he wasn't going to win this exchange. That he didn't *want* to. The understanding went through him slowly, like warmth spreading out from the pulse points under Reyes's hands, and he let it.

His shoulders dropped first. Then his wrists, the tendons unlocking one by one until his hands lay open and heavy against the wood, fingers curled loosely toward the ceiling. His jaw softened. The tension ran out of his spine and into the bench, and his mouth, which had been fighting for ground, simply opened under Reyes's and took what it was given.

He went slack. All the way. It was the least guarded he had ever been in front of another person, and the strangest part was how *easy* it was once he stopped holding on.

A long, low breath left him through his nose, shaky at the end. His eyes had drifted closed. Under Reyes's thumbs his pulse was going wild again, and he didn't care that Reyes could feel it. He *wanted* Reyes to feel it. Proof, finally, of something he'd never been able to say across a strip.

When the kiss eased, he didn't chase it. He stayed exactly where he'd been left, lips parted, chest rising and falling, head tipped back against the bench, and he opened his eyes only halfway to look up.

He didn't speak. It cost him visibly. The words were right there, crowding behind his teeth. *There. Satisfied? Is that what you wanted?* He could feel them trying to get out. But he held them, lips pressed together for a moment, and something almost like pride flickered across his flushed face, as though holding his tongue were a discipline he was learning in real time, one bout at a time.

Instead he let Reyes read him. That was all. The dark, unhurried look. The throat still bared. The open palms under Reyes's hands, fingertips twitching once and then going still again, obedient, deliberately so.

His breath caught, audibly, and he let that be the only thing he said.

*Your tempo,* the look said. *I'm listening.*

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: Neither of us is quiet and neither of us cares who locks up. "Don't stop," he says, for once not arguing. (OOC: write the scene through, no fade.)

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
"Don't stop," Corvo said, and heard himself say it, and didn't take it back.

It was the simplest sentence he'd spoken all night. No second intention, no needle folded inside it. Just the thing itself, laid down on the bench between them like a blade set flat.

Reyes didn't stop.

The first slow push of Reyes's weight against him drew the air out of his lungs in one long, shaking exhale. He'd thought, lying there wrecked a few minutes ago, that he was spent, that there was nothing left in him to take apart. He'd been wrong. His body answered all over again, faster than he could have believed, heat pooling low and sharp, and he felt Reyes feel it and heard the small, satisfied sound Reyes made, and it undid him more than anything else had.

His wrists stayed pinned. He didn't test the grip again. He didn't need to know whether it would hold; he knew. What he let himself do instead was *push up into it*, arching off the wood, hips rising to meet Reyes's, and the answering press back down, heavier, steadier, pinning more than his hands, sent a groan out of him that bounced off the lockers and didn't stop echoing.

"God," he breathed. "*God*, Reyes."

Neither of them was quiet. He stopped keeping track of which sounds were his. The bench complained under them, creaking with every movement, and one of its legs had begun to knock against the tile in a rhythm that was anything but dignified. He laughed at it, breathless, and the laugh broke apart into something else halfway through, because Reyes had found an angle and was keeping it, deliberately, unhurried, as though there were all the time in the world and Corvo's composure was a lock being picked one pin at a time.

He'd spent four years reading tempo. He could read this one perfectly, and it was worse, because he could feel exactly where it was taking him and could do nothing at all to hurry it. Every time he tried, every time his hips jerked up to chase more, the weight on him settled and held him still, and he'd make a sound of pure frustrated want and Reyes would simply wait him out.

"You're," he gasped, "*doing* this on purpose."

He didn't need an answer. The next slow roll of Reyes against him was the answer, and it went through him like a current, curling his toes against the tile.

The sweat on his skin had gone cold and then hot again. His hair was stuck to his forehead. His heels had given up looking for purchase and simply hooked around the backs of Reyes's legs, drawing close, holding on, the only part of him still free to hold anything, and he used it shamelessly. Under Reyes's hands his fingers kept curling and uncurling, grasping at nothing, the tendons standing out in his forearms.

He was saying things. He could hear himself. Reyes's name, over and over, the way he'd once heard a man at a national final repeat the score under his breath as if it might change. *Four years* again, still making no sense. Something that might have been *please*, which he would deny under oath later and which, right now, he meant with every nerve in his body.

The tempo changed.

He felt it the instant before it happened, the fencer's instinct, the quarter-second tell, and his eyes flew open. Reyes had decided. The slow, patient rhythm hardened into something with intent behind it, and the bench leg rapped out a sharper beat against the floor, and Corvo's back bowed clean off the wood.

"*Yes*," he got out. "Yes, *there*, don't you dare—"

He didn't finish. He couldn't. It was building in him faster than the first time, sharper, less a wave than a lunge, and he had nothing to parry it with and no wish to. He dragged his eyes to Reyes's face above him, because he'd asked for that once tonight and he wasn't going to stop asking for it now, and held there, open and helpless and *seen*.

It broke over him with Reyes's name in his mouth.

He shook with it, hard, the whole length of him pulled taut against Reyes's weight and then shuddering apart. The sound he made rang off every surface in the room. His hands, still pinned, clenched into fists and then opened wide, and he felt Reyes's grip tighten in answer, holding him through it, and somehow that was the part that brought the sting to his eyes: not the pleasure, but being *held* through it, pinned and anchored and not allowed to fall anywhere at all.

When it let go of him he stayed arched a moment longer, trembling, and then sank, slowly, all the way down into the bench.

For a long time he only breathed. Ragged at first, then less so. The fluorescent tube buzzed. The radiator ticked through the wall. His heels were still locked behind Reyes's legs, and he found he had no intention of unhooking them.

Eventually he turned his head against the wood and looked up. His face was flushed to the collarbones, his mouth bitten red, his eyes wet at the corners and completely, disarmingly soft.

He opened his mouth. Shut it again. A slow, wondering smile spread across his face instead.

"I concede," he said hoarsely. "Properly. Formally." A breath of a laugh, barely there. "Put it in the record."

His fingers, still under Reyes's hands, turned over, just enough to lace loosely with Reyes's own, and stayed.

"Now come here," he murmured, "and let me hear what *you* sound like when you win."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I let go of his wrists and slide my hands under his back, lifting him off the bench and into my lap against the lockers. "You first," I say, my voice rough. "Tell me what it sounds like."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The world tipped. One moment there was hard wood under his spine and the next there wasn't. Reyes's hands slid beneath him and lifted, and Corvo, whose legs were still useless, simply went, a startled breath knocked out of him as he was gathered up and settled.

The lockers met Reyes's back with a rattle. Corvo landed astride Reyes's lap, knees sliding down against the cold tile either side, and had to throw a hand out against the metal door to steady himself. It clanged under his palm. He laughed, winded, and let his forehead drop against Reyes's for a moment while the room stopped moving.

*Tell me what it sounds like.*

He lifted his head slowly. There was a look on his face that anyone who'd ever faced him on a strip would have recognized: the look he wore right before an absolutely unnecessary remark.

"You've told me all night I talk too much," he said, hoarse and delighted. "And now you *ask*." He clicked his tongue, softly. "Terrible tactics, Reyes. Chapter two again."

But he answered. Of course he answered.

"It sounds like the box," he murmured, and bent to put his mouth just beneath Reyes's ear, letting every word land there, warm. "That little double tone when the light goes. You know the one. You hear it and your whole body knows before your head does." His lips moved lower, along the line of the throat. "Except it doesn't stop. It just keeps going, and you can't tell anymore whose light it is."

His hand came off the locker and found Reyes's chest, fingers spread flat over the heart, feeling for it the way Reyes had felt for his pulse an hour and a lifetime ago.

"It sounds like you saying my name," he went on, quieter, "like you've been saving it. Four years, and I never once heard you say it without an insult attached." A breath of a laugh against Reyes's skin. "I'd like to hear it without one. Consider that a formal request."

His hand began to move. Slowly, down the center of Reyes's chest, over the stomach, taking its time the way everything tonight had been taken. His own tempo, now, and he set it with deliberate, wicked patience, a man who'd just learned exactly what it was like to be on the other end of it and meant to share the lesson in full.

"And it sounds," he said, as his fingers found their mark and closed, unhurried, "like *this*."

He leaned back just enough to see Reyes's face. The flush was still high on his own cheeks, his hair a wreck, his mouth bitten red, and his eyes were dark and steady and fixed, the way Reyes's had been fixed on his.

"No," he said softly, when he thought Reyes might look away. "You made me watch. Fair's fair."

His hand kept its slow rhythm. His free one came up to cradle Reyes's jaw, the same line he'd touched first, thumb resting at the corner of the mouth.

"Now," Corvo breathed, "let me hear you."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: My head thuds back against the lockers, a breath punched out of me. "Corvo," I say, and the damn name comes out soft, no insult in sight.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The name landed somewhere under his ribs and stayed there.

Corvo went still. Not his hand, which kept its slow, stubborn rhythm, because he was many things but never careless with an advantage. The rest of him, though, stopped. His breath. His thoughts. The line he'd had ready, because of course he'd had one ready, gone like chalk off a board.

Four years. Four years of *Corvo* bitten off at the end of a sentence, flung across a car park, muttered through a mask after a touch that shouldn't have landed. He'd have recognized Reyes's voice saying it in a crowded hall with his eyes shut. He had never once heard it sound like *that*.

"Oh," he said, barely a sound at all.

He didn't laugh. He'd expected to; it was his reflex for everything that got too close. Instead something tightened hard in his throat, and he had to swallow twice before he trusted himself, and even then he didn't try to speak. He bent and pressed his mouth to the bared line of Reyes's throat, just below the jaw where the pulse was hammering, and held it there. Not a kiss so much as a thank-you he didn't have the words for.

Then, very deliberately, he changed the tempo.

Slower. Firmer. His thumb found the place that had drawn that breath out of Reyes a moment ago and returned to it, patient, relentless, a drill repeated until the body learned it. He'd been taught by the best tonight, and he'd been paying very close attention.

"Again," he murmured against Reyes's skin. It wasn't quite a request. "Say it again."

His free hand slid from Reyes's jaw into the hair at the back of the head, cradling it, keeping it from knocking against the metal a second time. The locker door was cold under his knuckles. Reyes was not. He could feel every shift of muscle beneath him, the hitch in each breath, and he read them the way he'd read a hundred opponents: the tells, the tension, the quarter-second before something gave. He'd never wanted so badly to be right about one.

He drew back just far enough to see Reyes's face, the head tipped back against the lockers, the flush, the parted mouth, and something in his own face went helplessly soft.

"You've no idea," he said roughly, "how long I've wanted to see you like this. Not beaten. Never beaten." His rhythm didn't falter. If anything, it grew surer. "Just *open*."

He leaned in until their foreheads met, the same way they had in the salle, breath mingling, eyes locked. His hand quickened by a single, careful degree, the fencer's half-step, the one that means *I'm coming*.

"Look at me," he whispered. "I'm right here. I've got you."

A pause, and then, because he was still Corvo, even now, the faintest curve at the corner of his mouth:

"And I'm keeping score."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: My hand comes up to fist in his hair, holding him there while I come. I don't look away.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The salle had emptied an hour ago and Corvo was still there, because of course he was, rewrapping a grip that did not need rewrapping.

"Three-two," he said, without looking up. "I want it on record that the third was generous."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "It's on record that you were slow," I say, and drop my bag next to his.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo glanced up at last, the strip of leather slack between his hands. His smile came slowly, as if he’d decided not to make it easy.

“Slow,” he repeated. “And yet you needed three touches to put me away.”

He set the grip down. The salle was quiet enough that the small sound seemed deliberate.

“Unless you’d rather stop keeping score.” His eyes stayed on Reyes. “For once.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I lean against the edge of the table, crossing my arms. "Oh, I'll never stop keeping score. I'm just deciding if you're worth the effort."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s smile sharpened, though the challenge in it had softened.

“Then take your time,” he said. “I’d hate to be accused of rushing a verdict.”

He set the leather aside and came around the table, stopping with a deliberate pace still between them. For once, he didn’t reach for another barb.

“I’ve spent four years trying to get under your skin,” he said. “I’m starting to wonder what happens if I stop pretending that’s all I want.”

His gaze held steady on Reyes’s. “No score. No audience. Just us—if you want.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I take the grip out of his hands and put it down, and I don't step back afterwards. "You've been slow all evening," I say.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s gaze dropped briefly to the grip, then returned to Reyes. The old retort rose easily; he let it die before it reached his mouth.

“Then I’d better stop wasting time.”

He closed the distance by a fraction, slowly enough to leave the choice where it belonged. His voice had lost its teasing edge, though the challenge remained in his eyes.

“Tell me to stop, and I will,” he said. “Otherwise, I’m going to kiss you.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I reach out and grab the front of his jacket, pulling him the rest of the way. "Don't you dare stop."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s breath caught—not with surprise, but with the effort of keeping his answer measured.

“Wouldn’t dream of it,” he murmured.

Then he kissed Reyes, all the restraint he’d been nursing finally spent. One hand settled at Reyes’s waist; the other came up to their jaw, careful even as the kiss turned hungry. The salle, the score, the years of clever little provocations—all of it fell quiet.

When he drew back, it was only far enough to speak against their mouth.

“Still think I’m slow?”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: We get as far as the changing-room bench and not one step further. Kit goes on the floor, both of ours, and neither of us is being quiet about it.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s laugh broke against Reyes’s mouth—low, breathless, entirely without its usual edge.

“Four years,” he managed, before the next kiss stole the rest of the sentence.

The bench creaked beneath him as he braced one hand against it, the other resting firmly at Reyes’s waist. His composure had gone to the floor with the kit; all that remained was the stubborn care in the way he held them, even as his own breathing turned ragged.

He pulled back just enough to look at Reyes, eyes dark and searching. “Still keeping score?” he murmured.

Then Corvo kissed them again, and made no attempt to be quiet about it.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Keeping score?" I say, breathless against his lips, as my hands slide under his jacket. "Yeah. This is me winning."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo let out a breathless laugh against Reyes’s mouth.

“Then I’ll have to live with the result,” he murmured, though his hand at their waist tightened as if he had no intention of making it easy.

He kissed them again, slower this time, the familiar urge to turn everything into a contest giving way beneath the warmth of Reyes’s hands under his jacket. When he finally drew back, his forehead rested against theirs.

“Don’t get used to winning,” he said, voice rough with amusement. “I’m still going to demand a rematch.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I get him flat on the bench and take my time about it with my mouth, which is the first thing all evening he hasn't had an answer for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s answer failed him completely.

His fingers curled around the edge of the bench, knuckles whitening as he tried—and failed—to recover the composure he’d been so fond of wielding. A rough breath escaped him. Then another. The familiar retort never came.

“Reyes,” he managed at last, their name frayed into something quieter than a challenge.

He tipped his head back against the wall, eyes briefly shut, and let out a helpless, disbelieving laugh. “You’ve been saving that for four years?”

Even that came out unsteady. Corvo swallowed, one hand still braced hard against the bench, and looked down at them with an expression stripped of every practiced barb.

“Don’t stop on my account,” he said, voice rough. “I’ve got nothing.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Nothing," I repeat against his skin, taking his hand and pressing it to the bench above his head. "I'm starting to like this new record."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s fingers flexed beneath Reyes’s hand, then went still against the bench. The helpless laugh he gave was quieter this time, scraped raw of its usual confidence.

“Enjoy it while it lasts,” he said, though the words had no bite. His gaze stayed fixed on Reyes, open and unguarded in a way it had never been across a strip. “I’m going to be insufferable about the rematch.”

He drew a breath that failed to steady him. Whatever clever answer he’d meant to make disappeared again, and his mouth curved in reluctant surrender.

“God,” he murmured. “You really are winning.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Prove the point properly," he says, "or concede," so I pin his wrists to the bench and stop letting him set the pace, which is exactly what he was asking for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s wrists stayed beneath Reyes’s hands. For once, he made no attempt to turn the hold into leverage.

His breath caught, and the last trace of his grin gave way to something more exposed. “That’s a very convincing argument,” he managed, voice rough.

He tested the pin just enough to feel its certainty, then let his hands settle again. His eyes held Reyes’s, bright with the frustration of having no clever answer—and something warmer beneath it.

“Don’t mistake this for a concession,” he said. “I’m choosing to lose.”

The words came out thin against the quiet of the changing room. Corvo swallowed, then gave up on pretending he had any interest in setting the pace.

“Go on,” he murmured. “Make your point.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: My point is the way your breath breaks when I finally let you come. That's my winning touch.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
For several seconds, Corvo had no answer—not even a bad one. His breath broke, his head fell back against the wall, and the hand pinned beneath Reyes’s grip flexed helplessly against the bench.

When he finally managed to look at them again, the smugness was gone from his face. In its place was a dazed, unwilling admiration.

“Winning touch,” he echoed, voice still rough. “I’ll grant you that one.”

He swallowed, then let out a quiet laugh. “Don’t expect me to be gracious about it tomorrow.” His gaze lingered on Reyes’s, warm and unguarded. “But tonight, you can have the record.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: Neither of us is quiet and neither of us cares who locks up. "Don't stop," he says, for once not arguing. (OOC: write the scene through, no fade.)

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s plea came out rough and unadorned. “Don’t stop.”

For once, there was no challenge tucked inside it, no cleverness meant to disguise what he wanted. His wrists had been freed; he kept one hand braced against the bench and used the other to draw Reyes close, then paused long enough to search their face.

The answer he found there eased something in him. He kissed them again, slower now, without trying to turn the moment into another contest. The bench creaked beneath them. Somewhere beyond the changing-room door, the building settled into silence.

Corvo forgot the score. He forgot the rematch he’d promised to demand. He remembered only to be careful when the heat of the moment threatened to carry him faster than he meant to go—and, eventually, to let it carry them both.

Later, he lay quiet on the narrow bench, breath finally returning to something like normal. His fingers traced a distracted line along the edge of his own discarded jacket.

“Right,” he murmured, eyes on the ceiling. “I’m revising the record.”

A pause. Then his mouth curved.

“You won. And I’m going to be unbearable about how close it was.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I shift to sit up, stretching out the crick in my back from the bench. "Unbearable is your default state, Corvo." I stand, gathering my gear from the floor. "But I look forward to hearing your excuses."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo pushed himself upright with a quiet wince, then looked at the narrow bench as if it had personally betrayed him.

“Those won’t be excuses,” he said, reaching for his shirt. “They’ll be a precise account of how the conditions favored you.”

He pulled it on, still watching Reyes with a crooked, tired smile. The familiar needling was back, but gentler now—its edge softened by the warmth in his eyes.

“And before you get smug: I’m only conceding tonight.” He gathered his jacket from the floor. “Tomorrow, I’ll expect you to defend that record.”

A beat passed. His smile tilted.

“Though perhaps we should find somewhere with better furniture for the rematch.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I toss my duffle over my shoulder and look back at him. "The bench didn't seem to bother you thirty seconds ago." I reach out and tug his collar straight. "But fine. Your place. And bring your A-game."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo glanced down at his straightened collar, then back at Reyes with a smile that was tired, crooked, and far too pleased with itself.

“The bench was adequate,” he said. “You were the distracting part.”

He gathered the last of his gear and slung his jacket over one shoulder. “My place, then. I’ll make sure the furniture is worthy of the occasion—and that I’m rested enough to defend my reputation.”

His gaze held on Reyes a beat longer than the joke required.

“Bring your A-game,” he said. “I’d hate for you to win by default.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Your reputation as a sore loser?" I walk backward toward the door, holding his gaze. "Consider it challenged." I turn and push the exit open. "Don't be late."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The salle had emptied an hour ago and Corvo was still there, because of course he was, rewrapping a grip that did not need rewrapping.

"Three-two," he said, without looking up. "I want it on record that the third was generous."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "It's on record that you were slow," I say, and drop my bag next to his.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's hands stilled on the grip. He looked up at last, one brow lifting, the old familiar edge already back in his mouth.

"Slow," he said, tasting the word. "That's a new one. Usually you just call it cheating and storm off to sulk in the showers." He set the foil aside, not quite done with it, and leaned a hip against the bench. The salle was quiet enough that he could hear the bag settle. "You staying to gloat, or did you actually want something?"

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Maybe I'm staying to see if you're going to actually finish that grip, or just stare at it until the tape unravels on its own." I unzip my bag, pulling out my water bottle. "And for the record, slow is accurate. You hesitated on the second parry. Age catching up to you?"

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's mouth tipped, not quite a smile. He took the foil back up, turned it once in his hands, and set it down again with the grip facing her, unfinished on purpose.

"Age," he said. "You counted the touch and missed the rest of it. I let that parry hang because you were already committed, and you walked straight into the riposte." He glanced at the water bottle, then at her, the needling gone thinner than usual. "Four years and you still think hesitation is the same thing as being slow."

He pushed off the bench. The salle lights hummed. He stopped a step short of her bag, close enough that she would have had to look up.

"Finish the grip yourself if it bothers you," he said, quieter. "Or tell me why you actually stayed."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I take the grip out of his hands and put it down, and I don't step back afterwards. "You've been slow all evening," I say.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's breath caught, just once, at the lack of distance. The unfinished grip lay between them on the bench and he did not look at it.

"All evening," he said. The words came out lower than he meant. He could feel the heat off her, the salle lights buzzing, four years of needling suddenly too thin to stand on. His hand lifted, stopped short of her wrist, and hung there. "Then you already know I wasn't hesitating on the parry."

He held her eyes. The corner of his mouth moved, not the old smirk.

"Say it straight," he said, quiet. "Or step back. I'm not guessing tonight."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I don't step back. "Fine. You weren't hesitating. You were waiting for me."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's fingers closed the last of the distance and settled on her wrist, light, the pulse under his thumb jumping once. The unfinished grip lay forgotten on the bench between them.

"Waiting," he said. The word came out rough. Four years of needling thinned to nothing in the quiet. He did not smile. "Every bout. Every time you walked off and I let you."

He stayed where he was, close enough that she would feel the next breath. His other hand rose, stopped just short of her jaw, and held there—an ask, not a take.

"Still not guessing," he said, quieter. "If you want this, you come the rest of the way."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: We get as far as the changing-room bench and not one step further. Kit goes on the floor, both of ours, and neither of us is being quiet about it.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's hands were already under what remained of her clothes, dragging her down onto the narrow bench with him. The wood complained. He didn't. His mouth found the hinge of her jaw, then the line of her throat, and the sound that left him was low and wrecked, nothing like four years of needling.

He got one arm around her waist and hauled her closer, hips lifting to meet her, the other hand braced so they didn't slide off the edge. Kit lay forgotten on the tile. The changing-room lights buzzed. He was not quiet, and he made no effort to be.

"Right there," he said against her skin, voice gone rough. His grip tightened at her hip. "Don't you dare go easy on me now."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I bite his shoulder, hard enough to leave a mark. "Easy? You think I'd start now?" My fingers tangle in his hair, pulling his head back so I can look at him. "Four years, Corvo. Don't you dare either."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's head tipped back under her grip, throat bare, and the bite burned in a way that made his breath break. He laughed once, short and unsteady, the sound catching against her mouth.

"Four years," he said, and it came out like a warning and a plea at once. His hand slid from her hip to the small of her back, pulling her down harder against him, the bench creaking under the shift. "You think I spent them learning how to be careful with you?"

He met her eyes, pupils blown, the old competitiveness stripped down to something rawer. His free hand found the mark she'd left and pressed into it, as if he wanted the ache to stay.

"Then don't," he said, low. "I can take it. I've been taking it." His hips rolled up into hers, deliberate, not gentle. "Show me you meant all of it."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I get him flat on the bench and take my time about it with my mouth, which is the first thing all evening he hasn't had an answer for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's head hit the bench and stayed there. The answer he might have had died somewhere behind his teeth.

His hand found the edge of the wood and locked around it, knuckles gone white. The other hovered, then settled in her hair—not guiding, not quite, just holding on, fingers flexing every time she didn't hurry. A sound broke out of him, low and unguarded, and he turned his face toward the lockers as if that might save him any of his dignity. It didn't.

"Christ," he managed, and it wasn't needling. His hips shifted once, involuntary, and he made himself still, breath coming short through his nose. Four years of having the last word, and he couldn't find one. His thumb dragged once, unsteady, along her temple.

"You're— enjoying this," he said, wrecked, almost accusing. His grip in her hair tightened and eased, tightened again. He looked down at her at last, eyes dark, mouth parted, the competitiveness burned clean out of him. "Don't stop. Don't you dare stop."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I pull back just enough to watch him come undone, my thumb brushing his lower lip. "I always enjoy winning," I say, voice rough. Then I sink back down before he can form a reply.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's answer never made it past his teeth. The moment she took him again his spine arched off the bench, a broken sound tearing out of him that the lockers threw back. His hand in her hair clenched, then loosened, then clenched again, fighting the urge to pull her closer and losing.

"Reyes—" It cracked in the middle. His other hand left the edge of the wood and found her shoulder, not pushing, just holding on as if the bench might tip. His hips jerked once, involuntary, and he forced them still with a hissed breath through his teeth. The mark on his shoulder burned. Four years of having something clever ready, and all he had left was the shape of her name and the white-knuckled effort not to finish before she decided he could.

He looked down at her, eyes gone dark and unfocused, mouth open on nothing he could say. His thumb dragged, unsteady, along the line of her jaw.

"You're going to ruin me," he managed, wrecked, almost proud of it. His grip tightened. He didn't look away. "Do it."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Prove the point properly," he says, "or concede," so I pin his wrists to the bench and stop letting him set the pace, which is exactly what he was asking for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's wrists hit the bench and stayed there. The fight went out of his arms all at once, not because he couldn't have tested the hold—because he didn't. His breath broke on a sound that had nothing left of a comeback in it.

"That's it," he said, wrecked, the words catching as she took the pace from him. His fingers curled uselessly against the wood, palms open, giving her the leverage. The bench complained under them. He didn't. His head tipped back, throat working, eyes locked on hers like conceding was the only bout he still cared about winning. "You want it— take it. I'm not— I'm not giving you an out."

His hips tried to rise into her and failed, pinned as surely as his hands. A laugh tore out of him, short and ruined, pride and need knotted so tight he couldn't tell them apart. The mark on his shoulder burned. Four years, and he had never once looked like this: flushed, open-mouthed, shaking under her and refusing to look away.

"Harder," he managed, voice gone. His wrists flexed once in her grip, not to break it—to feel it hold. "Don't concede for me. Finish it."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I lean down, my breath hot against his ear. "Concede? I didn't hear you say the words." I tighten my grip on his wrists, my movements relentless and unforgiving.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's wrists strained once against her grip and failed. The sound that left him was nothing he would have recognized—broken open, half a laugh and half a plea, cut off when she didn't let up.

"Concede," he managed, and it came out wrecked, the word catching on her name somewhere underneath it. His head turned into the heat of her breath, throat bare, the mark on his shoulder burning every time the bench shifted. He didn't look away. He wouldn't give her that, even like this. "There. You heard it. Four years and you finally got it out of me."

His fingers curled against the wood, palms open, not fighting the hold—testing that she meant to keep it. His hips tried to meet her and couldn't set anything. Pride and the rest of it knotted so tight his voice went thin.

"Don't ease off because I said it," he said, low, almost angry with how much he meant it. "You wanted the words. You have them. Finish what you started, or I'll take it back."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: Neither of us is quiet and neither of us cares who locks up. "Don't stop," he says, for once not arguing. (OOC: write the scene through, no fade.)

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's wrists stayed pinned. He stopped testing the hold and just took what she gave him, breath breaking on every thrust, the bench knocking the lockers in a rhythm neither of them tried to quiet.

"Don't stop," he said again, and this time there was nothing under it but the ask. His head tipped back, throat working, the mark on his shoulder burning every time the wood shifted. His fingers curled open against the bench, palms up, giving her all of it. Four years of the last word, and he let the next one go without a fight. "Reyes— I'm—"

It hit him before he finished. His spine arched off the wood, a sound tearing out of him that the empty salle would have heard if anyone had still been there to hear it—low, wrecked, her name split down the middle. His hips jerked up into hers once, twice, and then he couldn't set anything at all; he just shook under her grip, coming hard, pulse kicking against her hands where she held his wrists down. He didn't look away. He wouldn't, even like this, eyes gone dark and fixed on hers while it ran through him, mouth open on nothing clever.

When it eased he didn't ask her to let go. His breath came back in pieces. The grip on his wrists was the only thing keeping him on the bench, and he flexed into it once, feeling it hold, a ruined laugh catching in his chest.

"There," he managed, voice gone. His thumb dragged, unsteady, where her hand pinned him. "On record. You won." He swallowed, still not looking away, still not done with her. "Now don't you dare get up."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I finally let go of his wrists and slide my hand up to his jaw instead. "Who said I was done?" My voice is rough as I lean in to kiss him, slow and thorough. "Just getting started."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's mouth opened under hers before he had the breath for it. The kiss landed slow and he took it like that, unhurried for the first time all night, one hand coming up to her jaw in answer and the other still loose where she had pinned it, as if he hadn't quite remembered he could move. When she drew back enough for air he stayed close, forehead nearly against hers, the ruined laugh still caught somewhere in his chest.

"Getting started," he said, voice scraped raw. His thumb dragged once along her lower lip, the same place she had touched him. "Four years of running your mouth and you pick now to be thorough." He didn't smile. His hand slid from her jaw to the back of her neck, not pulling, just holding, feeling the heat of her. The bench was too narrow and his shoulder burned where she'd bitten him and he made no move to sit up. "Then don't talk about it. I'm right here. Show me what else you stayed for."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I don't talk. Instead, I shift to straddle his lap on the narrow bench, my hands framing his face. I kiss him again, deeper this time, swallowing whatever smart thing he was about to say. My fingers slide into his hair, keeping him close.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo met the kiss and lost the rest of the sentence in it. Whatever he'd been about to say went under her mouth and stayed there. His hands came up on their own—one settling at the small of her back, the other sliding into her hair to match the grip she had on him—and he pulled her down until there was no space left between them on the narrow bench.

A low sound caught in his throat, muffled against her. He kissed her back harder than the pace she'd set, then made himself ease, breath breaking when she didn't let him up for it. His hips shifted under her weight, not to take the lead back, just answering. The mark on his shoulder burned where her chest pressed it. Four years of having something waiting, and he had nothing now but the heat of her and the wood complaining under them both.

He drew back only far enough to breathe, mouth still against hers, eyes half-open and dark.

"All right," he said, rough, barely a voice. His thumb dragged along her jaw. He didn't smile. "I'm not going anywhere. Take what you stayed for."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I pull back just enough to look at him, my thumbs brushing his cheeks. My voice is quiet, not teasing for once. "Everything." Then I lean in again, kissing him slower, letting my hands slide from his face down to his chest.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The room was set up the way it always was before a scene, which Ari found steadying: everything in its place, nothing improvised.

Vex checked the last strap without hurrying. "Colour," she said. It was not a question so much as a procedure.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say. "Green all the way down."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex looked up from the strap. “Green noted.”

She checked that it lay flat, then stepped back to give Ari room. The written agreement rested on the table beside her, open to that evening’s limits.

“Safeword still stands. Yellow slows us down; red ends the scene. No explanations required.” Her voice remained even. “Before I begin, tell me whether anything on that page needs changing tonight.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I shook my head, a small smile forming. "No changes, Maitresse. Everything's exactly as I want it."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex gave a single nod and closed the agreement, leaving it within reach.

“Then the limits remained as written.”

She secured the first restraint and slipped two fingers beneath it to check the fit. Her attention stayed on Ari’s face as she adjusted the buckle a fraction looser.

“Your first task was simple,” she said. “Tell me if anything pinched. Otherwise, hold still while I finished.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex finished checking the last buckle, then took one measured step back.

“Since Tuesday,” she repeated. “And still, you held still when I told you to. Good.”

She set the strap’s loose end neatly aside. “Anticipation did not change the protocol. I would check in, and you would answer honestly—even if the answer disappointed me.” Her gaze remained steady. “Colour.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say, my voice a little breathier than before. "Honestly is part of the protocol too."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex’s expression softened by a degree, though her posture did not.

“Exactly. An honest yellow would have pleased me more than a convenient green.”

She checked the clock, then rested one hand on the back of the chair. The pause was deliberate; anticipation had its place, but it did not set the pace.

“For the next five minutes, your task was to listen and answer when I asked. Nothing else.” She glanced once at the restraints, then returned her attention to Ari. “And if that breathlessness became discomfort, you told me at once.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex noticed the change in Ari’s breathing. She did not reach for the next piece of equipment.

“Look at me,” she said, her voice quiet and precise. “You had nothing to prove by keeping your composure. You did have a responsibility to tell me the truth.”

She left the rope untouched and waited a beat. “Colour—and did you want the pace to stay where it was?”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I meet her gaze. "Green," I say, forcing a steadier breath. "I... yes, keep it exactly like this."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex held Ari’s gaze for another moment, then gave a small nod.

“Green, and the pace stayed.” She made no move toward the equipment. “That was a clear answer. Now you took one breath at a time and listened.”

She glanced at the clock, keeping the promised interval. “I had planned these five minutes, and I meant to use them. You did not need to recover your composure for me. You only needed to keep telling me the truth.”

Her hand settled on the back of the chair, still and visible. “I would ask again before anything changed.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not mistake the request for permission to hurry. She checked the clock, then moved close enough to be heard without raising her voice.

“I heard you,” she said. “And I was not going to make you work to say it twice.”

She checked the restraints once more, watching for any sign that the shaking had made them uncomfortable. “First, colour. Then tell me exactly what you wanted. If it was within tonight’s agreement, I would decide when.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath. "Still green, Maitresse." I swallow, the words sticking in my throat for a moment. "I want... I want your hands on me. Not the equipment yet."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex set the equipment aside.

“Hands, not equipment,” she said. “I heard you.”

She checked the nearest restraint, then placed one hand against Ari’s shoulder and the other over the wrist she had just checked. Her touch was firm and still. She watched Ari’s face rather than the clock.

“That was a clear request,” she said. “I could give you this without changing the pace.”

She kept her hands where they were. “Tell me if either restraint began to pull. Otherwise, you could leave the next decision to me.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex kept her hands where they were. “I heard the phrase,” she said. “It meant you wanted more. It did not mean I stopped checking.”

She let the silence hold for a moment, her gaze steady. “You had spent all evening trying to be composed for me. Now you were asking me not to let you hide behind it.” Her voice stayed quiet, but lost none of its edge. “You knew better than to think asking put you in charge of the pace.”

Her hand remained firm on Ari’s shoulder. “Colour once more. Then I would decide what you had earned.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Still green." My heart is pounding against my ribs. "I know it's your decision, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex nodded once. “Green noted.”

She kept one hand on Ari’s shoulder and moved the other to the back of the chair, leaving the equipment untouched.

“You asked for more, and then you remembered whose decision it was.” Her voice sharpened. “Good. All that effort you put into looking composed had been wasted. I had seen through it long before you said a word.”

She let the silence settle before continuing. “You would get my hands, as requested. The equipment could wait. And if anything changed, you would tell me plainly.”

Vex checked the clock. “For now, you stayed right here with me.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex heard the single word and did not ask for another. She kept her hand on Ari’s shoulder, steady pressure through her palm, and checked the clock only after she had checked the restraints.

“Green was enough,” she said. “You did not owe me a speech.”

She moved her other hand from the chair to Ari’s upper back. No equipment, no sudden change of pace. She let the contact settle before her voice took on its harder edge.

“You asked me not to soften it. So listen: you were dreadful at pretending you had yourself under control. I had watched that little performance all evening.” A pause. “And you were still doing your part. You told me what you wanted. You gave me your colour. That was what I required.”

Her hands stayed where they were. “I was going to keep them on you. If a restraint pulled, you told me. If you needed yellow or red, you used it. Otherwise, you stayed with my voice.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let out a shuddering breath at her words, my body trembling under her hands. "Green," I managed, my eyes closing.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex felt the trembling beneath her palms and kept her touch steady. She did not reach for the equipment.

“Green noted,” she said. “You could keep your eyes closed. I was still watching.”

She shifted her hand a little higher on Ari’s back, away from the restraints, and waited for the movement to settle. Her voice retained its edge.

“All that composure was a flimsy little performance. You knew it, and I knew it. You did not need to put it on for me again.” She paused. “What I required was the truth, and you had given it.”

Vex kept both hands in place as she counted a slow interval by the clock. Then she eased the pressure of one palm, making the change small enough to follow.

“That was all that changed,” she said. “My hands stayed. The equipment stayed where it was. If you needed me to slow down, you had the word.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I open my eyes, letting her see the gratitude in them. "Green, Maitresse. Thank you."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex saw the gratitude and held Ari’s gaze.

“You were welcome,” she said. “And you did not have to thank me for keeping my word.”

She let her hand travel from Ari’s upper back to the shoulder, slow enough that the change was unmistakable. Her other hand stayed still. For a few breaths, she said nothing.

“Since you asked me not to soften it: that look did not excuse your little performance earlier. You spent half the evening pretending I could not see how badly you wanted my attention.” Her mouth tightened with restrained amusement. “It was unconvincing.”

Vex checked the edge of the nearest restraint with two fingers. It still lay flat. She returned her hand to Ari’s shoulder and kept the pressure firm.

“But when I asked for the truth, you gave it. That was the part that mattered.” She glanced toward the clock. “I was keeping my hands here a while longer. No equipment. No surprises.”

She stayed close, attentive to each shift in breathing. “You could close your eyes again if you wished. I was watching.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I close my eyes again, a shaky exhale escaping me. "It wasn't... supposed to convince you," I manage, the admission softer than I'd meant it to be.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
He kissed back the way he'd been wanting to for eleven months — angry about it, thorough about it — one hand fisted in the front of Bee's jacket, hauling them both over the threshold so he could kick the door shut behind them.

He broke it first. That mattered. He needed it on the record that he broke it first.

"Eleven months," he said, not stepping back, still close enough that it counted as part of the kiss, "and you still can't let me finish a sentence."

Whatever the sentence had been, it was gone now. He didn't care. He was busy noticing that Bee still tasted exactly the same, which felt like an insult — his body never having gotten the memo.

"Shoes off," he said, and turned toward the kitchen like this was something they did, like it was a Tuesday, like he hadn't spent eleven months very pointedly not thinking about the jacket currently in his fist.

He let go of it. Eventually.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I wipe my mouth with the back of my hand, not breaking eye contact. "Your body remembers just fine, don't pretend it doesn't." I toe off my boots by the door, following him into the kitchen. "Got anything stronger than tea?"

dialogue.name: Ilya

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: "Don't pretend this is some big surprise." I push him back against the wall, my hands on his hips. "You knew I'd come back eventually."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
He let Bee hold him there exactly as long as it took to establish that he was letting them.

"'Eventually,'" he repeated. "That word's doing a lot of work. You came back when it cost you nothing. No apology, no phone call — just a knock on a door you were sure would open." His hands found Bee's wrists, not pulling them off, just noting them, the way you'd log evidence. "And you were sure. That's what's going to keep me up tonight. Not that you came. That you knew you could."

There was more — eleven months of more, filed and alphabetized — but Bee's hands were warm through denim, and his body was running its own negotiation without consulting him, and the good sentence, the one he'd been saving, dissolved on contact.

So he turned them instead. The hallway was narrow — a coat hook caught his shoulder, half a step, somebody's boot skidding on the floorboards — and then it was Bee against the wall and him standing in the space he'd just cleared, breathing like he'd run here instead of four steps.

"Bedroom's where it's always been," he said. "End of the hall, second door. I mention this for informational purposes only."

He didn't move. If they were going to do this against the hallway wall — and they were, he could see it coming the way you see weather — then Bee was going to have to be the one to close the distance. He'd broken the kiss first. He'd let go of the jacket. He was keeping a running tally, and he intended to win it.
