dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I stay there for a long moment, breathing hard against the wall. Then I push myself up, meeting his eyes. “Now you can make me that drink.”

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's flat still had the same broken buzzer, which Bee found unreasonably infuriating, as though he could have fixed it in eleven months and had chosen not to out of spite.

"You could have texted first," he said, standing in the doorway and not moving out of it.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content:
He watches me for another second, then steps aside with a sigh. "Fine. But don't start."

I brush past him into the flat, my shoulder bumping his deliberately. The place smells like coffee and stale cigarettes, just like I remember.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
He shut the door behind them and left the chain off — a courtesy or a dare, he hadn't decided which.

"You bumped me on purpose," he said, leaning back against the wood. "Eleven months and you still open with the shoulder. I could have set a watch by you."

He crossed to the window, took the crumpled pack off the sill, and shook a cigarette loose with the slow theatre of a man unwrapping sweets in church. Bee had made lists about this once. Actual lists. He lit it, held the smoke, and let the silence do some work before he spoke again.

"Go on. You've been composing since the buzzer. I can hear you from here."

In the kitchen there was still a mug with a chipped handle that Bee had defended like a cause, three years running. He thought of it suddenly, with something close to fury, and put the thought down.

"You texted once. Once, in eleven months. And now you're standing in my flat shoving into me like we still—"

He stopped. Tapped ash against the frame, harder than the gesture needed.

He hadn't offered anything to drink. The bottle Bee would have gone looking for wasn't there, hadn't been in a long while, and he watched for the moment that landed too.

"Kitchen or sofa," he said. "Pick one before I pick for you."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I kiss him like it's a continuation of the argument, because it is.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
For one whole second he didn't move — long enough that it could have been refusal, long enough that Bee would feel it as one either way.

Then his hand came up to the back of Bee's jaw and he kissed back like he was trying to win.

The cigarette burned down between the fingers of his other hand; he reached past, blind, and ground it out against the sill without breaking contact. The ember stung his knuckles and he filed that under irrelevant. Eleven months, and his body had apparently kept Bee's seat. The ease of it made him furious — the zero distance between the argument and this, as if the breakup had been a long weekend he'd misremembered.

He was the one who broke it. It cost him, and he kept the bill off his face.

"No," he said, low, close enough that the word landed more on Bee's mouth than in the room. "You don't get to skip to this part. You don't get one text in eleven months and then walk in here and kiss me like I'm the one who left."

He didn't step back. That was the coward's version of walking away, and he knew it, and stayed anyway. He could feel Bee's breath going quicker and hated how well he still knew the rhythm of it, how his own had matched it without asking permission.

"So talk," he said. "The real reason you're here. Not the shoulder, not the corridor, not — that. The reason." His thumb had moved against Bee's jaw without authorization from the rest of him. He noticed. He didn't recall it. "And if it's what I think it is, you should have led with that instead of making me stand here being reasonable, which we both know isn't my best event."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I don't pull away. My mouth still feels the ghost of his. "You think I came here because I'm lonely? Because I miss you? Fuck you

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: We don't make it past the hallway. His shirt goes over his head and mine is already somewhere on the floor behind us.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
"Fuck you" was the most honest thing Bee had said in eleven months, because it wasn't a denial. Ilya had spent three years learning which of Bee's answers were doors, and that one was a door flung open with the hinges still smoking. He had a reply loaded — something about lonely being a two-way street, something that would've won him the round — and then his own shirt was over his head and the sentence died behind his sternum.

The hallway took them the way it always had.

He got Bee back against the wall because the wall was there and his knees had opinions about waiting for the bed. His mouth found the throat, the hinge of the jaw, places he'd stopped letting himself visit at four in the morning, and his body ran the whole route without once checking the map. That was the humiliating part. Not the wanting — the fluency. Eleven months sober, eleven months of rebuilding himself one deliberate day at a time, and here came the old drug with its shirt already off.

Anger made him precise. It always had. His knuckle stung where the ember had caught it, every time his hand slid up Bee's ribs — a bright thread of the earlier argument stitched through this one, and he kept it. Evidence. He wanted it on the record that they'd come here fighting.

Somewhere below, the buzzer went. Buzzed again. Gave up. The world, checking in; they let it go to voicemail.

He pulled back just far enough to see Bee's face, which was a mistake and a half, and did it anyway.

"Still not lonely?" he said. His voice had gone somewhere neither of them had permission to follow. "Say the fuck-you again. I liked it better than the text."

"Here, or the bedroom, where I have to look at you the whole time. Choose fast. I already know what I'm picking."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: "Bedroom." My hand tangles in his hair, pulling him back to me. "I want you looking at me."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I get my hand around him and he makes a sound he'd have been embarrassed by a year ago. "Still," I say, close to his ear. "Every single time."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
The sound cost him less than it should have, which was its own indictment — embarrassment required a future self to embarrass, and he'd spent eleven months refusing to be that man. So he let it land, let it out, and answered with his hands.

He bore Bee back down the hall and into the bedroom, mouth at the jaw, one palm flat on his chest — feeling the heart run ahead of them both and taking a petty satisfaction in it. The room received them like it had been waiting. That was the unforgivable thing about his bedroom: it had. He'd slept on the sofa the first four months because the bed was a witness. When he'd finally come back to it he'd slept diagonal, colonizing the far side, and it had never once worked. The mattress kept a shape in it like a held breath, and he hated that he knew which side he was steering them toward, that his body navigated by it without being asked.

He put Bee down on the wrong side anyway — his side, the colonizer's — and caught the wrist, the one doing the damage, and set it up beside his head against the pillow. Not hard enough to bruise. Hard enough to make a point. The knuckle with the ember sting came to rest on the sheet, bright thread of the corridor argument carried all the way upstairs and entered into evidence.

"Every single time," he repeated, looking down at him, doing exactly what he'd been asked and weaponizing it. "You want credit for counting. I did eleven months of every single night without—"

He stopped. Too much true. He heard it land in the room and refused to take it back.

"I'm sober," he said instead, quieter, jaw tight. "You should know that. Nobody's relapsing here except on purpose. I want it on the record."

His thumb moved at Bee's wrist — unauthorized again, unrecalled again.

"Now the rest of it. You wanted me looking at you. Fine. I'm looking. Look back and tell me why it took eleven months and one text."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I look right back at him, my pulse hammering under his grip. "Because it took me eleven months to stop being so fucking angry I wanted to break something," I say, my voice rough. "And then I just got tired of it."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: "Stop being careful with me," I tell him. "You don't get to be careful with me anymore." I pull his hand up to my throat and hold it there until he understands what I'm asking for.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
For a long second he let the hand stay where Bee had put it, both of them motionless above the held breath of the mattress, and understood that this — not the kiss, not the corridor, not the confession about the anger — was the most honest thing that had happened all night. A knife handed over handle-first. He'd spent three years learning Bee's dialects and this one said *stop handling me like I break*, and underneath it, quieter, the sentence he could have lived without hearing: *I trust you not to.*

"Careful," he said, "is the only thing I own. You want to know what it cost me? Nothing. That's the trick of it. Eleven months of careful mornings, careful four a.m.s, careful with the phone. It's the one skill I got out of the settlement, and you walk in and want it handed over in an evening like loose change."

His hand, though. His hand had already voted. Fingers settling along the side of Bee's throat, thumb finding the pulse — hammering, a thing in flight — and for the first time all night his body and the rest of him were in complete agreement, which frightened him considerably more than insubordination ever had. He tightened his grip. Not much. Exactly enough. The knuckle with the ember sting pulled taut and sang, the corridor's bright thread carried upstairs and entered into evidence.

"You said *tired*," he murmured, and put his mouth where his thumb had been, letting the word land against skin. "Your pulse didn't get the memo."

He took the dose with his eyes open. That was the whole rule now — anything, so long as he saw it coming. He had seen this coming for eleven months. He let it arrive.

"Fine print," he said, low, against the throat. "It cuts both ways. You don't get to be careful with me either. You stopped eleven months ago — I'm only matching your terms."

Then he lifted his head, looked at him the way he'd been instructed to, and did not move another inch.

"Careful's off the table, then. So answer me. Which wore you out first — the anger, or the missing? Be precise." His thumb rested on the pulse like a gavel. "I'm entering it into evidence."

And he waited the way he'd waited in the doorway: door open, not stepping through first. One of them had to. It had never once been him.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: "The anger," I say, the words coming out raw. "The missing was always there." I shift, pressing his hand harder against my throat like I'm proving a point. "Now are we done talking?"

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: It isn't gentle and neither of us wants it to be. "Don't stop," I tell him, and I mean don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
"Don't stop" wasn't an answer, but it would hold. Evidence could wait its turn.

He let go of the throat only to put his mouth where his hand had been — a transfer of custody, not a release — and then his hands went to work with the precision anger had always bought him. The drawer gave up what it had been holding for eleven months, stocked and restocked out of some habit of provision that had outlived the person it provided for, and he hated the drawer a little for being ready.

"Tell me to stop and I stop," he said, low, one last term laid on the table. "That's the final careful thing I own. After this we're past it."

Then he pushed in — slow, because fast would have been a mercy in reverse, and neither of them had earned one — and the bed finally let its held breath out under them. He kept his eyes open the whole way through. That was the rule: anything, so long as he saw it coming. He watched the anger drain out of Bee's face and something worse arrive underneath it, watched his own eleven months of careful four a.m.s get spent in a single act of withdrawal, and did not look away from any of it.

The ember sting pulled white across his knuckle where he gripped the sheet, the corridor's bright thread run all the way to its end. Anger made him precise, and precision made it good, and the good of it made him furious — that his body still ran this route without checking the map, that the fluency had survived everything he'd done to starve it. Somewhere in the middle of it his rhythm broke, one stuttered beat, and he covered the escape of it against Bee's throat. His hand had gone back there without authorization. He'd stopped issuing recalls.

"This is the part you skipped to," he managed, wrecked and vicious. "You want credit for the anger, fine. I'm billing you for the missing."

He felt the pulse jump under his thumb when Bee went over the edge — hammering, then slowing, then hammering again — and his own arrival came a breath behind, no ceremony, no distance, the whole dose taken with his eyes open.

After, he didn't retreat. Coward's version of walking away, and he knew it. He stayed where he was, weight and sweat and the slowing of both, the room smelling like smoke and the corridor argument finally settled out of court. The mattress had its shape back. He noticed which side they'd ended up on. He declined to move.

"Still sober," he said into the dark, when he could. "Still on the record."

His thumb rested at Bee's throat, reading the slowdown like a verdict.

"Fair's fair, though. You answered mine." He lifted his head, and there it was — the door open, not stepping through first. It had never once been him. "Ask me which one wore me out. The anger or the missing." A beat. "And you're not leaving tonight. That's not a question. That's the terms."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I laugh, ragged, but it’s not a happy sound. “You’re a terrible accountant.” My hand finds the back of his head, fingers threading through his hair. “Fine. Which one, Ilya? Don’t make me guess.”

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: "The missing," he says, low, into the space between us. "Eleven months and the anger ran out of things to burn. The missing just sat there waiting for you to come back." He lifts his head finally, and his face is stripped bare. "Now you're here. Fix it."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I lift my chin, meet his stripped-bare look with one of my own. “I can’t fix it. I can only be here.” My thumb brushes his cheekbone, a touch that feels too soft for this wreckage. “But I *am* here.”

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The room was set up the way it always was before a scene, which Ari found steadying: everything in its place, nothing improvised.

Vex checked the last strap without hurrying. "Colour," she said. It was not a question so much as a procedure.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say. "Green all the way down."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex held Ari’s gaze for a beat, then gave a precise nod. “Good. The safeword and limits stood as written. If your colour changed, you said so; I stopped.”

She checked each cuff once more, testing the fit with practiced care before settling the first restraint into place. Her voice remained even. “You’ll answer clearly when I check in. No guessing what I want to hear.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Always," I say, the weight of the first cuff already grounding me. I lean into the touch as you adjust it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex registered the shift of weight and paused, giving the cuff a final careful check: snug, secure, with room for circulation. She watched Ari’s face as she tested the restraint, then moved to the next strap without rushing.

“Still green?” she asked, her voice level. “Answer clearly.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex let the silence hold for a moment. “Anticipation isn’t an answer,” she said, calm and exact. Her hands stayed clear of the straps. “Still green?”

She watched Ari’s face, waiting for the check-in before she went any further.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: *I nod, a little chastened.* "Green."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex gave one precise nod. “Good. I heard you.”

She resumed only after the answer, making one last measured check of the restraints before stepping back to assess the setup as a whole. Her attention stayed on Ari, watchful and composed.

“Then we proceed by the agreement,” she said. “You answer every check-in honestly. If your colour changes, you tell me. Nothing is worth guessing.” A brief pause, then her voice softened by a fraction. “Ready for the next step?”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex studied Ari for a moment, attentive rather than amused. “Composure wasn’t a requirement,” she said. “But anticipation doesn’t replace an answer.”

She checked the rope once more, confirming that nothing had shifted or pinched, then met Ari’s gaze. “Colour—and are you ready for the next step?” Her hands stayed still as she waited.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: My breathing's already gone shallow. "Still green. Ready." I tilt my head back against the restraints.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex accepted the answer with a small nod. “Good. Then we began slowly.”

She selected the agreed paddle and let Ari see it before bringing it into the scene. “One light test. Then I check in.” Her gaze stayed attentive as she positioned herself beside Ari, careful to keep the first strike to a safe, fleshy area.

The tap landed measured and restrained. Vex lowered the paddle at once. “Colour?” she asked, watching Ari closely.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex set the paddle aside and let the scene go still. She watched the tremor in Ari’s body, then checked the restraints with practiced care, looking for any sign of strain.

“Colour,” she said, calm and immediate. “Then tell me exactly what you were asking for. I won’t guess.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: *I take a shaky breath, focusing on the question.* "Green. I was asking for a harsher stroke."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex kept the paddle lowered. “I heard you. ‘Harsher’ is not precise enough for me to act on.”

She checked Ari’s expression and the restraints, then met Ari’s gaze. “Name the level you wanted, within what we agreed. I’ll give you one measured stroke, then check in again. You can change your mind before I begin.” Her voice stayed calm and exact. “What level?”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex held Ari’s gaze, then gave a precise nod. “I heard the agreed phrase. I’ll raise the intensity within the written limits. One stroke, then I check in. Nothing you said overrides a limit or the safeword.”

She lifted the paddle, giving Ari a brief moment before delivering one firmer, measured stroke to the agreed safe area. Then she lowered it at once.

“Look at you,” she said, voice cool and exact. “Shaking, and still making me ask you to say what you want. You don’t get to hide behind that composure now.”

Her attention stayed on Ari’s face. “Colour?”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I flinch at the strike and my breath catches. The sharpness of it is exactly what I needed. "Still green. Please, Maitresse, again."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex held Ari’s gaze for a beat, checking that the answer matched the request. “Heard. One more at the same level, then I check in.”

She waited a moment, leaving room for Ari to change their mind, then delivered another measured stroke within the agreed limits. The paddle lowered immediately afterward.

“Still asking so plainly,” she said, cool and controlled. “Good. You can ask; I decide what’s safe to give.”

Her attention returned fully to Ari. “Colour?”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex set the paddle down.

“Green was good,” she said, steady and composed. “But I promised one stroke, then a check. I won’t turn your answer into permission for more.”

She watched Ari closely and let the room settle. Then she checked the rope and cuffs, careful not to tug at either, before returning her attention to Ari’s face.

“Do you want another at that level, or did you want a pause?” Her voice stayed cool, but the question was unhurried. “You can answer with the agreed words. If words aren’t there, use the signal we settled on. I’ll wait.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I force myself to take a deep, slow breath, and hold up the agreed two fingers for "same level, please." My hand's shaking.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:

She gave Ari a moment to change their mind, then delivered one measured stroke to the agreed area. The paddle came down at once.

“Good,” she said, cool and deliberate. “You asked clearly. You held the signal steady.” She set the paddle aside and kept her attention on Ari. “Colour?”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green." I let my hand drop, the tension leaving my shoulders. "Thank you, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex set the paddle well out of reach and let the room settle. “You’re welcome,” she said, measured and calm. “And you kept the signal clear. That mattered.”

She checked the rope and cuffs without tightening them, then watched Ari’s face. “We’re pausing here. Green tells me how you are; it doesn’t obligate you to continue.” Her voice softened by a fraction. “Would you like the restraints kept on while we pause, or would you like me to release them?”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I consider the question, still breathing deeply to steady myself. "Keep them on, please." I let my head rest back against the post. "I want to feel the weight a little longer."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The room was set up the way it always was before a scene, which Ari found steadying: everything in its place, nothing improvised.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say. "Green all the way down."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex nodded once. “Green noted.”

She tested the strap with two fingers, checking its fit rather than tightening it. “Yellow means I slow down. Red means I stop. Neither requires an explanation.”

She stepped back to look Ari over. “Before we begin, tell me whether anything pinches or pulls.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "No pinching or pulling, Maitresse." I shift slightly in the restraints, testing the sensation. "Everything feels secure."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex checked each restraint once more, then moved the water glass to the small table beside her.

“Secure was the aim,” she said. “Not trapped. That distinction remained yours to make at any point.”

She picked up the written protocol, glanced over the limits they had confirmed earlier, and set it down again. “We’ll begin slowly. After each round, I’ll ask for a colour. If you need me before then, say it.”

Vex paused, giving the instruction room to settle. “Ready to begin?”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex laid the protocol back on the table. “Since Tuesday,” she repeated, with the faintest hint of a smile. “Then a few more seconds won’t trouble you.”

She stayed where Ari could see her. “I asked whether you were ready to begin. I wanted an answer to that question, not proof that you’d been looking forward to it.”

Her gaze remained steady. “Ready?”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Yes, Maitresse. Ready." I take a slow breath in, letting the anticipation settle into focus.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex let the answer stand. “Good.”

She moved to Ari’s side, where she remained in view, and took up the padded implement from the table. Before using it, she pressed it lightly against the outside of Ari’s upper arm.

“We begin here,” she said. “Three measured strikes. Then a colour check.”

The first strike landed with a muted sound. Vex left a pause before the second, watching for any sign that the agreed pace needed to change. The third came no harder than the others. She lowered her hand at once.

“Colour,” she said.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: *I flinch slightly, but more from anticipation than pain.* "Green, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex inclined her head. “Green noted.”

She did not reach for the implement immediately. “I saw the flinch. You needn’t hold still for my benefit.” She gave the straps a quick visual check, then picked up the padded implement. “Two more at the same strength. No increase.”

She delivered them with a measured pause between, then set the implement down.

“Colour.”

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex

She checked the restraints without pulling at them and moved the water glass within reach of her own hand. “No more strikes until I have an answer. Take your time.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green." I let out a shaky breath. "It's green. I just... I want to ask if we can move to the next phase now. Please."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex set the implement aside and took a moment to look Ari over.

“Green noted. Thank you for asking.” Her voice softened without losing its precision. “I saw you shaking, so we pause here first. Water is available, and I’ll check the restraints again before anything changes.”

She rested a hand on the written protocol. “Tell me which part of the next phase you’re asking for. I won’t guess, and I won’t treat green as agreement to something we haven’t named.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex left the implement on the table.

“‘More’ was the phrase we agreed on,” she said. “I heard it. ‘All of it’ was not a substitute for the limits we wrote down.”

She checked the restraints, then stepped back into view. “You asked me not to soften my words. Very well. You were impatient, and you were trying to rush past the part where I made sure you could bear what you asked for. That was not your decision to make alone.”

Her expression stayed steady. “I’ll begin the verbal phase as agreed. Nothing else changes until the next colour check. Green, yellow, or red—each will be enough.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I swallow, the correction landing exactly where it needed to. "Understood, Maitresse. Thank you." I let my shoulders relax into the straps, waiting.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex waited until the silence had settled. She left the implement on the table.

“You thanked me for holding the line,” she said. “Good. Remember that the line was there because we chose it together.”

She paced a slow step, remaining in view. “You wanted more, but wanting did not excuse you from being precise. You knew better than to ask me to guess. Tonight, you would follow the protocol even when impatience made that difficult.”

She paused, studying Ari’s face without asking for a performance.

“That was the verbal phase. Nothing else changed.” Her voice returned to its procedural calm. “Colour.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex acknowledged the answer with a single nod. “Green noted. You’ve given me what I need.”

She checked the straps again, then picked up the padded implement. “Three at the same strength. No increase.”

She let the first strike land, waited, then delivered the second and third with the same measured spacing. When she finished, she put the implement down.

“You asked me not to soften my words,” she said. “So hear this clearly: impatience did not put you in charge of the pace. You knew the protocol. You could want more and still be expected to follow it.”

Vex remained in view. Her tone shifted back to the familiar check-in. “Colour.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green." I'm breathing heavier now, the straps holding me steady. "I'm sorry, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex put the implement down rather than reaching for another round.

“Green noted. And I heard the apology.” She waited a beat. “You did not need to apologize for wanting more. You did need to let me set the pace we agreed on. You did that when I asked.”

She checked the nearest strap with two fingers, then stayed where Ari could see her. “We were not going to turn an apology into another demand on you. Take one breath. Then tell me whether you wanted to continue at the same strength, or pause for water.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I take the breath, slow and deliberate. "Continue, please."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex nodded. “Continue at the same strength. Three, then I check.”

She confirmed that the straps still sat correctly. The next round followed the count and pace she had promised. When it was done, she set the implement down and remained in view.

“That was three. Nothing changed.” She reached for the water glass but did not bring it closer yet. “Colour.”

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The room was set up the way it always was before a scene, which Ari found steadying: everything in its place, nothing improvised.

Vex checked the last strap without hurrying. "Colour," she said. It was not a question so much as a procedure.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say. "Green all the way down."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex let the word settle before she answered it. Green all the way down was a phrase Ari only used on good nights, and she filed it away the way she filed everything: the steadiness of the voice, the loose set of the shoulders against the frame, the slow breath that had come just before it.

"Good," she said. "Then we'll see how far down that goes."

She stepped back to look at her work. The cuffs sat snug but not tight; she had checked two fingers' clearance at each wrist herself, as she always did, because she trusted leather less than she trusted her own hands. The room was quiet except for the low tick of the radiator and the soft sound of her heels on the boards as she circled once, unhurried, letting Ari feel her moving out of sight and back into it.

When she came around again she was holding the flogger, the suede one, heavy and thuddy, the one she always began with. She let the falls trail across Ari's back, not a strike, just the weight of them, a promise laid down where it could be felt.

"You know the rules," she said, close enough that her voice needed no volume. "You say *yellow*, I slow down. You say *red*, everything stops, and I will not be disappointed in you for a single second. Those words belong to you. Everything else," and here the suede drew slowly downward, "belongs to me."

She stepped back and found her distance. The first stroke landed square across the shoulders, broad and deliberate, more sound than sting. Then a second, in the same place. She was building a rhythm the way a drummer counts in, watching the muscles along Ari's spine for the moment they stopped bracing and started receiving.

"There," she murmured, when they finally did. "That's better. Look at you, so eager to be good for me. Pathetic, really." The word came out almost fond, exactly as it had been negotiated, the edge sheathed in something warmer. "Tell me what you are."

The flogger stilled at her side. She waited, head tilted, and missed nothing.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Yours," I breathe out, the word soft and certain against the leather of the cuff. My shoulders have gone loose under the weight of the falls, and I press my forehead into the frame, letting the rhythm sink in.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex was quiet for a moment, and in that moment the room seemed to lean toward her.

*Yours.* Not the word she had asked for, not the one the script would have handed back. Something truer. She let it land and stay, because correcting it would have been a small cruelty, and she had never been interested in small cruelties.

"Yes," she said at last, and her voice had dropped into the register she kept for moments like this. "You are."

She came forward until the heat of her was at Ari's back without quite touching, and she laid her free hand flat between the shoulder blades, over the warmth the suede had raised. She held it there, not stroking, just present, feeling the rise and fall under her palm. She was counting breaths. She was always counting something.

"You gave me a better answer than the one I asked for," she said near Ari's ear. "Clever pet. I'll allow it, once." Her thumb pressed briefly into the knot of muscle beneath the shoulder blade, firm enough to be felt and gone before it could be leaned into. "But don't think it earns you anything gentle."

Her hand withdrew. Her heels stepped back to the distance she had measured before, two strides, no more. The flogger lifted.

This time she didn't count in. The strokes came in a figure-eight, left shoulder, right shoulder, the suede rolling off her wrist in a continuous, looping rhythm that left no gap in which to brace. It was heavier now, deeper, the thud travelling inward rather than skimming the surface. She watched the colour bloom and spread evenly across the upper back, and she kept it high, well clear of the kidneys and the spine, every fall placed with the same fussy precision she gave the cuffs.

"Such a needy thing," she said over the sound of it, unhurried, as if remarking on the weather. "Strung up and grateful for it. You'd thank me for anything, wouldn't you? You'd beg for it."

She broke the rhythm without warning and let the silence ring. The only sounds were the radiator and the breathing she was listening to so closely.

When she spoke again it was softer, and it was not part of the game.

"Colour."

She waited, flogger lowered, eyes on the line of the shoulders and the angle of the head against the frame. She would not move until she had her answer.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex heard what Ari had said, and she heard, just as clearly, what Ari hadn't.

She did not lift the flogger. She set it down on the low table instead, falls laid out straight, and came around the frame to where she could see Ari's face. Whatever the game had been a moment ago, it waited now, suspended, the way the room itself seemed to wait.

"Since Tuesday," she repeated, and something in her mouth softened at the corner. "I'm glad. I want to hear all about Tuesday. Later, with tea, when you're wrapped in the blanket and complaining that I'm fussing." She reached for the nearest wrist and slid two fingers beneath the cuff, then the other, checking the skin above the leather for colour and warmth. Both were fine. She checked anyway, and she took her time about it, because this was the part she never hurried.

"But that wasn't a colour, pet."

She said it without reproach, simply as a fact laid on the table beside the flogger. Her hand came up to rest lightly at the side of Ari's jaw, not steering, just there, so she could read the answer in the face as well as hear it.

"I asked you a question, and I don't go on without the answer. Not a nice sentence instead of it, not a lovely thought about Tuesday. The word." Her thumb moved once along the jaw, slow. "Green, yellow, or red. Any of them is the right answer. There's no wrong one tonight. If something's shifted, if you're floating further than you expected, if a strap's rubbing or your hands are tingling or you just want a breath, yellow costs you nothing. And if you're still where you were a minute ago, tell me so, and I'll pick that up exactly where I left it."

She stayed where she was, close enough to catch the smallest change in breathing, far enough that Ari had room to answer. The radiator ticked. Her eyes did not leave Ari's face.

"Colour," she said again, quieter still.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let my eyes meet hers for a beat, grounding myself in the steady blue of them. "Green," I say, voice a little rough. "Still green." I turn my head just enough to brush a light kiss against her thumb.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex took the kiss against her thumb the way she took everything Ari offered: noticed, weighed, kept.

"Still green," she echoed, and she let herself look for a moment longer than the procedure required. The roughness in the voice was the good kind, the kind that came from depth rather than strain. The eyes had met hers cleanly and held. The breath under her palm, when she laid her hand briefly at the sternum on her way past, was slow and even. She believed it. She had learned, over two years, exactly when she could.

"Thank you," she said, and meant it plainly. Then her hand slipped from the jaw, and the softness went with it, folded up and set aside like a cloth over a mirror.

"And a kiss, on top of it." Her mouth curved. "Trying to sweeten me. As if that ever works."

She walked back around the frame, and when she picked up the suede she weighed it in her palm and laid it down again. Her fingers moved instead to the second flogger on the table: leather, narrower falls, lighter in the hand and sharper on the skin. She let Ari hear the difference as she drew it through her fingers, the dry whisper of it, so there would be no surprise in what came next, only anticipation.

"You've been thinking about this since Tuesday," she said, taking up her distance again. Two strides. "Four days of it. Sitting at your desk, standing in queues, doing your little errands, and all the while this is what was going on behind your eyes." The first stroke landed across the right shoulder, crisper than anything before it, a bright line laid over the deep warmth the suede had left. "Four days of wanting to be tied up and used like this."

A second stroke, left shoulder, matched to the first.

"How very dignified of you."

She settled into a slower cadence than before, deliberate, each stroke given its own space so it could be felt all the way through before the next arrived. She kept to the broad muscle of the upper back and the tops of the shoulders, the places already warmed and ready, and she watched how the skin took the leather: the pink rising sharper now, even and clean, no marks she did not intend.

"Poor thing," she went on, in the same fond, level tone. "All that waiting, and you still couldn't manage to answer a simple question the first time I asked it." Stroke. "Had to be told twice." Stroke. "Like a puppy that hasn't learned its name."

She paused between one stroke and the next, long enough to let it breathe, long enough to see the shoulders loosen again rather than lock. Then she stepped in close, the leather falls hanging against her thigh, and spoke low at the back of Ari's neck.

"But you did learn it in the end. You looked right at me and told me the truth." Her free hand traced a single line down the warmed skin, fingertips only, cool against the heat. "That's the only thing I actually need from you. Everything else is just for fun."

She stepped back. The flogger rose.

"Now. I want to hear you count the next ten. Out loud, clearly, so I can hear every one." A pause, weighted. "Lose count, and we start again from one. And I promise you, pet, I have nowhere else to be tonight."

The first of the ten fell, and she waited, head tilted, listening.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not raise the flogger for the second stroke.

She had asked for a number, and what came back instead was a sentence, and not a sentence that belonged to this room. There was no rope tonight. There had been no rope at all: leather cuffs, two fingers' clearance, checked twice. *She hasn't done anything to me yet.* Four strokes of suede and a dozen of leather said otherwise.

She set the flogger down beside the other one, falls straight, and the game went with it. She did not announce the pause. She simply let it happen, the way she let everything happen: deliberately.

When she came around the frame she came slowly, into the line of Ari's eyes before she was close enough to touch, so that nothing arrived unseen. She stopped just short and studied the face in front of her: the focus of the eyes, the set of the mouth, how far away the gaze had gone.

"Pet," she said, low and level, in the plain voice with no edge in it at all. "I'm right here. Look at me."

She laid her hand at the side of Ari's jaw again, warm and still, an anchor rather than a caress.

"I'm going to ask you a few easy things. There's no trick in them, and there's nothing to get right or wrong. I just want to hear you." She let a breath pass. "What's holding your wrists right now? And what was I just using on your back?"

Her other hand went to the nearest cuff while she waited, two fingers slipping beneath the leather, then to the hand itself, pressing gently at the fingertips to feel for warmth. She didn't hurry. Her eyes did not leave Ari's face.

"If you've drifted somewhere lovely and deep, that's all right. I'll bring you back up, or we'll sit in it together for a while. And if you're tired, or muddled, or you'd simply like to come down now, you only need to say so. You won't have disappointed me. Not one bit."

Her thumb moved once along the jaw, slow and steady, the way she had done before, so the gesture itself would feel familiar.

"Tell me where you are, darling," she said softly. "Then give me a colour."

She waited. The radiator ticked, and she stayed exactly where she was: close, patient, listening, and not going anywhere until she had both answers.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I blink, the world sharpening back into focus around her hand on my jaw. "Leather cuffs," I say, voice steadier than I expected. "And the falls were leather, after the suede." I swallow. "I'm here. I'm here with you. Colour is...still green."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex listened to every word of it: the order they came in, the swallow, the steadiness that arrived a little sooner than Ari seemed to expect. *Leather cuffs. Leather, after the suede.* Right on both counts, and in sequence. The eyes had come back and settled on hers, focused and present.

She let out a breath she had not quite admitted to holding.

"There you are," she said, and her thumb stilled against the jaw. "Thank you. That was exactly what I needed."

She stayed where she was a moment longer, reading. The fingertips under her other hand were warm. The pulse at the wrist was quick but even. There was nothing wrong that she could see, and she had looked very hard.

"I believe your green," she said. "I want you to know that. I'm not taking it away from you." A pause. "But twice tonight you've gone somewhere I couldn't follow, and that tells me something, even if you're perfectly all right now. Green is your word, pet. The pace is mine. So I'm bringing us down a level. Not stopping. Just deciding how deep we go from here." The corner of her mouth moved. "Which, if you'll recall, is rather the point of me."

She released the jaw but did not step away at once. Instead she moved around the frame at arm's length, one palm resting flat on Ari's back the whole way, so there was never a moment without contact. At the table her hand passed over the leather flogger without pausing and took up the suede again. She let Ari hear the choice: the soft, heavy settle of it.

She stood closer this time than before, one stride instead of two, near enough that her voice needed no volume at all.

"Five," she said. "Not ten. Slow ones. You count, and I'll be right here, and between each one I want to hear you breathe." Her free hand stayed where it was, low between the shoulder blades, warm and steady. "No starting over tonight. If you lose the number, you just tell me where you think you are, and we go on from there. Nobody's keeping score but me, and I'm feeling generous."

The first stroke came broad and gentle across the shoulders, more weight than sting, the kind of thud that sank inward and settled rather than sharpened. She let it land fully. She let the silence after it stretch, unhurried, her palm rising and falling with the breath beneath it.

"There," she murmured. "Such a good thing, when you're right here with me." And then, softer, not quite part of the game and not quite outside it: "That's all I wanted. You, here."

She waited, suede resting against her leg, head tilted, listening for the number.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The five had become something slower than counting. Vex had let it, because the breath beneath her palm had stayed with her through each one, and because she had been close enough to hear every ragged, honest sound. But she heard the shaking before she saw it: the faint rattle of a buckle against the frame, rhythmic, not quite in time with anything she was doing.

And she heard the asking. Out loud, unprompted, the thing Ari usually made her work for.

She lowered the suede and did not lift it again.

For a moment she simply stood with her hand spread between Ari's shoulders, feeling the tremor run through the muscle under her palm. It might have been the good kind. Adrenaline did this. Wanting did this. So did a body that had been held up by its wrists for a long while and was quietly running out of whatever it had been running on. She could not tell which from behind, and she did not guess about things like that.

"Hush," she said, not unkindly. "I heard you."

She set the flogger on the table and came around the front, into Ari's line of sight, and this time she did not stop at the jaw. She went straight to the cuffs. The left buckle, then the right, her fingers quick and practised. She kept one arm firm across Ari's chest as the second came free, so there was no moment of dropping, only the weight shifting from leather into her.

"I've got you. Arms down, slowly. Let them be heavy."

She took the forearms one at a time and chafed them briskly from wrist to elbow, pressing her thumbs into the palms, watching the fingers flex and pink. Then she drew Ari down with her, not far, just to the edge of the bench beside the frame, her own body taking up the space at Ari's back so the shaking had something solid to shake against. The blanket was within reach; it always was. She pulled it around both of them without ceremony.

"Now," she said, low at Ari's ear, her arms crossed firmly over Ari's chest, holding tight enough to be felt through the tremor. "This isn't me saying no, pet. And it isn't me being disappointed. You've been lovely tonight, every inch of it. You're shaking, and I want you somewhere I can hold all of you while I decide what happens next. That's my job. You don't get a vote on that part."

She let a few breaths go by, counting them against her own chest, waiting to feel the shaking change.

"But you asked me for something just now, without being made to." Her voice warmed, a thread of the game coming back into it, deliberate and controlled. "Out loud. Very brave. Very unlike you."

Her hand came up and turned Ari's chin, gently, until she could see the eyes.

"So say it again. Here, looking at me, with your feet on the floor and my arms around you. Tell me what you want, and tell me your colour." The corner of her mouth moved. "If it's still true down here, you'll find me very much in the mood to be generous. And if it was the float talking, then we'll drink something sweet, and you'll tell me about Tuesday, and I'll get it out of you another night. The slow way."

She waited, holding on, eyes steady on Ari's face, listening to the breath and the words both.

dialogue.content: "I want you to fuck

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The sentence broke off, and Vex let it hang in the air between them. She did not rush to finish it for Ari.

She felt the words more than heard them, the way the breath caught on the last one and went nowhere. Under her crossed arms the shaking had begun to change. It came in longer waves now, with pauses between, like a tide working out what it meant to do. She noted it and kept holding on.

"*Fuck*," she repeated, softly, tasting it. Her mouth curved against Ari's temple. "Well. That's a very good start."

She didn't loosen her grip. If anything she held a little firmer, one hand spread flat over Ari's sternum where she could feel the heart going under it, quick and hard. The blanket had slipped from one shoulder; she tugged it back without looking.

"But it's only a start, isn't it? You ran out of nerve right at the interesting part." Her voice had gone low and warm, the edge back in it but sheathed, the way she liked it best. "Two years, pet, and you still think you can hand me half a sentence and let me fill in the rest. I know exactly what you want. That's not the point. The point is that I want to hear you *say* it."

Her fingers stayed under Ari's chin, holding the gaze where she'd put it. Her eyes moved over the face the way her hands had moved over the cuffs: patient, thorough, missing nothing. She took in the flush high on the cheeks, how clear or clouded the eyes were, and whether they stayed on hers or slid away.

"So. All of it this time. Every word, right to the end, and don't mumble." Her thumb traced once along the jaw, the familiar gesture, slow. "And then the other thing. You know which other thing. You skipped it."

She let that sit a moment, not a reproach, simply a fact laid down between them the way she'd laid the floggers on the table.

"The whole sentence," she said, quieter now, the words meant only for the few inches between their faces. "Then your colour. Then I'll decide how generous I'm feeling."

Her arms stayed wrapped around Ari, solid as the frame had been, and she waited.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex went very still.

*More.* Not a plea improvised in the moment, not the float talking. It was the word they had written down together at her kitchen table, in her handwriting, on the page of the protocol headed *Verbal*. Ari had chosen it cleanly and said it to her face, with the eyes on hers and not sliding anywhere.

She let the silence run for three of Ari's breaths. She counted them against her palm. The shaking had slowed to a low, intermittent shiver, the kind that came from wanting rather than from running out.

Then the warmth went out of her face entirely. It wasn't coldness. It was a door closing on the soft room behind it.

"Look at you," she said, and there was no sheath on it now. "Shaking on my bench in a blanket I had to put on you, because you couldn't hold yourself up. And the first thing out of your mouth when I let you down is *fuck*." Her fingers tightened under Ari's chin, not hard, just enough to be undeniable. "You don't get to ask me for things, pet. You get to be grateful when I decide to give them."

Her other hand stayed exactly where it had been, flat over the sternum, reading the heart beneath it the whole time she spoke. The words were for Ari. The hand was for her.

"You're a greedy little thing. Four days of dreaming about being strung up, and when I finally do it you can barely keep count to five. And you want *more*." She let a slow, unkind smile show. "Of course you do. You'd take anything I gave you and beg for the next thing before you'd finished thanking me for the last."

She leaned in until her mouth was at Ari's ear.

"One word, and I want it in that pretty, wrecked voice. Say *green* for me, like the needy thing you are. Then you'll find out exactly what *all of it* means."

She didn't wait long for it. She didn't need to. She had been watching the mouth.

When it came, she moved. The blanket went to the floor. She turned Ari by the jaw and pressed them back along the length of the bench, her knee finding the space beside Ari's hip, her weight settling in above so there was nowhere to look but up at her. One hand pinned a wrist to the leather. She held it the way the cuffs had, firmly, with two fingers of give that she checked without seeming to.

"You asked me not to soften it," she said, low, looking down. "So I won't. You're mine to use tonight, and I'm going to take my time doing it, and you're going to lie there and *take it* and thank me when I'm finished." Her free hand slid slowly down, unhurried and deliberate, and she watched Ari's face the whole way, missing nothing. "And if you want me to stop, you know the word. It's the only thing you own in this room."

The radiator ticked. The lamp threw her shadow long across both of them.

Vex bent her head, and the rest of the night closed around them like a hand.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I arch up into her touch, a sharp, wordless sound catching in my throat. The contrast is perfect—her voice so cold, her hand so warm, and the word *green* still ringing in the air between us.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex watched the arch, and the sound, and the way Ari's eyes stayed open and on hers through both. She filed each one away. Then she let the smallest, most satisfied smile touch the corner of her mouth, and did not let it reach her voice.

"Listen to you," she said, cool as the leather under Ari's back. "One touch. That's all it took. I've barely started, and already you're making noises like that for me." Her hand stilled, deliberately, and she held it there. She wasn't withdrawing. She was waiting, and making Ari feel the waiting. "Did I say you could move?"

She let the question sit unanswered. She didn't want an answer. She wanted Ari to lie still under the weight of it.

When she moved again it was slower than before, maddeningly patient, the pace of a woman who had meant it when she said she had nowhere else to be. She kept her face above Ari's, close enough that every breath passed between them, and she talked the whole time in that low, unhurried, merciless voice. She told Ari exactly how desperate they looked. She told them how easy they were, how transparent, how she'd known since the moment they walked in tonight precisely what state they'd be in by now. Every word was one they'd written down together, and she gave none of them any cushion at all.

The hand pinning Ari's wrist never tightened past two fingers of give. Every so often her thumb brushed the inside of it, where the pulse ran, and she read it the way she read everything else.

"Look at me," she said, when Ari's eyes began to lose their edge. The words came sharp, but they were an anchor, and she meant them as one. "Here. Right here. You don't get to disappear on me this time. You're going to stay exactly where I can see you and feel every second of what I'm doing to you."

The lamp burned low. The radiator ticked. Time stretched and folded, and Vex took it at her pace, drawing it out until the sounds under her had frayed into something wordless and raw. She did not soften, not once, because she had been asked not to, and she kept her promises.

When at last it broke, she held Ari through it, one hand firm and the other flat over the hammering heart, and she said nothing cruel at all. She said only, very quietly, "*Good.*"

Then she stayed exactly where she was, her weight settled and steady, and let the silence come back into the room. She released the wrist and chafed it gently between her palms, then the other one. She reached down without looking for the blanket on the floor and drew it up over both of them.

The door she had closed on her softer self opened again, slowly.

"There you are," she murmured against Ari's hair, and her voice was warm now, entirely warm, with nothing sheathed in it anywhere. "Every word I said in that part stays in that part. You know that. Out here, you were extraordinary, and brave, and exactly who I wanted."

Her hand moved in slow circles between Ari's shoulder blades, over the warmth the floggers had left.

"Water first," she said. "Then tea. Then you're going to lie there and let me fuss, and you're going to tell me all about Tuesday." A pause, and the faintest thread of the old edge: "That's not a request, either."

She didn't move to get up yet. She held on and counted the breaths, and waited to feel them slow.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex heard the word and heard, underneath it, everything that wasn't there. It came out single and scraped thin, the only word Ari seemed to have left. She did not mistake it for an invitation to carry on as though nothing had changed. Words were fraying, and she adjusted.

"Green," she repeated quietly. "I heard you."

She reached past Ari's head for the water on the side table. It was always there, set out before the scene along with the blanket and the cuffs. She slid a hand beneath Ari's neck and tipped the glass to their mouth, slow, a little at a time. "Small sips. There's no hurry. There never is with me."

When the glass was back on the table she took Ari's right hand and folded it around two of her own fingers.

"Listen to me, because this matters more than anything else I say tonight. You're past talking, and that's all right. I like you like this. But I won't have you trapped behind a word you can't reach." She pressed once against Ari's grip. "Squeeze twice, hard, and it's red. Everything stops, same as if you'd said it. Squeeze once when I ask, and it's green. Show me now, so I know your hand can do it."

She waited, eyes on the hand and on the face at once, until she had felt both signals clearly. Only then did she nod.

"Good. Keep hold of me. I'll be checking."

She left that hand free, wrapped around her fingers, and took Ari's other wrist in her other hand. She laid it against the leather above Ari's head and held it there with her familiar two fingers of give. Then she let the warmth leave her face again. She didn't do it all at once this time. She did it slowly, deliberately, so Ari could watch it go.

"You're a mess," she said, low and even. "Wrung out, half gone, and you *still* said green. Couldn't bear for me to stop, could you? Couldn't bear to be done with." She bent until her mouth was just above theirs, not touching. "Greedy. Shameless. Mine."

Her hand drew the blanket down to Ari's waist and then lower, unhurried, and she followed it with her palm. She moved across the flushed skin of the chest and the soft plane of the stomach, where muscles jumped under her fingers. She lingered at the hip bone. She pressed her thumb there, hard enough to be felt, and watched the breath hitch.

"Still," she said. "I didn't say you could move."

She slid lower, and her touch found Ari already wet and aching from the first time. She did not hurry. She traced slow, deliberate circles, just shy of where Ari wanted her, then just over, then away again. Each time she withdrew she watched the frustration break across their face, and she let herself enjoy it openly.

"Look at that. I've barely touched you and you're begging with your whole body. No words at all, and you're still the loudest thing in the room."

She pressed one finger into them, slowly, all the way, and held it there. She felt the heat close around it and the tremor that ran through Ari from the inside out. Then she added a second and curled them. She set a rhythm that was steady and unrelenting and far too slow, the pace of a woman with the whole night and no intention of giving any of it back.

"This is what you asked for," she murmured, working her hand with the same fussy precision she gave the floggers and the cuffs. "Nothing gentle. Nothing soft. Just me, taking exactly what I want from you, and you lying there because you can't do anything else."

Her thumb found the swollen place above her fingers and pressed. She held it there, then moved it in tight circles, and she watched the arch of the spine and the helpless tilt of the head against the bench.

"Eyes on me." Sharp. An anchor. "*Here.* You don't disappear. You stay with me and you feel every bit of this."

She read the eyes as they came back to hers, glassy but tracking. Then, without breaking her rhythm, she moved the fingers held in Ari's right hand. "Colour."

She waited for the squeeze. She would have stopped dead without it. When it came, one clear pulse, she let her mouth curve against Ari's cheek.

"Good. Then I'm not finished with you."

She sped up. The slow, patient rhythm tightened and deepened, her wrist working and her fingers curling on every stroke. Her thumb never left its place. She kept up a low, constant stream of words, every one from the page they had written together. She called Ari desperate, easy, ruined, made for this, and she gave none of it any cushion. The sounds beneath her went ragged and then wordless, and the thighs began to shake against her arm. She felt the tightening build around her fingers, the whole body drawing up like a held breath.

"Not yet," she said. "You wait until I tell you."

She held them there, right at the edge, for one breath, then two, then three. She counted them against the wrist under her hand and watched Ari's face for the exact moment when wanting started to tip toward too much.

It was close. She saw it.

"*Now.*"

She didn't slow as it broke. She worked them through every pulse and shudder and kept the pressure steady until the clenching around her fingers began to ease. Only then did she gentle her hand. She slowed by degrees, stilled, and finally slipped her fingers free, and she laid her palm flat and warm between Ari's legs, just holding.

Then she said the word she'd saved, quietly, into their hair.

"*Good.*"

The cold went out of her all at once, as if she had set it down on the table beside the floggers. She let go of the pinned wrist and chafed it between her palms. She took the other hand, the one that had held her fingers all this time, pressed a kiss into its palm, and kept hold of it.

"That's it. That's everything. You're done, darling. You don't have to hold anything up anymore."

She drew the blanket back over both of them and tucked it around Ari's shoulders, and she settled her weight alongside rather than above, one arm firm across their chest, where the heart was still hammering.

"Every word I said stays in there," she murmured. "Out here, you were brave and lovely, and you trusted me with all of it. I'm so proud of you I could burst."

She reached for the water again and held it ready at Ari's lips, and she waited. She counted breaths against her arm and felt for the moment they began to slow.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I take a sip, then turn my head into her shoulder, letting the last tremors run through me. My hand finds hers under the blanket, holds on. "You kept your promise," I manage, voice rough but clear.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex felt the words against her shoulder before she fully heard them: the warmth of breath, the rough edge of the voice, and underneath it something clear and whole that had not been there a few minutes ago. She closed her eyes for a moment. Clear. A full sentence, with a subject and a verb and a meaning. It came from somewhere solid.

She set the glass back on the table without letting go of the hand that had found hers.

"I always do," she said, and it wasn't the game's voice, or the cold one, or even quite the soft one. It was simply hers, plain and quiet. "That's the whole arrangement, pet. You give me everything, and I keep every promise I make with it. The ones about not softening and the ones about stopping. They're the same promise, really. I just wear different faces for them."

Her thumb moved slowly over Ari's knuckles, then turned the hand over and traced the inside of the wrist where the cuff had sat. The skin there was warm, unmarked, just faintly pink. She checked it anyway, and then the other, because she would have been a stranger to herself if she hadn't.

"Your wrists are fine," she reported, as if Ari had asked. "Your back will be pink and smug about it tomorrow. I kept it high. Nothing near your spine." She pressed her lips briefly to Ari's hair. "I'll put arnica on it before you sleep, and you'll complain that it's cold, and I'll ignore you."

The radiator ticked. Somewhere beyond the curtains a car passed, its headlights sliding briefly across the ceiling and gone. Vex let the ordinary world come back into the room by degrees, a little at a time, the way she had let the water in.

"You scared me a little, earlier," she said after a while, and there was no reproach in it at all. "Twice you went further than I expected, and I had to come and find you. I'm not telling you that so you'll feel bad. You didn't do anything wrong. I'm telling you because we'll talk about it properly tomorrow, over breakfast, when your head's your own again. What it felt like from in there. Whether you knew you'd gone. What I can do to catch it sooner." Her arm tightened across Ari's chest, a small squeeze. "That's for the notebook, not for tonight. Tonight you did beautifully, and you came back every single time I asked you to."

She shifted, carefully, so that Ari's head sat more comfortably in the hollow of her shoulder, and drew the blanket up another inch.

"Now," she said, and a thread of the old dryness crept back in, affectionate and unmistakable. "You owe me a story. Four days of thinking about this, you said. Since Tuesday." Her mouth curved against Ari's temple. "I want to know what Tuesday was. What set it off. Whether you were at your desk being terribly professional while all this was going on behind your eyes."

She reached, without looking, for the mug she had set out before the scene and found the flask beside it, still warm. She poured one-handed, her other hand never leaving Ari's, and she didn't hurry that either.

"Tea first," she said, holding it where it could be reached. "Honey in it, because you need the sugar and I'm not asking. Then Tuesday. Slowly. Take as long as you like."

She settled back against the bench, Ari's weight warm and loose against her, and waited. She was still counting the breaths, and she was still missing nothing. For the first time all evening she was not waiting for a colour at all.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: The tea is too sweet, just the way I like it after. I take a slow sip, letting the warmth settle. "Tuesday," I start, my voice still a little rough. "You wore that grey sweater to breakfast. The one with the high neck. You didn't even touch me."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex was quiet for a moment. Then something happened to her face that she did not quite manage to control. It started at the corner of the mouth and spread, slow and helpless, into her eyes.

"The grey sweater," she repeated.

She knew exactly which one. Charcoal, soft wool gone slightly thin at the elbows, the high neck that sat just under her jaw. She had put it on because the flat had been cold and she had been running late, and she had stood at the counter buttering toast and reading something on her phone and thinking, as far as she could now remember, about nothing more thrilling than whether the boiler needed servicing.

"I was reading about *radiators*, pet," she said, and a low laugh escaped her, warm against Ari's hair. "I was entirely oblivious. And you were sitting across from me having an entire evening's worth of thoughts over your porridge."

She shifted the mug a little so Ari could reach it more easily, and her thumb resumed its slow path over the knuckles under the blanket.

"*You didn't even touch me.*" She tasted the phrase the way she had tasted the other words tonight, turning it over. "That was the part, wasn't it? Not the sweater. Not really. The sweater was just where it caught. It was that I was right there and I didn't reach for you, and you had to sit with it."

She didn't say it as an accusation or a tease. It was simply what she did: noticing, weighing, keeping. She had been doing it for two years, and she was not about to stop just because the leather was back on the table.

"Well. That's very useful to know." A note of the dryness returned, affectionate and unmistakable. "Four days of torment from a woman eating toast. I shall have to be much more careful at breakfast." A pause, and the smile deepened. "Or much less careful. I haven't decided yet."

Her hand left Ari's knuckles long enough to brush the damp hair back from their forehead, and then it came back and took hold again, as if it had never gone.

"Tell me the rest," she said softly. "What were you thinking, sitting there with your spoon? And don't tidy it up for me. I want the version that was actually in your head, not the polite one." Her mouth curved against Ari's temple. "You're not in any state to be polite anyway. It's one of my favourite things about you like this."

The radiator ticked. The tea steamed faintly in the lamplight. Vex settled back against the bench with Ari's weight warm along her side. She was already making a note, somewhere in the tidy back room of her mind, to leave the grey sweater folded on the end of the bed tomorrow morning, and to watch very closely what happened to Ari's face when they saw it.

She waited, listening, in no hurry at all.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I was thinking about the way your hands looked when you stirred your tea. I wanted them on me instead. Wanted you to walk around the table and take the spoon right out of my hand.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The salle had emptied an hour ago and Corvo was still there, because of course he was, rewrapping a grip that did not need rewrapping.

"Three-two," he said, without looking up. "I want it on record that the third was generous."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "It's on record that you were slow," I say, and drop my bag next to his.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
"Slow," Corvo repeated, giving the word the same suspicious weight he'd give a blade that flexed wrong. He set the grip down on the bench — the wrap was immaculate, had been immaculate the last two times he'd redone it — and finally looked up.

Reyes's bag had landed close enough that its strap lay across his own. Four years of reading this man's distance, and Corvo knew exactly what it meant when Reyes closed it.

"Slow is three touches to your two," he said. "Slow is standing in an empty salle an hour after lights-out, rewrapping a grip that didn't need it, waiting to see whether you'd actually walk out or whether you'd—" he tipped his chin at the bags, the crossed straps, the whole arrangement, "—do that."

He stood. He didn't step in — he'd never once made anything easy for this man, and he wasn't about to start with the footing — but he didn't give ground either. He left the distance exactly what it was: one lunge, if either of them meant it.

"So. Pick your line." His voice came out even. His pulse wasn't, and he suspected Reyes could hear it anyway. "Take the bag, call me slow all the way to the door, and we do this again next month. Or say the thing you came back to say." A beat. "En garde either way."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The bench caught Corvo at the backs of his knees and he went down pulling Reyes with him — one hand fisted in the man's collar, the other, empty at last of anything he could pretend to be working on, spread flat against the warm plane of his back. Four years of reading this man's measure, and now there wasn't any. Zero. Corps à corps, the card for which was yellow, and there was no referee in the building, and neither of them had ever once honored a penalty they thought they could get away with.

Corvo laughed against his mouth — ragged, delighted, the laugh of a man who'd finally been given the match he'd spent four years angling for — and then he stopped laughing and got to work.

"For the record," he started, and got no further, because the words stopped being words somewhere around his sternum. Fine. He'd make the confession with his hands instead: blunt, honest, mapping the back he'd done nothing to but shove for four years. He bit down where Reyes's neck met his shoulder, deliberate, setting a tempo the way he set everything with this man — no touch given away for free.

He wasn't being quiet either. He'd stopped trying somewhere between the

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I shift my weight, pinning him to the bench with my body. "*That* was slow too," I breathe against his ear, my grip tightening on his hip. "But I'm not complaining."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: My hand slides up to tangle in his hair, pulling just enough to make his breath catch. "Seen you watching me during drills," I say, voice rough. "Always wondered if you fought dirty off the piste too."

dialogue.name: Corvo
