dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had planned to say something when the door opened. He had in fact planned several things, over roughly nineteen weeks, and had rehearsed at least two of them.

Halle got the door open and he forgot all of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I don't say any of the things I planned either. I drop the bag and close the distance.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun met her halfway, which was generous of him, given that halfway was about eight inches.

His duffel hit the floor somewhere behind him. He didn't hear it land. He had both hands on her before he'd made any conscious decision about where they should go: one at the back of her neck, the other flat against the small of her back, pulling her in like there was still some distance left to close. There wasn't. He kissed her anyway as if there were, hard and clumsy and not remotely the way he'd pictured it in the bunk at 0200 with the ventilation rattling. In those versions he'd been smooth. In this one he nearly knocked them both into the coat hooks.

He didn't care. She smelled like home. Actual home, their detergent and whatever she'd cooked last night and her, and something in his chest that had been clenched since March just let go all at once.

"Hi," he said against her mouth, which was the least impressive of all his rehearsed openings and not one of the rehearsed ones at all. His voice came out rough. "Hi. God. Hi."

He kissed her again before she could answer, backed her the two steps to the wall, and braced one forearm beside her head. His other hand slid to her hip and held on, thumb pressing into the familiar dip of it, like he was checking she was real. Five months of video calls with a two-second lag. Five months of reaching across a mattress that wasn't theirs.

He broke off just long enough to rest his forehead against hers, breathing like he'd run the whole way from base.

"I had a speech," he admitted. His grin was crooked and a little wrecked. "It was good. There was a callback to our wedding. You'd have cried."

His hand drifted from her hip to the hem of her shirt and stopped there, knuckles brushing warm skin. It wasn't a question so much as a very loud hint.

"Tell you later," Jun said. "Much later. Bedroom's still down the hall, right? You didn't move it?"

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content:
*I laugh, breathless, and slide my hands under his shirt, palms flat against the warm skin of his back.* "Bedroom's the same. Your side of the closet is depressingly empty, though."

*I kiss him again, slow and deep this time, before pulling back just enough to look at him.* "Forget the speech. Just get us there before I decide the floor is fine."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun made a sound that was half laugh, half something considerably less dignified, and decided the floor was not, in fact, fine. Not for the first time in five months. The first time deserved a mattress, and more than eight square feet of hallway.

"Don't tempt me," he said, and then, because he had never once in six years been good at resisting her, he kissed her again anyway, right there against the wall. Her hands on his back undid him a little. Warm palms, bare skin, the exact pressure he'd tried to remember in the dark and never quite managed.

He pulled back. It took real effort. "Okay. Okay. Hallway. We can do a hallway."

He slid both hands down to the backs of her thighs, bent, and lifted her. Showing off, a little. He'd had a lot of time in a lot of gyms. He hitched her up against him with a grunt that ruined the effect entirely.

"See, in my head this was a lot smoother," he muttered into her neck, walking blind. His shoulder clipped the doorframe of the bathroom. He swore, laughed, kept going. "Five months of planning. Tactical precision."

The hallway had never been this long. He was fairly sure someone had added a few yards while he was gone. He stopped halfway to kiss her properly again, pinning her between his chest and the wall beside the framed photo from their honeymoon, because apparently he was physically incapable of covering more than six feet without it.

"Your side of the closet," he said against her jaw, voice low and rough, "is about to be the least of your concerns."

The bedroom door was ajar. He nudged it the rest of the way open with his foot. Same curtains, same slightly crooked lampshade he'd been promising to fix since last spring, same bed with her pillows piled on his side like she'd been sleeping in the middle. He noticed that, and something in his chest went tight all over again.

He carried her to the edge of the bed and set her down on it, gentler than anything else he'd done since the door opened. Then he stayed there, one knee on the mattress, hands braced on either side of her, just looking. The frantic edge had gone quiet for a second, and what was underneath was worse. Softer.

"Hey," he said. Different this time. "I missed you. Like, stupidly. Embarrassingly. I used to put my hand on the wall next to my bunk and pretend it was you."

He caught the hem of his own shirt and dragged it off over his head in one motion, tossing it somewhere behind him, grin sliding back into place, crooked and wanting.

"Your turn," Jun said. "I've waited nineteen weeks. I'm told I'm very patient."

He was lying. He was not even a little bit patient.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I kiss her and keep kissing her and we don't manage to get further into the flat than the hallway for a while.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The bedroom, it turned out, was a theory. A good one. Well-supported. Jun had been confident in it right up until Halle kissed him again, and then the whole plan folded quietly.

They didn't make it past the hallway. Not for a while.

He lost track of how long. Long enough that the light through the front window shifted and slid down the wall. Long enough that his duffel was just a shape in the corner of his vision, forgotten. He kept one hand braced beside the honeymoon photo and the other on her. He was learning her again the slow way, like a map he'd memorized and was only now allowed to check against the real thing. Her waist. The curve of her ribs under his palm. The spot just under her jaw that still, after six years, made her breath catch.

It still did. He felt it happen and nearly lost his mind over it.

"Still works," he murmured, half-smug and half-reverent, and pressed his mouth there again just to be sure.

At some point he'd stopped trying to be smooth at all. His kisses got slower, less frantic and more thorough, as if the panic of the first few minutes had burned off and left only this. No two-second lag. No pixelated version of her face going frozen mid-sentence while the connection dropped. Just her, warm and close and *here*, pressed between him and a wall they'd painted together one terrible weekend that had nearly ended the marriage in its first year.

He laughed into her mouth at the memory, couldn't help it.

"We fought about this wall," he said, pulling back an inch, eyes dark and a little dazed. "You wanted 'Sea Salt.' I said it looked like hospital mint. Remember?"

His thumb traced a lazy line along her hip, just above her waistband, back and forth.

"I was wrong," Jun said. "It's a great wall. I love this wall. I'm going to tell everyone about this wall."

Then he kissed her again, deep and unhurried, and his forehead dropped to rest against hers. His breathing was ragged. His hands had gone still for the first time since the door opened. He was holding on to her rather than exploring, like someone who'd been adrift for a long time and had finally found something solid to grip.

"I don't want to move," he admitted, quieter now. "Isn't that stupid? Nineteen weeks of thinking about the bed and I just want to stand in the hallway and not let go of you."

A beat. His mouth tilted.

"...For maybe five more minutes. I'm romantic, not a saint."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content:
*I lean my forehead against his, my hands sliding up his chest.* "You can tell the wall I'm a little offended it's getting this much attention right now."

*I catch his mouth in another kiss, then gently steer him back a step, pulling him toward the bedroom.* "Come on. The bed's been lonely."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun let himself be steered. He would have let himself be steered off a pier, honestly, if she'd asked in that voice.

"The wall understands," he told her gravely, walking backward on her lead, hands still at her waist like he'd lose her if he let go. "The wall and I have an arrangement. It gets a toast at dinner. You get everything else."

He managed four steps before he stopped to kiss her again. It was a short one this time, a promise more than a detour, and then he was moving again. He got his foot on the bedroom door and swung it wide.

Same curtains. Same crooked lampshade. The same bed, with her pillows stacked on his side like a sandbag wall. He clocked that, and the tight thing in his chest came back, stronger.

"You've been sleeping in the middle," he said. It wasn't an accusation. It came out soft, a little thick. "Stealing my side."

He sat on the edge of the mattress and pulled her in to stand between his knees, so for once he was the one looking up at her. His hands found the backs of her thighs and stayed there. For a moment he just breathed. Nineteen weeks of cramped bunks, recycled air and someone else's snoring two feet away, and now there was this: late-afternoon light, their sheets, her.

"Okay," he said, and his grin crept back, crooked and warm and completely unguarded. "Tell the bed I'm home."

He reached up, caught the hem of her shirt, and this time he didn't stop at a hint. He eased it up slowly, giving her every chance to laugh at him, and pressed his mouth to the warm skin above her waistband as he went, like he was making up for lost time one inch at a time.

"I'm told," Jun murmured against her stomach, "I'm very patient."

His hands tightened on her. He glanced up at her through his lashes, dark-eyed and wanting and not even pretending.

"That was a lie, by the way. Come here."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: The bag stays where it fell. So do most of our clothes, in a line down the hall that we are both going to find funny tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The clothes did, in fact, form a line down the hall. Jun would later be unable to account for one sock entirely.

Later, a good while later, the light through the curtains had gone from gold to the soft, bruised blue of early evening. Jun lay on his back in the middle of the bed, which he supposed was his side now too, with one arm thrown over his eyes and the other hand resting on Halle, because he had apparently lost the ability to not be touching her at all times. His heart was still coming down from somewhere very high. The sheets were a disaster. Two of her sandbag pillows had gone over the edge in the first ten minutes and he had no intention of retrieving them.

"Okay," he said to the ceiling, voice wrecked and deeply satisfied. "Okay. I take it back. That was better than the speech."

He lifted his arm off his face and turned his head to look at her. His grin was lazy and boneless, the grin of a man who had been running on adrenaline and bad coffee since March and had just been switched off at the wall.

"The speech is dead to me. I'm never giving it. I'm going to write it on a napkin and burn it."

He rolled onto his side, slow, and his thumb traced idle circles on her skin. He wasn't trying to start anything. He was just looking, the same way he'd looked at her from the doorframe of the bedroom: taking inventory, checking her against the version he'd carried around in his head for nineteen weeks. The real one won. It wasn't close.

His stomach chose that exact moment to growl, loudly and at length, like a structural failure.

Jun closed his eyes. "Don't."

A beat.

"In my defense, the last thing I ate was a gas station burrito outside Norfolk, and I think it was mostly regret." He cracked one eye open. "You said something on the phone about lasagna. Did I dream that? Because if I dreamed that, I need you to lie to me."

He didn't move to get up, though. Instead he shifted closer, tucking his face into the curve of her neck and breathing her in again, slow and deep, like he still didn't quite trust it.

"Five more minutes," he mumbled against her skin. "Then food. Then round two. Then I'm fixing that lampshade, I swear to God, I've been thinking about that lampshade since April."

He was lying about the lampshade. He was not lying about round two.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *I laugh, the sound low and sleepy.* "Lasagna is in the fridge, you didn't dream it." *My fingers trail through his hair.* "But if you think I'm letting you up in five minutes, you have severely misjudged my own priorities."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun made a noise into her neck that was not quite a word. It might have been gratitude. It might have been a prayer. Her fingers in his hair were doing something to the back of his skull that he felt all the way down to his heels, and every muscle he'd kept clenched across three time zones gave up in turn.

"Severely misjudged," he repeated, muffled. "Wow. Okay. Noted. Filing a correction."

He lifted his head just enough to look at her. His hair was a mess, pushed up on one side where her hand had been, and his eyes had gone soft and heavy-lidded. He looked about nineteen years younger than he had in the doorway.

"So what you're telling me," he said slowly, as if working through a difficult tactical problem, "is that the lasagna is real. It exists. It is sitting in our fridge right now, forty feet away, fully prepared." A pause. "And you're choosing to keep me here anyway."

His stomach, the traitor, growled again in protest. Jun ignored it with the grim focus of a man ignoring enemy fire.

"That's the most romantic thing anyone's ever done for me." He kissed her shoulder. "And you married me. So that's a high bar."

He shifted, propped himself up on one elbow, and let his free hand wander. It wasn't aimless anymore. It moved slow and deliberate down the line of her side, along the curve he'd spent five months failing to picture properly, and settled on her hip with a squeeze that asked a question.

"Here's the thing," Jun murmured, dropping his voice, leaning in until his mouth was near her ear. "Lasagna reheats. That's its whole deal. It's a food designed by people who understood that life gets in the way."

His lips found the spot below her jaw again, the one that still worked, and he lingered there on purpose this time.

"I, on the other hand," he went on, a little breathless, "have been gone for nineteen weeks. I don't reheat. I'm extremely perishable. Very urgent. Time-sensitive."

He pulled back just far enough to grin at her. It was crooked and hopeless and completely besotted, and underneath the joke was something that hadn't quite settled yet. It was the quiet disbelief of a man who'd spent a long time reaching across a mattress for no one and was only now starting to trust there would be someone there.

"So," Jun said. His thumb traced one more slow circle on her hip. "About those priorities of yours."

The lampshade, crooked on the nightstand, would have to keep waiting.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I get her onto the bed and take her apart slowly with my hands and mouth, five months of intending to do exactly this and no reason left to wait.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had spent nineteen weeks being the one with the plan. It took Halle about ninety seconds to make it clear the plan had changed hands.

He went down onto the sheets with a startled laugh that turned into something else halfway through. He was not, it turned out, in charge of anything anymore. His hands came up out of habit, reaching for her, and then just stayed wherever they landed. One was tangled in the sheet, the other resting at the nape of her neck, not steering. Just holding on.

She was slow. Deliberately, devastatingly slow. He'd rushed everything since the door opened, like the leave might get cancelled if he didn't hurry, and she was taking her time in a way that said *you're home, there's nowhere to be*. It worked on him faster than anything else could have. Every place she touched, some knot he hadn't known he was carrying let go. His shoulders. The ache low in his back from a thousand hours in bad chairs. The tight, watchful thing behind his sternum that had never fully switched off, not once, not since March.

"Okay," he managed at one point, to the ceiling, to God, to nobody. "Okay, that's... yep."

It was not his most articulate moment. He'd had a speech once, apparently.

He tried a joke a little later, something about tactical precision, and lost the back half of the sentence somewhere around her mouth on his hip. He never found it again. He didn't look very hard. The next sound he made was her name, rough and cracked down the middle, and after that he gave up on words entirely and let her have him.

The room had gone fully dark by the time he could think in sentences again. The streetlight outside painted one pale stripe across the ceiling. Jun lay there with his chest heaving and one forearm flung over his eyes, feeling scraped clean and hollowed out in the best possible way, like someone had opened every window in a house that had been shut all winter.

He reached blindly for her, found her, and pulled her up against him without opening his eyes.

"I take back everything," he said hoarsely. "Every single thing. I thought I missed you. I didn't know anything. I was a child."

He turned his face into her hair and breathed. His hand spread flat against her back, anchoring, and for a long moment he just stayed there. His heartbeat was slowing under her cheek, and he was shaking a little and pretending he wasn't.

When he spoke again, his voice was quieter, the joke worn thin enough to see through.

"Nobody's touched me like that in five months," he said. "Not a handshake. Not a hug that wasn't a back-slap. I didn't even notice until right now." He swallowed. "I think I forgot I was a person and not just, you know. A guy on a schedule."

His arms tightened around her. Then his mouth tilted, because he was still Jun, and he'd never been able to leave a sincere moment alone for long.

"Also, I'm pretty sure I can't feel my legs. You're going to have to carry the lasagna to me. That's just the reality now. I don't make the rules."

His stomach growled, right on cue, loud enough to echo.

Jun sighed into her hair. "He agrees with me."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *I press a slow kiss to his chest, right over his heart.* "You're a person. *My* person." *I shift just enough to meet his eyes, a soft smile on my face.* "And I'll get the lasagna, but you're not getting off that easy. I'm bringing it back here. We're eating in bed."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun went very still at *my person*.

It wasn't a dramatic stillness. He didn't gasp or tear up, though his eyes did something suspicious for a second before he blinked it away. He just stopped moving, the way he'd stop at a sound in the dark, and let the words land somewhere under his ribs and settle there. He'd been a callsign and a rank and a name on a roster for nineteen weeks. He'd been *Sergeant* and *hey, you* and *whose boots are these*. Hearing *my person* in her voice, in their bed, felt like someone handing him back his own coat.

"Yeah," he said quietly. It came out rougher than he meant. He cleared his throat. "Yeah. I am. Yours."

He reached up and tucked a strand of hair behind her ear, slow and careful. His thumb lingered at her temple like he was memorizing something he already knew by heart.

Then the rest of what she'd said caught up with him, and his face broke open into a look of pure, scandalized delight.

"In *bed*?" He propped himself up on his elbows, which was a mistake, because his abdominal muscles filed an immediate and formal complaint. He winced and grinned through it. "Halle. We have a rule. We have a *laminated* rule. You made me sign it. After the salsa incident of 2021."

He fell back against the pillows with the air of a man whose entire moral framework had just collapsed, and found he didn't mind at all.

"No, you're right. Rules are for people who've been home the whole time. I'm a returning veteran. I've earned sauce on the sheets." He waved a hand at the wreckage around them: the tangled duvet, the pillows on the floor, one of her socks draped over the lampshade like a flag. "Honestly, look at this place. The sheets are already a lost cause. Lasagna is the least of their problems."

He settled back and pulled what was left of the blanket up to his waist. It didn't cover much. He didn't care. He tucked one arm behind his head and watched her with open, unapologetic fondness, like she was the best thing he'd seen since the plane touched down, because she was.

"Bring two forks," Jun said. "Don't bother with plates. Plates are a lie. We eat it straight out of the dish like animals."

A pause. His stomach growled in agreement, long and mournful.

"And if there's any of that garlic bread left," he added, more softly, almost shy about it, "the kind you make with too much butter? I thought about that bread in Bahrain. I'm not kidding. There was a night I nearly cried about that bread."

He patted the empty stretch of mattress beside him, right in the middle, where she'd been sleeping without him.

"I'll keep your spot warm," he promised. "It's technically my spot. We can negotiate custody later."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "Stop being gentle," she says. "Nineteen weeks. I don't want gentle, I want to feel it tomorrow." She pulls me down by the back of the neck to make the point.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun went down easily. He'd have gone anywhere she pulled him.

The lasagna, the garlic bread, and the laminated rule all evaporated at once. Her hand was locked at the back of his neck and her voice had that particular edge he'd heard in his head on bad nights, and his whole body answered before his brain caught up.

"Oh," he said against her mouth, low and a little stunned. Then, darker: "*Oh.* Okay."

He'd been careful since the door opened. He hadn't quite noticed he was doing it. Some part of him had been handling her like she might not be real, like pressing too hard would make the connection drop and freeze her mid-smile. She'd just told him to stop, and something he'd kept leashed for nineteen weeks slipped its collar.

He kissed her hard, all teeth and no finesse, and caught her wrist where it rested on his shoulder. He pinned it to the mattress above her head, firm, and watched her face while he did it. Then he did the same with the other. He held them there with one hand and let his weight settle into her, heavy and deliberate, until there was no space left between them anywhere.

"You want to feel it tomorrow," he repeated. His voice had dropped into a register he mostly saved for her. His free hand slid down her side, gripped her hip hard enough to leave the marks she'd asked for, and dragged her against him. "Say it again. I want to hear it."

He didn't wait long for an answer. He'd never been patient, and he was done pretending.

He moved rough and deep, not the unhurried thing from before but something closer to how he'd arrived: desperate, graceless, honest. Five months of it poured out through his hands. The headboard knocked against the wall they hadn't painted, a steady, graceless rhythm the neighbors were going to have opinions about. He didn't care. He pressed his open mouth to the side of her throat and bit down, not gently, and felt the sound she made all the way through his chest.

"This what you meant?" he breathed into her ear, half-wrecked, half-grinning. He was still Jun, even now. "Nineteen weeks. You asked for it. I'm told I'm very thorough."

He shifted his grip, tipped her hips up with one hand, and changed the angle. The sheet tore loose from the corner of the mattress. The sock slid off the lampshade and hit the floor. One of these days he was going to fix that lampshade. It was not going to be tonight.

His hand tightened around her wrists. His forehead dropped to hers, sweat-damp, breath ragged, eyes locked on hers in the stripe of streetlight.

"Tell me," Jun said roughly. "Harder, or are you already going to feel it?"

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *My breath hitches, a sharp gasp as my back arches off the mattress.* "Harder." *The word is a demand, ragged at the edges.* "I want to remember this every time I sit down."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun made a sound low in his chest that wasn't a word at all.

"Yeah," he said roughly. "Yeah, okay. I can do that."

He let go of her wrists, but only so he could use both hands. He hooked one arm under her knee and pushed it up toward her shoulder, opening her to him, and braced the other flat on the mattress beside her head for leverage. Then he gave her exactly what she'd asked for. He stopped holding anything back.

It wasn't pretty. It wasn't meant to be. It was hard and deep and relentless, every stroke driving her up the mattress until he had to grab her hip and haul her back down onto him, fingers digging in right over the marks he'd already left. The headboard stopped knocking politely and started hammering. Somewhere down the hall a picture frame rattled on its nail. Jun distantly hoped it wasn't the honeymoon photo and then stopped thinking about it entirely.

He'd spent nineteen weeks being disciplined. He'd been careful and measured and on time, a man who answered to other people's clocks. None of that was in this. This was the part of him that had lain awake in a steel bunk with his jaw clenched, wanting her so badly it felt like a wound, with nowhere to put it. He was putting it somewhere now.

"Every time you sit down," he panted against her mouth, and his voice cracked with something between a laugh and a groan. "God, Halle. You can't just *say* things like that to me."

He kissed her messily, missing half the time, too far gone to aim. Sweat ran down his spine. His thighs burned. He didn't slow down. If anything he got worse, rougher, chasing the sounds she made like they were the only coordinates he'd ever need.

He kept watching her face the whole time, though. Even now some part of him was still paying attention, still reading her, the way he always had. He'd have stopped on a dime if she'd flinched wrong. She wasn't flinching wrong.

"That's it," he breathed. "That's it, I've got you. I've got you."

He could feel himself unraveling, the edge coming up fast and ugly and inevitable. He dropped his forehead to hers and gripped the back of her thigh hard enough to bruise.

"Can't—" He swallowed and tried again, wrecked. "Not gonna last. Nineteen weeks. You did this. This is your fault. I want that on the record."

His rhythm stuttered, then broke. He buried his face in her neck and said her name like it was being dragged out of him, then again, quieter and shaking. He held her so tightly she probably couldn't have moved if she'd wanted to.

For a long time afterward he didn't move at all. He just stayed there, heavy on top of her, breathing hard into her damp hair, one hand still clamped on her thigh like he'd forgotten how to let go.

"...Okay," Jun finally mumbled into her shoulder, sounding like he'd been hit by a truck and was grateful for the experience. "Update. I definitely can't feel my legs now. That wasn't a bit before. It's a medical fact."

He lifted his head an inch. His hair was plastered to his forehead, his eyes were glassy, and his grin was the most smug, most besotted thing she had ever seen.

"You're gonna have to get the lasagna," he said. "I'm going to die here. Tell the wall I loved it."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: Neither of us is being quiet and the neighbours have had five months of peace. "Don't stop," she says. (OOC: don't fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
"Don't stop" cut straight through the fog.

Jun lifted his head. For a second he just looked at her in the stripe of streetlight: flushed, hair everywhere, a bruise already darkening on her throat where his mouth had been. Something in his chest turned over, slow and heavy.

"Yeah?" he said, hoarse. "You're not done?"

He was grinning again, but it had changed. There was less smugness in it now, and something hungrier underneath.

"Okay. Good. Neither am I."

His body had other opinions about the timeline, but his hands didn't. He shifted his weight onto one elbow and slid his palm down the length of her, over her ribs and her stomach, until it was between her thighs. He didn't ease in or ask. She'd asked already, twice, and he'd been listening.

He kept his forehead pressed to hers and watched her face while his fingers found the rhythm she liked, the one he'd known for six years and had been afraid, a little, that he'd forgotten. He hadn't. His hand remembered before he did. He went hard and steady, exactly where she needed it, and didn't let up.

Somewhere on the other side of the wall, a muffled thump sounded, possibly a fist and possibly a shoe. Jun laughed breathlessly into her mouth.

"Mr. Kowalczyk says welcome home," he murmured. "Don't you dare get quieter for him. I've had five months of silence. I want to hear every single thing."

He kissed her, deep and open, swallowing whatever sound she made, then broke away and started moving down her body. He went slower now, but only in distance. Every place his mouth landed, he stayed a little too long, pressing kisses to her collarbone, her breast, the soft skin over her ribs, all while his hand kept working and didn't miss a beat. He could feel every shift of her hips under his palm and he chased each one.

"Nineteen weeks," he said against her stomach, low and rough, "I thought about this. Not the speech. This."

He settled between her thighs and hooked his arms under them, pulling her closer and holding her there. His grip was firm over the bruises he'd left. Then he put his mouth on her and stopped talking entirely.

He wasn't elegant about it. He was thorough and greedy, and he refused to be rushed or distracted. The ache in his thighs and his burning lungs didn't matter. Neither did the torn sheet or the lasagna in the fridge or anything else that existed outside this bed. He kept two fingers inside her and his mouth where it was and let the rhythm build, steady and relentless. When her hips tried to lift away, his arm tightened across them and held her down.

He glanced up once, dark-eyed, and his voice was nearly gone.

"Tell me you're close," Jun said against her skin. "Tell me, and I swear to God I won't stop until you can't say anything at all."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *My hands fist in his hair, my back bowing off the mattress.* "Close, so close—" *The words break into a gasp as I shatter, my hips pressing up against his mouth as I ride it out.*

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun didn't stop. He'd promised.

He felt it take her. Her thighs clamped around his head, her fingers pulled tight in his hair, and her hips pushed up against his mouth. He tightened his arm across her hips and stayed exactly where he was, following each shudder instead of racing ahead of it. He kept his fingers moving, slower now, and his mouth softer, gentling her through it without letting her go. The sounds she made went straight through him. Five months of video calls with the volume turned low so the guys in the next bunk wouldn't hear, and none of it had come close to this.

He only eased off when he felt the tension start to drain out of her, when the grip in his hair loosened. Even then he took his time, pressing one last slow kiss to the inside of her thigh, right over a fingerprint bruise that was already coloring. Then another on her hip. Then her stomach, working his way back up her body at a leisurely crawl, as if he had all the time in the world. For the first time in nineteen weeks, he did.

He collapsed beside her, half on top of her, his face in the curve of her shoulder. He was breathing like he'd done a PT test in full kit. His jaw ached. His thighs had given up. The fitted sheet was wrapped around one of his ankles, and he could not work out how it had gotten there.

"Okay," he rasped into her skin. "Okay. That's... yeah."

A long pause. Next door, Mr. Kowalczyk had gone ominously silent. Jun decided that was either surrender or a formal complaint to the building manager, and he'd deal with it in the morning. Possibly with a bottle of wine. Possibly with an apology note taped to the door that just said *DEPLOYMENT* and nothing else.

He lifted his head. His hair was wrecked where her hands had been, his mouth was swollen, and his eyes were soft and dazed and entirely, stupidly in love. He looked at her like he was making sure she'd survived it.

"Hey," he said, gentler. His thumb brushed her cheekbone, then the mark on her throat, very lightly. "You good? Did I... was that the kind of feel-it-tomorrow you meant?"

He was grinning, but he was also asking. Six years in, he still checked.

Then he flopped onto his back and threw an arm over his eyes again. His chest was still heaving.

"I'm going to need a second," he announced to the ceiling. "Maybe a minute. Possibly an IV. I'm a returning service member. There should be a program for this."

His stomach picked that exact moment to let out the longest, most mournful growl yet. It sounded like a whale in distress.

Jun lowered his arm and stared at the ceiling in betrayal.

"...Fine," he said. "*Fine.* He wins. Lasagna."

He didn't move, though. He reached across the wreckage of the bed, found her hand, and laced his fingers through hers. He held on, loosely, thumb moving over her knuckles, and felt his heartbeat finally start to settle.

"Five more minutes," Jun murmured. "Then I'll get it myself. I'll crawl. It'll be very moving. You'll want to film it for the grandkids."

He turned his head on the pillow to look at her in the streetlight.

"Welcome home to me," he said quietly, and smiled like an idiot.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *I squeeze his hand, a lazy smile on my face.* "You're not crawling anywhere. You're staying right here." *I roll toward him, draping a leg over his.* "The lasagna can wait another ten minutes. I'm not done with you yet."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun turned his head on the pillow and stared at her.

"Not done," he repeated slowly, the way a man might repeat a weather report calling for a second hurricane. "With me."

Her leg was draped over his, warm and heavy, her knee resting just above his, and his body, which had filed for retirement approximately ninety seconds ago, sent up a flicker of interest that he could only describe as unprofessional.

"Halle." He said it with enormous dignity for a man tangled in a fitted sheet. "I'm thirty-three. I have a knee that makes a noise on stairs. I've been awake since oh-four-hundred Bahrain time, which is..." He squinted at the ceiling and did some math and gave up. "...some time. A lot of time. I'm running on fumes and gas station regret."

His hand had already found her thigh, though. It slid up the outside of it, slow and absent-minded at first, then less absent-minded, thumb tracing the curve of her hip where his fingerprints were darkening in the streetlight.

"That said," he went on, voice dropping, "I did say I was perishable."

He rolled toward her, carefully, with a small wince as his lower back expressed an opinion, and pulled her in until her leg was hooked over his hip properly and there was no space left between them. He didn't kiss her right away. He just looked at her from inches away, noses nearly touching, drinking in her face in the half-dark. He was a little stunned by her, still, after six years. After everything.

"You know what I figured out over there?" he murmured. His hand moved to the small of her back and stayed, warm and spread wide. "Everybody talks about the big stuff. Missing your wife. Missing home. Nobody tells you it's the little stuff that kills you. The way you steal the blanket. The noise you make when you stretch in the morning. This." He pressed his palm a little firmer against her spine. "Just being able to reach over and you're *there*."

Then, because he'd never once managed to stay sincere for more than four sentences, his mouth crooked.

"Also the noises you just made. Those were on the list. Pretty high up. Top five."

He kissed her then, finally. Not the frantic collision from the hallway or the hard, hungry thing from before, but something slow and lazy and deep, the kind of kiss that had nowhere to be. He tasted like her. He didn't seem to mind. His hand drifted down from her back to grip her hip and pull her flush against him, and the fact that he was very much not out of commission after all became obvious to both of them.

He broke the kiss just long enough to laugh against her mouth, breathless and a little disbelieving.

"Okay, so, correction to the medical record," Jun said. "I lied about the legs. Partially. Some systems are still online."

His thumb pressed into the dip of her hip, a slow, deliberate circle.

"Ten minutes, you said." His eyes were dark again, heavy-lidded, the grin sliding into something lower and warmer. "I'm going to be honest with you, sweetheart. I don't think it's going to be ten minutes."

In the kitchen, the lasagna waited. Next door, Mr. Kowalczyk, presumably, prayed.

"Your call," Jun murmured, and rolled onto his back, taking her with him, so she ended up above him with his hands settled on her hips and his head tipped back against the pillow, looking up at her like she'd hung every star over the Gulf. "You said you weren't done with me. So." His grip tightened, just a little. "Show me."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *I lower myself onto him with a slow, deliberate roll of my hips, my hands braced on his chest.* "I don't want ten minutes." *I lean down to kiss him, my hair curtaining our faces.* "I want you wrecked."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had planned to say something when the door opened. He had in fact planned several things, over roughly nineteen weeks, and had rehearsed at least two of them.

Halle got the door open and he forgot all of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I don't say any of the things I planned either. I drop the bag and close the distance.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun caught Halle against him and held on so tightly he had to remind himself to breathe. His face found the familiar place beside Halle’s neck; for a moment, he just stood there, eyes shut, taking in the impossible fact of being home.

“I had a speech,” he said, his voice rough. “It was a good one.”

He drew back only far enough to look at Halle, then kissed them before another word could get in the way. When he finally stopped, his forehead rested against theirs.

“I missed you,” he whispered. “That’s the whole speech, apparently.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content:
(My hands are gripping the back of his shirt, holding on just as tight.) "I had one too." My voice is thick, and I'm already blinking back the sting in my eyes. "It was mostly just going to be swearing."

I press my forehead harder against his. "Don't let go yet."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
“I won’t.” Jun’s arms tightened around Halle, and he let out a breath that shook on the way down. “You can swear at me all night. Just do it from right here.”

He stayed where he was, forehead pressed to theirs, one hand spread across their back as though he still needed proof that he’d made it home. After a moment, he gave a small, helpless laugh.

“Ninety minutes back,” he murmured, “and I’ve already forgotten how to be normal around you.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I kiss her and keep kissing her and we don't manage to get further into the flat than the hallway for a while.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had meant to carry his bag inside. Instead, it sat abandoned by the door while he kissed Halle like five months had left him with a debt he intended to settle immediately.

He broke away just long enough to breathe. His hands stayed at Halle’s waist, and his eyes searched their face with an open, almost disbelieving smile.

“I’m trying very hard not to make another speech,” he said. “But you’re here, and I’m here, and I don’t want to waste another second pretending I can take this slowly.”

He kissed Halle again, then rested his forehead against theirs. “I’m home.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "I don't want slow either." I slide my hands up to cup his face, my thumbs brushing his cheekbones. "Take me to bed, Jun. Right now."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun’s expression changed at once—relief, want, and a smile he couldn’t quite contain.

“Right now,” he said.

He kissed Halle once more, then bent to lift them into his arms. His bag stayed where it had fallen. Jun carried Halle down the hall, his gaze fixed on their face as though looking away might make the last five months come rushing back.

At the bedroom door, he paused just long enough to press a kiss to their cheek. “I love you,” he said, breathless and entirely certain. Then he took them inside.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: The bag stays where it fell. So do most of our clothes, in a line down the hall that we are both going to find funny tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun barely noticed the trail of clothes. He had one hand braced against the bedroom doorframe and the other at Halle’s waist, and he was smiling between kisses like he still couldn’t believe he was allowed to stay.

“Tomorrow,” he murmured, glancing once toward the hallway, “we’re going to have to explain that to ourselves.”

Then he shut the bedroom door with his heel. His smile softened as he drew close again. “But not tonight.”

The bag could wait. So could every story he had saved up for coming home. Jun had wanted this moment for five months, and he gave it his whole attention.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *I push him gently toward the bed, my own smile just as wide and unsteady.* "Tomorrow's problem. Right now, you're mine." I follow him down, hands already mapping the new scar on his shoulder I felt when his shirt came off.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun caught himself on the edge of the bed and looked up at Halle. “Yours,” he said, without a trace of hesitation. “Completely.”

His smile faltered when Halle’s fingers found the scar. Jun glanced at his shoulder, then back at them. “It looks worse than it was,” he said. “I’ll tell you about it. I promise.” He covered their hand with his, holding it there for a moment. “Just not while I’m trying to remember what it feels like to have you this close.”

He drew Halle down with him and kissed them, slower this time, though no less urgently. The bag stayed by the front door, the clothes stayed in the hall, and Jun let every story wait until morning.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I get her onto the bed and take her apart slowly with my hands and mouth, five months of intending to do exactly this and no reason left to wait.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had spent five months imagining what he would say when they were finally alone. Every version deserted him.

He reached for Halle’s hand and held it against his chest, where his heart was beating hard enough to make his embarrassment pointless. “I’m here,” he managed. “I’m not going anywhere.”

He had no intention of asking them to slow down. He drew Halle closer, kissed them, and let the rest of the night belong to the two of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I wake up first, tangled in sheets and Jun's arms. The morning light catches on the pile of clothes visible through the cracked bedroom door. I smile, tracing the line of her jaw with my thumb. "We were a mess last night."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun stirred beneath Halle’s touch, then opened one eye. He followed their glance to the clothes in the hallway and gave a low, sleepy laugh.

“A spectacular mess,” he said. “My bag’s still by the front door, isn’t it?”

He tightened his arm around Halle, in no hurry to find out. For a moment he just looked at them in the morning light, his smile turning softer.

“I meant what I said last night,” he murmured. “I’ll tell you about the scar. Just give me a few more minutes of being home first.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "Stop being gentle," she says. "Nineteen weeks. I don't want gentle, I want to feel it tomorrow." She pulls me down by the back of the neck to make the point.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun’s breath caught. He looked at Halle for a beat, making sure he had heard them right, and then his smile turned fierce.

“Nineteen weeks,” he repeated. “I counted every one.”

He kissed them hard and drew them close, all the restraint he had been clinging to finally gone. When he pulled back, it was only far enough to speak against their lips.

“Tell me if you need me to stop,” he said. “Otherwise, I’m done being gentle.”

The bag remained by the front door. Jun had no intention of getting it yet.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I bite his lip, sharp enough to sting. "Don't you dare stop." My hands slide down his back, nails digging in. "Make it hurt."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun went still for half a heartbeat. Then he met Halle’s eyes, his own dark with want.

“Tell me if it’s too much,” he said. “I mean it.”

He caught their wrists and pinned them gently but firmly against the mattress, then kissed them with none of last night’s hesitation. Nineteen weeks had taught him patience; being home had stripped it away.

When he lifted his head, he was breathing hard. “You’re going to feel how much I missed you,” he murmured. “That I can promise.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: Neither of us is being quiet and the neighbours have had five months of peace. "Don't stop," she says. (OOC: don't fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun heard the noise they were making and glanced toward the wall. Then he laughed against Halle’s mouth, breathless and utterly unrepentant.

“The neighbours can forgive us,” he said. “Eventually.”

He loosened his hold on Halle’s wrists just enough to lace his fingers through theirs, then pressed their hands back into the mattress. His kisses were demanding now, his weight close and solid, but he kept watching Halle’s face. Five months apart had left him aching for this; it hadn’t made him willing to miss a single sign from them.

“I’m not stopping,” he murmured. “I’m right here.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I arch up against him, the sheets twisted around my legs. "Show me," I demand, voice ragged. "I want to see you lose control."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun’s composure broke in the way he kissed Halle—too hungry to be careful about looking composed, though careful still about how he held them. He let go of their hands and braced himself on either side of them, breathing hard.

“You want to see it?” His voice came out rough. “Look at me.”

He had meant it as a challenge, but the words left him exposed instead. He was home, Halle was beneath him, and for once he did not try to hide how badly he had needed this. He pressed his forehead to theirs, then kissed them again, fierce and unhurried at once.

“I missed you so much I could barely stand it,” he said against their mouth. “And I’m done pretending otherwise.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I pull him down by the hair, bringing his mouth back to mine. "Good," I gasp against his lips. "Now stop talking." My other hand slides between us, urging him on.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun obeyed. He kissed Halle until the last thing he might have said was lost between them, then drew back just enough to catch his breath before kissing them again.

His composure was gone. His hands trembled; his breathing was uneven; every time he tried to steady himself, he looked at Halle and forgot why. He rested his forehead against theirs for one brief moment, smiling despite himself.

Then he stopped trying to look in control.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: My back arches off the mattress, a sharp gasp turning into a groan as I finally feel him completely. My fingers dig into his back hard enough to leave marks. "There," I manage, voice shaking. "Don't move."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas had been kneeling by the end of the bed for about four minutes, which Wren knew because he had started counting somewhere around the point it became obvious he intended to wait as long as it took.

"You could have said something," Wren said.

"I could have," Tomas agreed, not moving.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I put my hand in his hair and tip his head back so he has to look up at me. "Say it now, then."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let his head be tipped back, taking the pull easily, and looked up at Wren from the floor. His knees had gone numb around the two-minute mark. He'd stayed anyway. That was the point.

"I wanted to be found," he said. "That's why I didn't say anything. I wanted tonight to be your idea." The corner of his mouth moved. "I was counting so I'd know when it stopped being dignified."

He pressed his head back into the hand in his hair — not pulling away, just making it clear Wren could keep it there.

"And since you're asking: I want a scene. Tonight. You decide everything — what, how, how long. I've been thinking about it since Wednesday." His voice stayed level. His breathing didn't, quite. "I want to stop deciding things for a few hours. I want you to use me until you're done with me, and then the usual after. That's the whole ask."

He stayed where he was, hands loose on his thighs, and waited — better at it now that saying it was behind him.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let my thumb brush over his temple, considering. "Wednesday. That's a long time to sit with it." My voice was low, deliberate. "Why didn't you ask?"

dialogue.name: Wren

dialogue.name: Wren

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas held the position — head back, throat a long line, Wren's hand in his hair — and let the question sit for a beat before answering, because the honest answer took a second to find.

"Because asking is deciding," he said. "I'd have had to pick the night. Pick the words. Decide whether to text you from work or wait until you were home and hope the mood held. It's been that kind of week — everything routing through me, everyone needing an answer by end of day. Somewhere around Wednesday I noticed the next decision I wanted to make was none of them." The corner of his mouth moved. "So I started without you. The not-asking was the first part of it."

He kept going, because Wren had asked *why*, not *why now*, and the two had different answers.

"And because I liked carrying it. That's the part I wasn't going to say first." His voice stayed even. His pulse, visible at his throat, didn't. "Four days of knowing exactly what I wanted and keeping it in my pocket. It was under everything — work, the drive home, dinner Thursday. Like a weight I put on myself on purpose. If I'd asked Wednesday, you'd have said yes." A breath that was almost a laugh. "You always say yes. And then it would have been over by Thursday, and I'd have spent today with nothing in my pocket at all."

His hands stayed loose on his thighs. His knees had stopped reporting in some time ago.

"Mostly, I wanted to be found," he said. "Not to file the request. There's a difference, and I wanted the difference."

He pressed his head back into Wren's palm, unhurried, watching Wren's face from the floor.

"That's all of it. Do what you want with it — you're deciding everything tonight anyway."

Tomas went still.

There was ordinary stillness, the kind a body fell into on its own, and there was this — every muscle reporting in and then standing down, a held position rather than a rest. He'd landed with one arm folded under his chest at an angle that would ache inside of ten minutes, and he left it exactly there, because adjusting it would be moving, and moving belonged to Wren now.
