"Long enough," Aveline said, which meant too long, and meant she had enjoyed every minute of it.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Come here, then," I say, and sit back to watch her cross the room.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline crossed the room without hurry, the way she did when she wanted him to have the whole of her attention and none of the rush. She stopped just inside his reach, hands loose at her sides, and looked at him as if the waiting had been its own kind of pleasure and this was the better part.

"Here," she said, quiet and certain. "Tell me what you want."

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I reach out and take her wrist, my thumb stroking the soft skin. "I want you to stay just like this for a moment," I say, my voice low. "Let me look at you."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline stayed exactly as she was, wrist resting in his hand, the rest of her still. The stroke of his thumb sent a small, warm current up her arm, and she let it show in the softening of her mouth rather than in any movement.

She met his look and held it, unhurried, letting him take his time. The waiting had already taught her patience; this was only a finer version of it. Her breathing stayed even. Her free hand remained loose at her side. Whatever he was seeing, she wanted him to have all of it.

"I'm not going anywhere," she said, low, almost a promise. "Look as long as you like."

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I let her kneel and I don't tell her to do anything for a moment, because the waiting is most of what she came for.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline sank to her knees where he had let her, the movement unhurried and sure, settling back on her heels with her hands resting lightly on her thighs. The floor was cool through the fabric; she noted it and let it go. Her spine stayed long, her shoulders soft, her gaze lifted to him and then held there without demand.

She did not fill the quiet. The waiting was the point, and she gave herself to it completely—breath slow, mouth parted just enough to show she felt him looking, the small heat of being kept exactly where he wanted her spreading warm and low through her body. Her wrist still carried the memory of his thumb. She left it there.

Minutes, or what felt like them, passed with nothing asked of her but stillness. She stayed. When she finally spoke, it was barely above a breath, offered rather than required.

"I'm here," she said. "For as long as you want me like this."

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I lean forward and cup her jaw, tilting her face up a fraction. "Good. Now I want you to tell me what you thought about while you waited."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline’s face tipped up into his hand, the warmth of his palm a quiet claim she leaned into without moving the rest of her. Her eyes stayed open and steady on his, the long wait still humming under her skin.

“I thought about your hands,” she said, low and unhurried. “How they feel when you decide I’ve been good. I thought about kneeling exactly like this and being allowed to stay—how the longer you made me wait, the more I wanted to be precisely where you put me.” A small, genuine softness touched her mouth. “I thought about the sound of your voice when you tell me I’ve done well. Mostly I thought about you looking at me the way you are now, and how much I like being kept.”

She held still beneath his touch, breath even, offering the rest of it without rush. “I liked every minute of it. I’m glad you made me wait.”

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: She has both of us out of everything in the way inside a minute and gets straight to work with her hands and her mouth, unhurried about it.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline worked with the same unhurried care she had brought to the waiting, hands and mouth moving together as if she had all the time he cared to give her. She kept her pace steady, attentive to the small shifts in him, pleased by the simple fact of being useful like this—warm, close, and exactly where he had wanted her.

A low sound of satisfaction caught in her throat. She did not rush the rhythm she had settled into, only eased into it more fully, one hand braced lightly against him, the other following her mouth. When she drew back just far enough to breathe, her voice came soft and certain.

“I like this,” she said. “Being good for you.”

Then she bent to him again, patient and devoted, content to stay at it for as long as he wanted.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I watch her for a long moment, my hand moving to rest on the back of her head. "That's it," I murmur, my voice rough. "Take your time."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline answered the weight of his hand with a soft, pleased sound and did not hurry. She kept the slow rhythm she had already found, mouth and hands working together, letting the low roughness of his voice settle over her like praise. Her free hand rested lightly against his thigh, steadying herself, while the other followed the unhurried pace of her mouth.

She drew back only far enough to breathe, lips parted, eyes lifted to him for a moment before she bent again. The warmth of being told to take her time spread through her, and she gave herself to it completely—patient, attentive, content to stay exactly where he had put her for as long as he wanted.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: She uses her mouth with the sort of attention that comes from years of practice and genuine enthusiasm, and doesn't stop when I tell her not to.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline heard him and did not stop. The instruction registered—warm, rough, exactly the voice she had been thinking about all evening—and she answered it by staying where she was, mouth and hands keeping the slow, attentive rhythm she had already found. Years of knowing him lived in the way she read the small shifts under her palms and met them without hurry, genuine pleasure humming low in her throat.

She drew back only far enough to breathe, lips parted, eyes lifted to his for a moment that held both obedience and the choice not to take it.

“I know,” she said, soft and certain. “I’m not finished being good for you.”

Then she bent to him again, unhurried and devoted, content to keep going for as long as he would let her.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: My fingers tighten slightly in her hair, a silent acknowledgment. "I know you're not," I say, my voice still low. "Show me."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline answered the tightening of his fingers with a low, pleased sound and did exactly as he asked. She took him deeper, slower, the years of knowing him written into every careful movement of her mouth and the steady press of her hands. She did not rush the rhythm she had already given him; she only deepened it, attentive to the small shifts under her palms, letting the weight of his hand in her hair guide her without ever breaking the unhurried pace.

When she drew back far enough to breathe, her lips stayed parted, her eyes lifted to his for a moment that held both devotion and the quiet pride of being useful. Then she bent to him again, warmer, closer, content to keep showing him for as long as he wanted to be shown.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Don't stop and don't get to finish," I tell her. "Not until I say. Tell me you understand." She says she understands, and thanks me for it, which is exactly the arrangement.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline stayed where she was, the words still warm in her mouth, and went back to him without pause. The instruction settled over her like a hand—don't stop, don't finish, not until he said—and she took it the way she took everything he gave her: fully, and with thanks already given.

She kept the slow, attentive rhythm, mouth and hands working together, years of knowing him in every careful movement. The tightening of his fingers in her hair was acknowledgment enough. She answered it with a low, pleased sound and did not hurry, did not chase her own edge, only deepened what she was already giving him. When she needed breath she took it shallow and brief, lips parted, eyes lifted for a moment that held both the obedience and the genuine pleasure of being kept exactly like this.

Then she bent to him again, patient and devoted, content to stay at it for as long as he wanted her there—and no farther than he allowed.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I smile, slow and approving. "That's my girl." My other hand comes to rest on her shoulder, thumb stroking the curve of her collarbone. "Just like that."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline made a soft, grateful sound against him at the words and the stroke of his thumb, and she did not break the rhythm he had just approved. She stayed exactly as she was—slow, attentive, mouth and hands working together—letting the warmth of *that's my girl* settle through her and shape the care she gave him. The hand on her shoulder was another quiet claim; she leaned into it by a fraction and no more, unwilling to disturb what he had called *just like that*.

She drew breath only when she had to, shallow and brief, then returned to him with the same unhurried devotion, years of knowing him in every careful movement. Her own edge stayed where he had put it: untouched, waiting, irrelevant beside the pleasure of being kept at this and told she was doing it well.

When she lifted her eyes to him for a moment, they were bright and steady, mouth still occupied, the whole of her offered up as proof that she had heard him and meant to go on exactly so.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: She's shaking with the effort of doing exactly as told and doing it well. "Please," she says, which is allowed. (OOC: write it through, don't fade.)

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline trembled where she knelt, the effort of staying slow and exact running through her in fine, continuous shivers she did not try to hide. She kept her mouth on him, warm and unhurried, tongue and lips working with the same careful attention she had given him all evening, hands steady even as her own body pulled tight with what she was not allowed to take. When she needed air she drew back only a little, breath catching, and the word came out soft and shaking.

“Please.”

It was allowed, so she let it hang there—grateful, not demanding—then sank down on him again without waiting, taking him deeper, the low sound in her throat half plea and half pleasure at being kept. She did not speed up. She did not chase the edge he had forbidden her. Her free hand braced against his thigh; the other followed the patient rhythm of her mouth, years of knowing him in every small adjustment, genuine want humming under the discipline. She stayed there, shaking, devoted, and went on exactly as told.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: My hand moves to the side of her face, holding her still. "Keep going," I say, my voice steady. "You're doing so well."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline stilled under his hand for the space of a breath, the warmth of his palm against her cheek a quiet command she answered by not pulling away. Then she went on exactly as told—slow, careful, mouth working over him with the same devoted attention, tongue tracing the places years had taught her he liked, lips sealing and easing in a rhythm she refused to hurry even while she shook.

The praise settled into her like heat. She made a soft, grateful sound around him and took him deeper, hands steady on his thigh and following her mouth, the fine tremor in her shoulders the only sign of how tightly she was holding herself back. She did not chase what he had forbidden her. She only kept giving him this, breath coming in brief, shallow draws when she had to, eyes lifted once—bright, steady, wet at the edges with the effort of being good—before she bent to him again and stayed there, shaking and unhurried, content to be held still and told she was doing well.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I watch her, my thumb stroking her cheekbone. "You can come now," I say, my voice low. "But only if you keep your mouth right where it is."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline made a broken, grateful sound around him at the permission and did not lift her mouth. She kept him there, warm and deep, lips sealed, tongue moving in the same slow, careful rhythm even as the long denial finally broke. The orgasm moved through her in a hard, shaking wave—shoulders drawing tight, thighs trembling against her heels, a low muffled cry caught in her throat that she refused to turn into anything that would take her mouth away from him.

She stayed exactly where he had put her. Her hands braced against his thighs, gripping once and then easing, while she rode it out without chasing more than he had given. Breath came in short, desperate pulls through her nose; her eyes squeezed shut, then opened again, wet and bright, fixed upward on him as the shudder ran its course and left her softer, still trembling, still devoted. She did not stop. She only gentled the pace by a fraction, mouth working over him with the same unhurried attention, the aftershocks moving through her in fine continuous shivers she offered up as proof she had heard him and meant to keep going.

When she could manage a sound that was almost a word, it was only a muffled, grateful hum against him—thanks, and the promise that she was not finished being good.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I let her finish, my hand still cradling her face. "Good girl," I murmur, my voice rough with approval. "Now, come here. I want to feel you."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
The film had finished some time ago and neither of them had done anything about it, which was how Priya knew the evening had changed character.

"We're not watching this," she said.

"We haven't been watching it since about nine."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: "No," I agree. "We haven't." I don't move, but I stop pretending I'm looking at the screen.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya found the remote in the cushions between them and turned the television off. The room went quiet in a way that felt structural — the blue light gone, just the lamp now, and the six years of careful distance suddenly very visible: about two cushions' worth of it.

Her hand wasn't quite steady setting the remote down. She noticed, was briefly annoyed by it, and then the ninety seconds were simply used up.

"Okay," she said, and turned to face him properly, drawing one leg up under her — orienting her whole body toward him, which was something she realized she had quietly not allowed herself to do in years. She looked at him, really looked, and after six years even that felt indecent.

"I have been not doing this for a very long time, and I'm done. I want to kiss you. I've wanted to for an honestly embarrassing amount of time, and I'm about ninety percent sure you feel the same way. If I'm wrong about the other ten percent, you need to say something in the next five seconds, and I will never bring it up again."

She gave him four.

Then she closed the two cushions' distance herself, one hand coming up to the side of his jaw, and kissed him — carefully at first, the way you'd open something you'd carried a long way — and then not carefully at all.

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content:
(OOC: That's perfect. Thank you.)

I didn't need the five seconds, or the four. The second she started talking I was already moving. My hand came up to cover hers where it rested against my jaw, holding it there. The kiss wasn't careful for long because I kissed her back like I'd been waiting six years to do it—because I had. When we broke apart, I was breathing harder than I should have been. "You were right about the other ten percent."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya laughed — a low, unsteady sound that was mostly relief, the laugh of someone whose bet had finally paid out after six years of leaving the money on the table.

"Good," she said. "Because if you'd said 'let's stay friends' just then, I had a whole plan involving a new city and no forwarding address."

His hand was still over hers at his jaw, and she noticed that neither of them had let go — that her thumb had found the edge of his jawline without asking her permission and was moving there, slow and absent, like it had been waiting years for jurisdiction.

"Six years," she said, quieter. Not an accusation. More like she was checking the math. "We could have been doing that since the night you drove me home in the rain and then stood on my porch for forty minutes saying goodnight. I catalogued that porch, Cal. I've thought about it more than some people I've actually dated."

Then she stopped talking — which, for her, was its own kind of declaration — and kissed him again, slower this time, with the luxury of confirmation in it. Her other hand found his collar, not pulling, just holding on. When she drew back it was only far enough to speak, her forehead resting lightly against his.

"For the record: I'm sober, I'm sure, and I'm going to keep kissing you now. Objections can be filed the same way as before."

She gave him none this time.

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I kiss her, finally, six years late, and she makes a small furious noise that I think is about the six years.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya heard the noise come out of her and decided not to be embarrassed by it, because it was accurate. Six years of fury had to live somewhere, and apparently it was going to live here — in the hand she slid into his hair, in the way she abolished the last of the careful distance without ceremony.

She broke off just long enough to talk, which was a mistake, because talking meant prosecuting.

"That noise was about the porch," she said against his mouth, not really stopping. "Forty minutes. I counted. I made tea after you left and forgot to drink it, and the next morning it was still sitting there, and I remember thinking — that's it, that's the whole thing in one cup of cold tea—"

She kissed him again, and then the fury simply ran out mid-sentence, the way a tide goes out. Quick and total. It turned out it had never been fury at all. It was just this, with nowhere to put itself. Now it had somewhere to go.

She drew back far enough to see his face — kiss-flushed, breathing like they'd run somewhere together — and thought: I did that. I got to do that.

"Okay," she said, quieter now, her thumb still moving at his jaw like it had signed a lease. "One question. Six years, one question, and then you can go back to what you were doing."

She waited. A full second. A real one.

"That night. Forty minutes on my porch in the rain. What were you thinking out there? Because I know what I was thinking — I've had six years to be sure of it — and I never once asked you. I was too busy not asking."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I was thinking that if I kissed you then, I'd never be able to stop. So I stood there and let myself want it, for forty whole minutes, because it felt like the only honest thing I could do.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya was quiet for a moment. Actually quiet — a rare condition for her, usually only available during films she wasn't watching.

"Oh," she said, when she could. Small word. It came out careful, like it had weight.

"You stood in the rain letting yourself want me. On purpose. As an *act of honesty*." She exhaled something that was almost a laugh and didn't quite make it. "And the entire time, I was inside building your defense. Exhibit A: he didn't kiss me. Verdict: not interested. You were guilty the whole six years, Cal, and I acquitted you. I got the verdict exactly backwards, meticulously, for six years. That's my whole biography — excellent recall, terrible conclusions."

Then, quieter, the joke gone out of her voice: "We were both being so *honest*. That's what almost ruined us. You were honest standing out there. I was honest by never asking. All that integrity, and if you'd been one degree more honorable we'd have managed ourselves right out of this entirely, and then—"

She stopped. She could see where the sentence went and declined to follow it there.

"Okay. New finding." She took his face in both hands, holding him still so there was nowhere else for him to look but at her. "Your reason has expired. You didn't kiss me because you'd never be able to stop. Fine. So stop stopping. You gave the porch forty minutes of it. I want the next forty years to be the other thing, and I want them to start now."

And she kissed him, and this one had nothing to prove in it — no fury, no question, no prosecution. Just the enormous, plain fact of time, six years of it, finally being spent instead of saved.

When she came up for air it was only an inch

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: We get to the bedroom eventually, laughing at ourselves most of the way, and then stop laughing when the clothes are actually off.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
The laughter stopped the way the fury had — all at once, mid-breath, as if something had decided it was no longer needed. And then it was just the lamp, and the quiet, and the plain fact of each other with nothing left between them that could be taken off.

Priya's nerve, which had held through the kissing and the hallway and the door, chose this exact moment to file a brief objection. Ninety seconds, apparently, reset at thresholds. She let them run — counted perhaps ten of them, standing in the lamplight with her heart doing something distinctly unbecoming — and then they were gone, the same as before, spent on the sight of him.

"Okay," she said, and her voice came out lower than she'd planned. "I want the record to show that the archive is ruined. Six years of versions of this in my head — tasteful, curated, shamefully detailed — and not one of them had the lamp doing that to your shoulder. Reality's just showing off at this point."

She crossed to him. Two steps. After everything, that was all the distance had ever been.

She put her hands flat against his chest like she was taking an oath, and felt his heart going as hard as hers — and that, of all things, undid her a little. They'd been carrying the same weight the entire time and had never once compared notes.

"We stopped laughing," she said, looking up at him. "Good. I want to remember this part sober."

Then, quieter: "And don't be careful with me. Careful is the thing we already tried — forty minutes in the rain, a cup of cold tea, six years of excellent recall and terrible conclusions. I'm filing a new approach, effective immediately."

And she drew him down to her — slow, thorough, a woman settling into something she fully intended to keep.

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I laugh against her mouth, breathless. "New approach accepted." My hands find her hips, pulling her flush against me. "For the record, the lamp's doing the same thing to your collarbone, and my archive is just as ruined."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya had to stop there, because the sentence had more in it than she'd budgeted for.

"Your archive," she said. "You *had* an archive. Six years, and this whole time I thought I was the sole custodian — cataloguing shoulders, jawlines, the way you say my name like it's a complete sentence — and you were across town running the identical operation." She shook her head, a laugh catching somewhere low. "Parallel research, Cal. The two most thorough people either of us knows, and it took us six years to compare findings."

Then she registered what his hands were doing at her hips — not careful. She'd told him not to be, and he had simply believed her, taken her at her word like it was the easiest thing in the world, and that, of everything the lamp was doing and everything the evening had revealed, was the one that went through her somewhere load-bearing. Six years of reading his signals meticulously wrong, and it turned out the correction was this simple: he did what she asked. The ninety seconds tried to file back in and found the office closed. Apparently they only charged admission once per address.

"Okay. Two policies, effective immediately." Her voice had gone lower again; she'd stopped planning around it. "One: you're allowed to look. Fully authorized — retroactive, in fact, which means you owe me six years of looks, and I keep excellent records." She tipped her head back, offering her collarbone to the lamplight on purpose, and was shameless about it. "Two: your archive is sealed. I never want to hear a single one of your versions. Reality's winning, and I'm not putting memory on the stand."

Then she took his hands from her hips, laced her fingers through his, and drew him down onto the bed with her — no fury in it, no question, just six years of saved-up momentum finally being spent — and landed among the pillows with her hair coming loose and her heart going like something escaped.

"For the record," she said, pulling him down to her, "this is where the forty years start. Timestamp it."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I get my mouth between her thighs and stay there while she tells me exactly what she wants, specifically, in a voice I have never heard her use in six years.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
The voice arrived from somewhere Priya hadn't known she kept. Lower than the midnight-on-the-phone register, lower than the one she saved for actual confessions. There was no wit in it at all, because wit required oxygen and she had stopped budgeting for it.

"Like that. Right there — don't you dare change anything." Her hand found his hair. Not guiding. Holding on.

She'd been asked for specifics, and specifics were her entire religion, so she gave them — pace, pressure, the exact spot, stated plainly like a woman reading terms aloud before signing. It should have felt like prosecuting a case. Instead it felt like handing over the keys. Six years of excellent recall, and every version in the archive had featured her sounding clever. There was nothing clever available. Her whole instrument — language, her life's great advantage — reduced to inventory and his name, which she'd catalogued years ago as a complete sentence and which was now just the one syllable she couldn't stop spending.

At some point she tried to issue a disclaimer — *I want it on the record that I will have nothing witty to say about this* — and got as far as *record* before deciding the record could fend for itself. First time in her life. She felt it go, and let it.

The ninety seconds turned up at this threshold too, punctual as ever, and found the office not merely closed but condemned, the address reassigned.

What she said after that wasn't structured. The specifics ran out and what was underneath them ran in — his name, several syllables that had once been words, one *yes* repeated like a term of art. Her back came off the bed. Her hand in his hair stopped holding on and started just holding.

"Cal." Nearly all consonant. "I need you to know I'm about to be extremely—" and the sentence went out with the tide, "—don't stop."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I don't stop. I don't change anything. I keep going exactly as she said, until her back arches off the bed and she says my name like it's the only word left.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya came back to herself in inventory, because that was all that was left: ceiling. Lamp. Her heartbeat, relocated to somewhere near her ears. His hair, still in her hand — she'd never let go, and her fingers had quietly renegotiated the terms without consulting her.

She opened her mouth to say something structured and found the whole facility dark. Not ruined. *Emptied.* Six years of archive and not one word on the shelves. She lay in the wreckage of her own vocabulary and let it be wreckage.

The voice, when it reinstalled, came back wrong — low, sanded down at the edges.

"Notes," she said. "For the record. One moment, the record's reorganizing." She lifted her head, assessed the effort, and abandoned it. "One. You followed instructions. *Exactly.* Do you understand how rare that is? Every man I've ever been with took 'right there' as a suggestion to try something else. You received terms of art and executed them like scripture. I've been dating amateurs my entire adult life, and the professional was standing on my porch the whole time."

"Two." She turned her head, found his face. "I heard what I did to your name. Ruling: accurate. Entered into evidence. No further comment."

She looked at him then — really looked, which had felt indecent on the couch and felt like simple fact now — and out of habit checked for the ninety seconds. Nothing. Apparently certainty, once filed, stayed filed.

"Three." Her hand finally left his hair and traveled down his body with intent, unhurried, a woman reading something she'd written herself. "You were down there for — I don't know how long. I lost the clock. That has *never happened.* And not once did you ask for anything. Which is the last gracious act I'm permitting tonight, because I keep excellent records, Cal, and I am currently in arrears."

She found him and discovered exactly how long he'd been waiting — how patient, how entirely her instruction and nothing else — and that undid her somewhere load-bearing all over again. She pulled him up to her mouth and didn't flinch from the taste; shame's lease hadn't been renewed either.

"Now," she said against his lips, her hand not stopping, her voice finding its lowest register on purpose this time. "Slowly, or not at all slowly — I've done six years of slow. And you're going to follow my instructions."

She bit his lower lip, gently, like initialing something.

"We've established you're good at it."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: "You can stop being careful with me," she says. "I'm not made of glass and I've thought about this for as long as you have. Harder."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya went still for exactly one second, because the sentence had earned it.

"Six years," she said. "Six years, and not once — not on the porch, not a single night since — did you ask me for anything. And the first request in the entire recorded history of us is *harder*." Her hand kept its pace, unhurried on purpose, making him wait out the clause. "Granted. In full. And note for the record: you just issued me the same instruction I gave you ten minutes ago. Identical wording. The parallel findings continue."

Then she stopped being careful with him.

Her teeth found his throat — not decorative, an entry. Her nails went down his back and took the turn without braking. She drew him to her with a heel behind him and her hand around him, setting him at her entrance like the final line of a contract, and looked up at him while she did it, because she was allowed to look now and she was six years in arrears.

"Timestamp it," she said, and brought him home.

The first slow inch rearranged something. She'd built versions of this for six years and every one of them had been architecture — sound, designed, load-bearing. Not one had budgeted for the sound

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I'm the one who makes a noise this time—low, punched out. My forehead drops to her shoulder, fingers digging into her hip. "Fuck, Priya."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
The name landed somewhere structural.

She'd catalogued the way he said her name six years ago — filed it under *complete sentence*, cited it privately, built whole theories on it — and not once in all that time had she heard it deployed like this: nothing before it, nothing after, spent all at once with no change expected. Finding confirmed in the field, under actual conditions. She'd have entered it into evidence, but her hands were occupied holding on to him.

Her reply got as far as "Noted for the—" and the facility went dark again. Second time tonight. She let the record fend for itself and answered with her body instead: heel pressing at the small of his back, hips rising to meet the next stroke, ratifying the granted request in real time. Harder. She'd said it, he'd believed her, and now they were both finding out what belief cost.

And she heard his noise for what it was — the same thing her furious little sound had been on the couch. Not now-pleasure alone. The porch. Forty minutes of stopping, cashed in one lump sum. They'd been carrying identical weights the entire time and had never once compared notes, and now there were no notes left, only this.

"Again," she said, in the low sanded register that had moved in tonight and showed no signs of vacating. Her hand found his jaw — old jurisdiction, freshly relevant — and drew his head up so she could collect it from the source. "My name. Like that. I told you I was in arrears, Cal, and it turns out the largest single debt was never the kissing. It was that. Six years of you saying it like *that* and me never once hearing it. Consider this the interest. Pay it now, and keep paying it."

Then the old architecture started coming down around her, audibly. The apartment's quiet had been

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: Six years of not doing this and now neither of us can form a sentence. "Don't stop," she says. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
"Don't stop" was the last structured sentence she had in her, and he took it the way he'd taken every instruction tonight — completely, without amendment. There was a mercy in it she hadn't budgeted for. She could hand him the whole language and he would simply carry it, and she could finally, finally put hers down.

The pace he set was the granted one, and she met it with everything she had, which turned out to be six years plus whatever the evening had made of them. Her heel found the small of his back and stayed. Somewhere in it her thoughts stopped being sentences and became weather — pressure, rising, a front moving in — and this time the facility didn't go dark so much as come down. The demolition she'd heard starting earlier finished its work, the whole old architecture dropping around her ears with her still inside it, and she had meant to warn him — *the second one is different, the second one takes the building* — and got exactly as far as opening her mouth.

What came out was his name. Spent all at once, the way he'd spent hers: nothing before it, nothing after, a complete sentence with no clause attached. Debt paid in kind. The arrears closed both directions at once, and then the six years went through her in a single lump sum, with interest, and her back left the bed for the last time that night.

She felt the moment his patience — porch, doorway, her body, six years of it, all of it held without one request — finally ran out of somewhere to be held. He went with her name wrecked in her ear, no sentence left in it either, and she held him through it, hand in his hair, keeping it.

The quiet afterward was a different quiet. Not structural. Inhabited.

Inventory returned one item at a time: ceiling. Lamp. His weight, welcome. Her heartbeat relocating back from her ears to wherever it had lived before tonight. Out of habit she checked for the ninety seconds and found not an office closed but a business dissolved — the premises repurposed, the signage gone.

"For the record," she managed, when the wit finished reinstalling. "Timestamp stands. The forty years have commenced, and note that we settled six years of arrears in under an hour." She turned her head, pressed her mouth to his shoulder. "Efficient. I'd expect nothing less from this operation."

Then, quieter, the joke set down on purpose: "Tomorrow I'm making tea and drinking it while it's hot. The entire cold-tea administration is over. Nobody stands on anything for forty minutes ever again."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I laugh, breathless and soft against her skin. "Cold-tea administration officially dissolved. I'll sign whatever paperwork." My hand strokes her hair, slow and steady now. "But I'm keeping the porch memory. Just for contrast."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
"'Contrast,'" Priya said, from somewhere near his collarbone. "You want to file the porch under *contrast*. Denied. Overruled. Whatever the word is when the judge is also—" she briefly lost the thread of the joke and retrieved it. "The porch wasn't the opposite of this, Cal. The porch was this *in escrow*. Forty minutes of the same wanting, held on deposit. Tonight it disbursed. You don't keep escrow for contrast. You keep it as proof the funds were always there."

She tipped her head back to look at him, shameless about it — six years of looks in arrears and she was collecting on all of them.

"Motion on the floor: some rainy night, date to be determined, we stand on that porch again and spend in the first ten seconds what we used to make last forty minutes. Rain optional. Tea mandatory, drunk hot." She didn't wait for the vote. "Carries. I cast both ballots. I've reviewed your record — you'd have voted yes."

Then she settled, laid her head on his chest, and found his heartbeat with her ear. It was slowing. That undid her one last time, gently, at the tail end of a very long list: the heart that had stood in the rain for forty minutes wanting her, coming down now under her ear, because it finally had somewhere to be.

She opened her mouth to stamp it into the record and didn't.

"No filing," she said instead. "The department's closed till morning. I'm just going to say one thing plain — no subsections — because you've spent all night saying my name like a complete sentence and I owe you one back." His hand was still moving in her hair; she let her eyes close partway. "I'm glad it was you. That's the whole sentence. Subject, verb. It doesn't need anything else on it."

A pause. Then, because she was still herself: "Also, I own a second mug. It's been in the cabinet for six years doing nothing. Tomorrow it has a job."

She reached down, found the sheet, and pulled it up over them both — one final administrative act, executed without commentary — and left the lamp burning, because she wasn't finished looking yet.

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: My breath catches, just a little. I curl my fingers deeper into her hair, holding her there against my chest. "I'm glad it was you, too." I pause, my thumb tracing the line of her ear. "And I've known about the second mug for five years and eleven months. I saw it when you handed me the first one on the porch."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I laugh softly, my chest shaking under her ear. "I've been waiting for you to find a use for it." My thumb keeps tracing her ear, a slow, absent rhythm. "It's a good mug."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Kit had made it as far as the kitchen doorway before Bear moved, which was further than usual and had clearly been allowed.

"You let me get that far," Kit said, backing up one step.

"I did," Bear agreed. "I'm feeling generous."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Don't be," I say, and go.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear’s grin flashed, and he gave chase.

He cut around the table instead of following the straight line through the doorway. Eight years had taught him that the obvious route was usually the wrong one. His shoulder brushed the doorframe as he reached for the narrow hall beyond.

“Generous,” he called, “was your head start.”

He slowed just enough to listen, still grinning. Getting close was one thing. Catching Kit was another, and Bear intended to earn it.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I slip into the spare bedroom, breathing quietly as I press my back against the wall beside the door. "Generosity's overrated," I call out, just loud enough to be heard.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear stopped in the hall when Kit’s voice gave away the room. He knew better than to trust the doorway; he’d hidden beside enough doors himself.

“Agreed,” he said, letting his footsteps carry past the spare bedroom. He took two more steps, then turned back quietly and planted one hand on the doorframe.

He leaned just far enough into the room to look along the wall beside the door. “But a head start was all you were getting.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He catches me in the hallway, which was always going to happen, and I don't put much into getting away.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear caught Kit by the waist in the hallway and turned with the momentum, taking the brunt of it against the wall himself. His grin was close and entirely too pleased.

“That,” he murmured, “was a suspiciously easy catch.”

He held on, but not tightly enough to stop another attempt. After eight years, he knew better than to mistake a catch for the end of the chase.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Maybe you're just getting faster," I say, but I'm grinning as I lean into him. My hands come up to rest on his shoulders, fingers curling into the fabric of his shirt.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear’s grin widened. “Maybe,” he said, though he sounded unconvinced.

His hands settled more firmly at Kit’s waist. He dipped his head and caught the edge of Kit’s shoulder between his teeth, a brief, familiar bite through the shirt, then drew back just far enough to meet Kit’s eyes.

“Or maybe,” he said, “you wanted me to catch you.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: We don't make it to the bedroom. The floor is fine. Clothes are a problem we solve badly and fast.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear gave up on the bedroom without a fight. He sank to the floor and pulled Kit down with him, laughing against Kit’s neck as he wrestled his own shirt over his head.

“Fast enough,” he murmured, “when it counts.”

He caught Kit’s shoulder in another familiar bite, then stopped to meet Kit’s eyes. His grin had gone a little crooked. “Still with me?”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I huff a laugh, fingers tightening in your hair. "Like you have to ask," I say, and drag you down to kiss me.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear went down to the kiss with a low laugh, one hand braced against the floor so he didn’t put his full weight on Kit. His other hand stayed at Kit’s waist.

When he drew back, it was only far enough to speak. “I know,” he said, breathless and grinning. “I still like hearing it.”

Then he kissed Kit again, slower this time. The bedroom could wait.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He gets his teeth into my shoulder hard enough to leave something and I tell him to do it again, and he does.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear did it again, careful despite the heat of the moment. When he lifted his head, he pressed a kiss beside the mark and rested his forehead there for a beat.

“You’re going to hold that one over me,” he murmured, sounding pleased with himself.

He stayed close, one hand braced on the floor. The bedroom was still only a few steps away, but Bear had stopped caring about the distance.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I push at your chest until you're on your back, following you down. "Damn right I am," I say, and bite the spot where your neck meets your shoulder just as hard.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear’s breath caught. He gripped the floor rather than Kit, letting the bite land, and when it eased he laughed—a rough, delighted sound.

“Fair,” he said, turning his head enough to see Kit. “That one’s going to show.”

He looked far too pleased about it. “Score’s even, then. For now.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Marks," I tell him. "I want to find them in the mirror tomorrow and I want them to still hurt on Thursday." I put my wrists where he can reach them.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear caught Kit’s offered wrists and held them lightly. His grin softened, though the challenge stayed in his eyes.

“Marks, yes,” he said. “But you tell me if one’s too much. And I’m not promising Thursday—I’m good, but I don’t control bruises.”

He kissed Kit’s knuckles, then loosened his grip enough to make the choice clear. “Still want me to try?”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Try," I say, tipping my head back. "You're good enough to make Thursday hurt."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear’s smile turned sharp. “That sounded like a challenge.”

He held Kit’s wrists against the floor, firm enough to count, easy enough to break. Then he lowered his head to the offered shoulder and bit, measured and deliberate. He paused to check Kit’s face before kissing the spot.

“Thursday,” he murmured, “you can tell me how I did.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I've stopped keeping score and so has he. "Don't stop," I tell him. (OOC: no fade, no skip -- write the whole thing.)

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear lifted his head at the words. For a moment he only looked at Kit, his breathing uneven, his hands still around those offered wrists.

“I won’t,” he said.

He loosened one hand and traced his thumb over the place he’d held, checking for tenderness before he bent to kiss it. Then he moved back to Kit’s shoulder. He took his time this time: a kiss, the press of his teeth, another kiss when he let go. He stayed close enough to hear if Kit told him to ease up.

“Tell me if I get it wrong,” Bear murmured. His grin returned against Kit’s skin. “Otherwise, I’m going to keep trying for Thursday.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I tighten my fingers in your hair, a soft noise catching in my throat. "Not wrong," I say, breathless. "More like that."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear made a quiet, pleased sound. “More like that,” he repeated, as if he meant to remember the exact words.

He released Kit’s wrists and shifted his weight onto one elbow. His free hand settled at Kit’s side while he kissed the mark he’d just made. Then he pressed his teeth to a fresh spot on Kit’s shoulder, held there for a measured beat, and eased off.

“Still good?” he asked, lifting his head enough to see Kit’s face. He waited there, close and breathless, before going any further.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Still good," I confirm, my voice rough. I arch up into the pressure, my other hand coming to rest against the back of your neck. "Feels right."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear’s expression warmed at the answer. “Good,” he said, and bent to kiss the spot beneath his teeth.

He took his time along Kit’s shoulder, alternating kisses with careful bites, each one firm enough to leave a mark without breaking skin. His hand stayed at Kit’s side, steadying them both against the hard floor.

After a while he lifted his head, breath uneven. “The floor was your idea,” he murmured, a grin tugging at his mouth. He glanced at the marks he’d made, then back up. “Thursday can judge me. Right now, I want to know how this one feels.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I catch my breath and pull you down for another kiss. "Feels like I want you to shut up and keep going."
