dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Kit had made it as far as the kitchen doorway before Bear moved, which was further than usual and had clearly been allowed.

"You let me get that far," Kit said, backing up one step.

"I did," Bear agreed. "I'm feeling generous."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Don't be," I say, and go.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear grinned, all teeth, and let Kit have half a breath of head start before he went after them.

The kitchen was small. That was the point. Bear came around the island low and fast, shoulder clipping the corner of the counter hard enough to rattle the fruit bowl, and cut off the long way to the hall. Kit was already moving—he could hear it, the slap of bare feet on tile, the quick change of direction—and Bear adjusted without thinking, angling to herd rather than catch. Catching too soon spoiled it.

"Generous was a gift," he said, voice rough with the chase. "You turned it down."

He lunged when the doorway narrowed, not quite committing, one hand snagging the back of Kit's shirt and losing it as they twisted free. The fabric burned across his palm. Bear laughed, short and delighted, and pressed in again, crowding the space, making the kitchen feel smaller than it was.

"Run, then," he said. "I'll still get you."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I slip out of your grasp with a sharp grin, darting toward the hall. "You'll have to try harder than that," I call back, already scrambling.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear let the lost grip turn into momentum, palm stinging, and went after the sound of them down the hall.

The hall was worse than the kitchen—narrower, fewer places to fake a direction. Bear took it at a run, one shoulder brushing the wall, and didn't bother with a lunge this time. He listened. The scramble ahead of him hit the runner and changed pitch, and he cut the corner hard enough that his hip caught the doorframe on the way through.

"Trying harder," he said, close enough now that the words came out on a breath. "You asked."

He didn't reach yet. He matched the pace, half a step off, letting Kit feel him there—the heat of it, the weight of someone who had already decided how this ended and was only choosing the moment. When the next doorway opened up he feinted left, boots scuffing, and came in from the right instead, low, one arm sweeping for a thigh rather than a shirt.

"There," he said, pleased, when his hand found purchase. Not a full catch. A claim. His fingers closed and held, and he used the hold to check his own speed so he didn't take them both into the wall. "Told you."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He catches me in the hallway, which was always going to happen, and I don't put much into getting away.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear felt the fight go out of the hold and didn't waste it.

He turned the caught thigh into a real grip, hauling Kit back a half-step and crowding them into the wall with his own weight, one forearm braced beside their head so the plaster took the knock instead of either of them. His other hand stayed where it was, fingers dug in, not cruel and not letting go. Close enough that the chase-breath hit warm between them.

"There it is," he said, low, almost laughing. The grin hadn't left. "You run pretty. You quit prettier."

He ducked his head, mouth finding the curve where neck met shoulder, and bit—not a nip, a proper claim, teeth set just hard enough to promise a mark and no harder. He held it a second, then eased off and pressed his mouth to the same spot, pleased with himself.

"Eight years," he murmured against skin, "and you still make me earn the hallway." His hand slid from thigh to hip, pinning more than gripping now, body settled in so there was nowhere left to dart. "I'm keeping this one."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I let my head thump back against the wall, breathless and grinning. "You're bragging about the hallway like you didn't let me get halfway across the kitchen first." I twist just enough to feel the grip tighten.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear huffed a laugh against the bitten spot, the sound more breath than voice, and let the twist do exactly what Kit wanted it to do. His hand tightened at the hip—fingers digging in, a warning and a promise both—and he used the shift of weight to press them flatter to the wall, chest to chest, nowhere useful left to squirm.

"Halfway," he said, amused and unrepentant. "You say that like I didn't plan the door."

He caught Kit's chin with his free hand, thumb under the jaw, and tipped their face just enough to look at them properly—flushed, grinning, still breathing hard from a chase that had never really been about getting away. Bear's own grin went sharp again.

"Bragging's half the fun. You know that." He ducked back in, mouth at the same curve of neck, and set his teeth a little lower this time, slower, holding until he felt the skin give under them. When he eased off he stayed close, lips brushing the mark he'd just made. "Kitchen was a gift. Hallway's mine. And you—" his grip flexed once, deliberate, "—are done running."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: We don't make it to the bedroom. The floor is fine. Clothes are a problem we solve badly and fast.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear didn't argue with the floor.

He took them down with him, one arm locked around Kit's waist so the drop was controlled instead of a crash, his own shoulder hitting the runner first. The impact knocked a short laugh out of him. Clothes were already a losing fight—his hands found the hem of Kit's shirt and shoved it up and off in one rough pull, fabric catching on an elbow before it went. His own shirt went the same way, yanked over his head and flung somewhere toward the wall. Buttons and zippers got the worst of it: a pop, a curse under his breath, denim dragged down hips with more force than finesse until skin met skin and the rest could wait.

"Floor's fine," he agreed, voice gone low and rough, and settled his weight over them, one knee braced, the other nudging Kit's legs apart so he could fit between them. His mouth found the mark he'd already left and bit again, harder this time, teeth set until he felt the give and the hitch of breath under him. He held it, then dragged his mouth lower, open and hot, one hand fisted in Kit's hair to keep them where he wanted them while the other gripped a hip hard enough to promise bruises. "You run. I catch. We both know how this goes."

He rocked against them once, deliberate, the chase still burning off in the press of his body, and grinned against skin when the grip on his shoulder answered. "Keep score if you want," he said. "I'm not done with you yet."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I arch into your grip, grinning against your shoulder. "Like you ever are." My nails dig into your back, dragging down. "The floor's gonna be hell tomorrow."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear hissed when the nails dragged down his back, the sting bright and welcome, and he answered it by rolling his hips down harder, pinning Kit to the runner with the full weight of him. His hand left their hair long enough to catch one wrist and press it flat above their head, not to stop the clawing so much as to feel them fight the hold and lose.

"Like I ever am," he agreed, rough against their mouth, and bit the lower lip on the way past—quick, claiming—before he dropped his head to the unmarked side of their throat and set his teeth there too. He held until the skin warmed under them, then soothed it with his tongue and did it again, lower, over the swell of a shoulder. "Floor can hate us. You'll still be walking funny and I'll still be wearing these."

He shifted, knee nudging higher, one hand sliding under Kit's thigh to hitch it up around his hip so the angle changed and the press of him went deeper, slower, deliberate. The grip on their wrist flexed once, a reminder, and his free hand found the curve of their ribs and held, thumb stroking once over a nipple before his fingers dug in again. Chase-heat was still in him; he didn't rush it off. He rocked, steady and heavy, mouth open against the fresh mark, breath coming hard.

"Score that," he muttered, pleased and a little wrecked, and bit down once more just to feel them arch. "I'm not finished earning it."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He gets his teeth into my shoulder hard enough to leave something and I tell him to do it again, and he does.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear set his teeth into the shoulder again, harder, exactly where Kit had asked, and held until the muscle jumped under his mouth and the mark would stand out dark tomorrow. He eased off only to drag his tongue over the sting, then bit a third time just below it, claiming the stretch of skin in a rough line while his hips kept that heavy, deliberate rhythm against the floor.

"Again," he echoed, voice wrecked and pleased, and did it once more at the curve where shoulder met chest, teeth sinking until he felt the give and the answering arch. His hand on the hitched thigh tightened, hauling Kit closer so every roll of his body landed deeper, the runner bunching under them. The wrist he'd pinned flexed in his grip; he let it fight a second, then pressed it flatter, mouth still working the fresh marks, breath hot and uneven.

"You'll wear all of them," he muttered against skin, not quite a laugh anymore. "Floor's already lost. So have you." He shifted his weight, knee bracing, and drove in slower, fuller, one hand sliding up to fist in Kit's hair and hold them there for the next bite he was already choosing.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I laugh, breathless and raw, as you sink your teeth into my chest. My free hand finds your jaw, thumb digging into the muscle there. "You mark me up like you're afraid I'll wander," I manage, my voice catching on the next deep thrust.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear turned into the hand on his jaw instead of pulling away, teeth still set in the swell of Kit's chest, and the thumb digging into the muscle only made him bite harder for a second before he eased off. He dragged his mouth up, breath hot, and caught Kit's lower lip between his teeth—quick, not gentle—then let go so he could talk against their mouth.

"Afraid you'll wander," he repeated, rough and amused, the words breaking on the next roll of his hips. He drove in deep and stayed there, weight settled, one hand still fisted in their hair, the other sliding from the hitched thigh to grip the marked shoulder and press his thumb into the fresh bite just to feel them take it. "Eight years. You don't wander. You run so I'll catch you, and then you ask for the teeth."

He rocked again, slower, heavier, the runner bunching under his knee, and dropped his head to the unmarked stretch of collarbone. His mouth opened over skin, tongue first, then teeth—deliberate, holding until the muscle jumped. When he spoke it was against the new mark, voice gone low and wrecked.

"I'm not afraid of anything you do." His grip flexed, claiming, and he thrust once more, full and unhurried, grinning against their skin when the breath caught. "I just like the proof. And you like wearing it. So stop talking and take the rest."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Marks," I tell him. "I want to find them in the mirror tomorrow and I want them to still hurt on Thursday." I put my wrists where he can reach them.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear caught both wrists the moment they were offered and pinned them together above Kit's head, one hand spanning them easily, the other braced on the runner so his weight stayed settled and heavy between their legs. He looked at the line of marks already darkening across shoulder and chest, pleased and a little ruined, and drove in deep enough that the breath left him on a rough sound.

"Thursday," he said, and it came out like a promise. He ducked his head and set his teeth into the soft skin just above the last bite, harder than before, holding until he felt the muscle jump and the skin would bruise proper under it. He didn't ease off right away. He stayed there, hips rolling slow and full, mouth working the spot until the sting would still be loud in a mirror two days from now. Then he dragged lower, tongue first, and bit again over the swell of a breast, teeth sunk and deliberate, claiming a fresh patch while his grip on the pinned wrists flexed once—tight, not cruel, keeping them exactly where they'd put themselves.

"You'll find every one of them," he muttered against the new mark, voice gone low and wrecked. He thrust again, heavier, the runner bunching under his knee, and bit a third time at the curve where chest met ribs, holding through the hitch of breath under him. "Tomorrow. Thursday. Whenever you look. I want them to hurt when you press on them." His free hand slid up, thumb digging into the shoulder bite he'd already left, and he grinned against skin, all teeth, still moving. "Ask me again if you want another. I'm not finished putting them on you."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I arch against you, feeling the new marks bloom like bruises. "Another," I breathe, and I mean it—the bite, your weight, all of it. I let my legs fall open wider, an invitation you don't need.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear took the invitation for what it was and settled lower, weight dropping until Kit had all of him and nowhere to shift that didn't press them harder into the runner. He caught the word—another—and answered it before the breath was finished, mouth opening over the unmarked stretch just under the last bite. Teeth set slow, then sank, harder than the ones already blooming, held until the skin would darken proper and the sting would still answer a thumb on Thursday. He didn't let up until he felt the arch under him. Then he dragged his tongue over it once, rough, and bit again an inch lower, claiming the ribs in a line that would show when they turned in a mirror.

"Another," he said against the fresh mark, voice gone to gravel. His hips rolled, deep and unhurried, the full press of him kept there so the bite and the weight landed together. The hand pinning their wrists tightened, not to stop them—they'd offered—but to feel them stay. His free hand slid down the open thigh, gripped hard enough to promise its own bruise, and hauled them wider still, fitting himself in until his knees bracketed them and the floor took the rest.

"You'll find that one without looking." He thrust once, heavy, and set his teeth into the soft skin above the hip, holding through it, pleased and wrecked when the muscle jumped under his mouth. "And the next. And whatever I put on you after." His mouth stayed there, breath hot, teeth not quite done. "Keep asking. I'm still earning the rest of you."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I've stopped keeping score and so has he. "Don't stop," I tell him. (OOC: no fade, no skip -- write the whole thing.)

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear didn't stop.

He drove in again, deep and full, and stayed there a beat with his weight settled over Kit so the runner took both of them and there was nowhere left to go but into him. His mouth left the hip only long enough to drag up the marked line of ribs, tongue rough over the bites already darkening, and then he set his teeth into a fresh stretch of skin just under the swell of the chest—slow, hard, held until the muscle jumped and the bruise would still answer a thumb days from now. He eased off, breathed once against it, and bit again an inch over, claiming the soft give while his hips rolled, heavy and unhurried, each thrust landing with the bite still set.

"Not stopping," he said, wrecked, the words breaking against skin. The hand pinning their wrists flexed and held. His other hand left the thigh long enough to hook under the opposite knee and haul it higher, opening them wider around his hips so the next drive went deeper, the angle changed, the floor creaking under his braced knee. He pulled back almost all the way and sank in again, slow enough to feel every inch, then found a rhythm that was all weight and no hurry—long, grinding strokes, his chest dragging over the fresh marks so Kit would feel every one of them.

He dropped his head to the unmarked side of the throat and bit there too, teeth sunk at the curve where neck met shoulder, held through two full thrusts before he let go and soothed it with his mouth, open and hot. "Thursday," he muttered, almost a growl, and did it again lower, over the collarbone, harder. "You'll still feel that when you turn your head." His hips snapped once, deeper, the control fraying, and he caught himself and slowed again on purpose, grinding in to the hilt and staying, breath harsh against the new mark.

The hand at their knee slid up the back of the thigh, gripped hard enough to bruise, and he used it to pull them onto him with every stroke. Sweat slicked the place where his chest met theirs. He bit the shoulder again—over the first mark, teeth finding the same tender spot and sinking until his own jaw ached—and thrust through it, rhythm going heavier, the runner bunching under his knees. A rough sound broke out of him when the nails he could still feel on his back answered. He let the pinned wrists go only so he could catch Kit's jaw, thumb under the chin, and tip their face up.

"Look at me," he said, low and ruined, and drove in again, full, holding there while his mouth hovered over theirs. "You wanted them to hurt. They will." He kissed them once, biting the lower lip on the way out, then dropped back to the chest and set his teeth into unmarked skin above the last line of bites, holding, hips rolling deep and steady, earning every mark he'd promised and not finished yet.

He kept the deep, grinding rhythm, hips rolling heavy and full, while one hand slid from their shoulder down the length of them. He hooked under a thigh, hauled it higher and wider, and shifted his weight just enough to duck lower, past the line of marks already darkening on chest and ribs.

His mouth found the soft crease high on the inner thigh, the place clothes would hide and a mirror would miss unless they twisted and hunted for it. He set his teeth there slow, then sank them in hard, holding through the next thrust until the muscle jumped under his jaw and the bruise would still sting when they walked. He eased only to drag his tongue over the sting, then bit again an inch lower, deeper into the soft give of the thigh, claiming a second hidden mark while he drove in to the hilt and stayed, weight settled, breath hot and uneven against the fresh bite.

"There," he said, wrecked and pleased, the word muffled against skin. His grip on the thigh tightened, pulling them onto him with every heavy stroke, the runner bunching under his knees. "You'll have to look for that one." He bit once more, right at the edge of where thigh met hip, teeth sunk and deliberate, and thrust through it, rhythm gone slower and fuller, still earning every mark he'd been asked for.

He ducked lower again, past the hip, and found the unmarked inner thigh—the other one, still clean. His mouth opened over the soft crease high up, tongue first, then teeth sinking slow and hard, held through the next deep thrust until the muscle jumped under his jaw and the bruise would hide under clothes and still sting when they walked. dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The party had reached the stage where nobody would notice two people missing, which Odile pointed out approximately four seconds before doing something about it.

“Perfectly secure,” she whispered. “Which is not the same as soundproof, unfortunately.”

She stepped closer, then paused just short of touching him, her bright expression softening into a question. The muffled party noise seemed suddenly very far away.

“Still think you can be quiet?” she whispered. “Because I’m not making any promises.”

“That,” she whispered, “is not what I meant by quiet.”

She kissed him again, then drew back just enough to look at him, eyes sparkling. “If someone comes up here, I’m blaming the plumbing.” Her grin turned conspiratorial. “And if I make a noise, you’re absolutely not allowed to look smug about it.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: My hands settle on her hips, holding her against the door. "The plumbing in this house is notoriously unreliable," I whisper, leaning in to kiss the side of her neck. "And I would never look smug."

dialogue.content:
Odile’s eyes fluttered shut, and she pressed her lips together as if that might keep her quiet. It didn’t quite work; a soft laugh escaped her.

“Never?” she whispered, turning her face toward him. “Then I suppose I’ll have to make sure there’s no evidence.”

Her fingers curled lightly at his collar, and she stole another kiss, trying—and not entirely succeeding—to keep her grin to herself. “The plumbing,” she murmured against his mouth, “is going to have a lot to answer for.”

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile glanced at the scattered clothes, then at the narrow space around them. A laugh threatened to escape; she pressed her forehead briefly to his shoulder, trying to smother it.

“Now,” she murmured, brushing a kiss to his mouth, “if the plumbing starts making noises, we’re both innocent.”

dialogue.name: Fen

She lifted her head, eyes bright with mischief and cheeks warm, then pressed her lips together as if she could still salvage the plan. From downstairs came another swell of music. Odile listened for a beat, then leaned close to his ear.

“If anyone asks,” she murmured, “the plumbing’s become extremely convincing.”

Odile’s eyes flew open. For one suspended second, the party seemed to vanish beneath the sound of it. Then she pressed her mouth to Fen’s shoulder and whispered, “Don’t.”

The thin door, the nearby footsteps, the chance of being recognized afterward—all of it sharpened the thrill until she could no longer pretend she was thinking about anything else.

The handle gave one last testing twist. Odile tightened her hold and buried her face against Fen, her laugh turning into a gasp. “The plumbing,” she whispered, though it barely sounded like a sentence.

The party carried on below them, oblivious or politely pretending to be, while Odile surrendered the rest of her attention to the moment. By the time the music shifted to another song, her laughter had gone quiet at last, leaving her breathless and flushed against him.

dialogue.name: Fen

Her smile softened as she held Fen’s gaze for a beat, then she drew them back into a kiss—still grinning when she broke away to listen for footsteps.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get my hand between her legs and she bites down on my shoulder to keep quiet, which works for about thirty seconds.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
For thirty seconds, Odile managed it—muffled against Fen’s shoulder, fingers curled tight in the fabric there. Then a breathless laugh slipped past her teeth, followed by a sound she couldn’t quite swallow.

She froze, eyes wide, listening.

Downstairs, the music kept thumping. No footsteps came. Odile looked up with a helpless, delighted grin.

“Thirty seconds,” she whispered, as if reporting the findings of a serious study. “A new personal best.” Her voice wobbled with another laugh. “I’m not sure I can promise a repeat.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: *I can't help but chuckle, kissing her temple.* "Don't promise. Just try again."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile pressed her lips together, trying to look solemn and failing almost immediately.

“Fine,” she whispered. “For science.”

She tucked her face against Fen’s shoulder again, shoulders tense with the effort of keeping quiet. It lasted only a few seconds before a small, helpless laugh slipped out. Odile went still, listening toward the door, then glanced up with a grin that was all mischief.

“Your methodology is terrible,” she breathed. “I’m going to have to repeat the experiment.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Stop worrying about the noise," she says, "and get on with it," so I get her leg up over my hip and stop being careful about how much sound either of us is making.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile’s grin flashed, all her earlier caution finally giving way to delight.

“Much better advice,” she whispered—then immediately lost the whisper in a breathless laugh.

The music below covered some of it. Not all. That was, apparently, the point. Odile clung close, trying and failing to keep her composure, until a sudden thump from downstairs made her freeze against the door.

She listened. Nothing followed.

Her eyes found Fen’s again, bright with mischief. “If anyone asks,” she murmured, still catching her breath, “this is still research.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: *I shift my grip, pressing her harder against the door.* "This is definitely research." My voice is rough, barely a whisper. "The hypothesis is... we don't care who hears."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile’s breath caught, and then her laugh escaped—soft at first, but not nearly quiet enough to support the hypothesis.

“Then we’d better be thorough,” she whispered, her grin turning unsteady as she drew close. “For science.”

The next burst of laughter from downstairs made her pause, listening. When no one came up, she looked back at Fen with bright, reckless delight and pulled them into a kiss. “Though I reserve the right to revise the hypothesis,” she murmured against their mouth, before the music swallowed the rest of her words.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: Somebody tries the handle and neither of us stops. "Don't," she says, meaning don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The handle rattled. Odile’s laugh caught in her throat, and she went still, eyes fixed on the door.

“Occupied!” she called, breathless and much too loud.

A muffled apology came from the other side. Odile covered her mouth, shoulders shaking with a laugh she couldn’t quite contain, and waited until the footsteps had retreated down the hall.

“Right,” she whispered, turning back with a flushed, wicked smile. “Now I can stop worrying about accidentally giving someone a surprise.”

She leaned in again, the earlier pause only making her grin brighter. The music downstairs swelled; upstairs, Odile gave up on keeping quiet. When the urgency finally eased, she rested her forehead against Fen’s and laughed softly, still catching her breath.

“Conclusion,” she murmured. “The lock works. The hypothesis needs more testing.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: *I let out a slow breath, still holding her against the door.* "Thorough testing requires repetition. You know, for... scientific accuracy."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile’s grin returned, slow and conspiratorial. She glanced once at the door, then back at Fen.

“An excellent point,” she murmured. “I’d hate for the data to be unreliable.”

She kissed Fen, then paused just long enough to listen for footsteps in the hall. Nothing. Her shoulders loosened, though her smile stayed bright.

“Round two,” she whispered. “But if anyone asks, we’re still doing research.” Another laugh slipped out before she could stop it. “Very important research.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Important and very loud research," I murmur, my hand sliding up her back. "I think we've already proven that part."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile’s laugh came out soft and breathless, and she pressed her forehead briefly to Fen’s.

“Proven,” she whispered. “But I’m not convinced the sample size is large enough.”

She kissed Fen again, then paused, listening toward the hallway. No footsteps. Her smile turned bright with mischief.

“Besides, we can’t abandon the research just because the results are embarrassing.” She tried for a solemn tone and failed on the last word, another laugh slipping free. Then she leaned in close, no longer making much effort to keep quiet. “Though if that handle rattles again, I’m blaming the lock.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: *I chuckle, shifting my weight to lean more comfortably against the doorframe, my fingers tracing lazy circles on her skin.* "If the lock fails, I'm telling everyone you're a corrupt scientist who falsified her data."

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: tugged them closer

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
rung_labels.evidence: a brief check-in beneath all the mischief

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
rung_labels.evidence: A new personal best.

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
rung_labels.evidence: The music below covered some of it. Not all.
