dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The party had reached the stage where nobody would notice two people missing, which Odile pointed out approximately four seconds before doing something about it.

"The bathroom upstairs has a lock," she said, into Fen's ear, over the music.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Does it work?" I ask, already moving toward the stairs.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
"I have no idea," Odile said cheerfully, and followed.

She caught up with Fen on the third step, which was not difficult since she took the stairs two at a time and nearly missed the fourth, grabbing the banister with one hand and Fen's belt loop with the other. Somewhere below, someone had put on a song that everyone apparently knew the words to, and a ragged chorus rose up the stairwell after them like a send-off.

"That's our cover," she whispered, much louder than a whisper had any right to be. "Nobody's going to hear anything over *that*."

The upstairs hallway was dim and smelled of someone's candle, fig or cedar or both, and lined with framed photos of their friends' wedding. Odile paused in front of one, the couple mid-laugh under a canopy of fairy lights, and pressed a hand to her mouth to smother a snort.

"Oh, we are terrible people," she said, delighted. "Look at them. They trusted us with their guest bathroom."

The bathroom door was at the end of the hall, half-open, a sliver of warm light spilling out across the floorboards. Odile got there first, slipped inside, and turned to face Fen with her back against the sink. There were little decorative soaps shaped like seashells in a dish beside her elbow. She looked at them, then at Fen, and her shoulders started to shake.

"Seashells," she managed. "They have *seashells*."

She reached past Fen to the door handle, fingers finding the small brass lock, and pushed it. It turned with a click that felt much more significant than it probably was. Then she jiggled the handle experimentally. It held.

"Works," she reported, and her voice dropped half an octave somewhere in the middle of the word, the laughter still in it but something warmer underneath. She hooked two fingers into the front of Fen's shirt and drew them in close, until there was no room left between them and the counter pressed into the small of her back.

"Right. New rule." Her breath was warm and smelled faintly of the wine she'd been nursing all evening. "Whoever makes the first noise loses."

Downstairs, the chorus hit its big note. Odile tipped her head back against the mirror, eyes bright, grinning like she'd already decided she was going to lose and didn't mind in the slightest.

"Loses what, you ask?" She pulled Fen's mouth down to hers before any answer could come, and against their lips she murmured, "Haven't decided yet."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I lean into the kiss, smiling against her mouth before pulling back just enough to murmur, "I can think of a few forfeits." My hand slides up her side, brushing against one of those ridiculous soaps and sending it clattering into the sink.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The seashell hit the porcelain with a sound like a very small gunshot, skittered twice around the basin, and came to rest against the drain.

Odile went absolutely still.

For one heroic second she held it together, lips pressed shut, eyes wide, staring at Fen with the look of someone trying not to sneeze in church. Then her whole body betrayed her. The laugh escaped as a strangled wheeze through her nose, and she dropped her forehead against Fen's collarbone, shoulders shaking helplessly.

"That doesn't count," she hissed into their shirt. "That was the *soap*. The soap made the noise. I'm filing an appeal."

She lifted her head, cheeks flushed and eyes wet at the corners, and fished the shell out of the sink with two fingers. She set it back in its dish with exaggerated care, nudging it until it lined up with the others, then patted it once.

"There. Crime scene restored. Nobody will ever know."

Her hands found their way back to Fen, one flat against their chest, the other sliding around to the back of their neck, fingertips tracing the hairline there in a slow, deliberate line. The laughter hadn't left her face, but it had gone quieter, pooling somewhere behind her eyes.

"A few forfeits," she repeated, low, testing the words like she was tasting them. "That's very ominous of you. I like it."

She shifted her weight and boosted herself up onto the edge of the counter, knocking a hand towel off its ring in the process. She ignored it entirely. Seated, she was almost level with Fen, and she used the new height to pull them in between her knees, hooking one ankle loosely behind their leg to keep them there.

"Tell me one," she murmured, lips brushing the corner of Fen's jaw, the hinge of it, just below their ear. "Just one. So I know what I'm up against."

Downstairs, the song ended. In the sudden gap before the next one started, the whole house seemed to go quiet: a murmur of voices, a clink of glasses, someone's laugh floating up the stairwell with perfect, horrible clarity.

Odile froze again, mouth still against Fen's neck. Then she started to grin. Fen could feel it against their skin.

"Oh no," she breathed, barely a whisper this time, which somehow made it worse. "Oh no, the cover's gone."

The next song kicked in, something slower, with a bassline that thudded faintly through the floorboards. Odile exhaled in relief, then immediately looked a little disappointed about it.

"Shame," she said, and kissed Fen properly this time, slow and unhurried. Her fingers tightened at the back of their neck, and a small sound escaped her, soft and involuntary, somewhere at the back of her throat.

She pulled back half an inch. She blinked.

"...Okay, that one counts," she admitted, breathless and not remotely sorry. "Go on, then. What's my forfeit?"

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get the door shut and her against it, and downstairs somebody turns the music up, which helps.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile went with it gladly, sliding off the counter and letting herself be turned, until the cool painted wood met her shoulder blades with a soft *thunk*. The door rattled in its frame. The little brass lock held.

"Very decisive," she whispered approvingly, and then the music swelled up through the floor, bass and all, loud enough that someone downstairs whooped. Odile's head tipped back against the door and she laughed outright, no attempt to hide it this time. "Oh, bless them. Bless whoever did that. I'm buying them a drink."

Her hands were already busy, tugging Fen's shirt free of their waistband, fingertips slipping underneath to find warm skin at the small of their back. She pulled them flush against her, and the laugh faded into something slower and more breathless. Her eyes were very dark in the warm bathroom light.

"You still haven't told me the forfeit," she murmured against Fen's mouth. "I think you're making it up as you go."

She kissed them before any answer could come, the kind of kiss that had stopped being a game some time ago, and when she broke off it was only to drag in a breath and press her mouth to the side of Fen's throat. She hooked her fingers through their belt loops and held on.

A second sound slipped out of her, louder than the first, and Odile clapped her own hand over her mouth. Her eyes were wide with scandalised delight above her fingers.

"Two," she mumbled into her palm. "I'm down *two*. This is a massacre."

She lowered her hand, still grinning, and slid it up to cup Fen's jaw. Her thumb traced their lower lip. The music thudded on, and somewhere below, glasses clinked in a toast neither of them would ever hear the reason for.

Then, faintly, right on the other side of the wood behind her head, the floorboards in the hallway creaked.

Odile's grin froze in place. She didn't move a muscle, barely breathed, her hand stilled on Fen's face. Footsteps paused just outside the door. The handle turned a quarter-inch and stopped against the lock.

"*Occupied!*" Odile called out, in a bright, perfectly normal, wildly unconvincing voice.

A pause. A muffled "oh, sorry!" and the footsteps retreated back down the hall toward the stairs.

Odile held it together for exactly as long as it took them to fade. Then she buried her face in Fen's shoulder and shook with silent, helpless laughter, clutching fistfuls of their shirt.

"That was *Priya*," she wheezed. "She's going to know. She's absolutely going to know." She lifted her head, flushed and bright-eyed and entirely unrepentant, and pulled Fen right back in by the collar. "Which means we'd better make it worth it."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I can feel your pulse hammering against my lips. "Worth it, huh?" My voice is low, rough. I slide a hand up her thigh, bunching her dress. "Priya's smart. She's probably already texting someone 'guess who's getting laid in the bathroom.'"

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's breath caught as Fen's hand moved up her thigh. The hem of her dress rode up with it, and the cool air of the bathroom met bare skin. Her fingers tightened in Fen's collar.

"Priya," she said, in a voice that had gone noticeably wobbly, "is *absolutely* texting someone. She's probably made a group chat. There's probably a *name*."

As if summoned, something buzzed against Fen's hip.

Odile stared at them. Then she looked down at the pocket of her own dress, where her phone was vibrating insistently through the fabric, once, twice, a third time.

"No," she whispered. "No, no, no."

She didn't take it out. She didn't dare. She pressed her forehead to Fen's and laughed so hard and so silently that her whole body shook against them, a hand braced flat on the door behind her to keep herself upright.

"I'm not looking," she managed. "I refuse to look. If I look, it becomes real." The phone buzzed a fourth time. Odile made a small, strangled, anguished noise. "That's three. That one counts. I'm losing *so badly*."

She fished the phone out without looking at the screen, reached blindly sideways, and dropped it face-down into the folded hand towels on the shelf, where it buzzed on, muffled and indignant. Then she turned back to Fen, and the laughter was still in her face, but her eyes had gone dark and steady and very, very focused.

"There," she breathed. "Now there's no one in the world but you."

She caught Fen's wrist where it rested on her thigh. She didn't stop them. She held it there, pressing their palm flat against her skin, and let them feel how fast her heart was going everywhere.

"You've been very smug about these forfeits," she murmured, lips grazing theirs with every word. "And I've been very noisy. So here's what I think happens." She tipped her chin up and kissed them, slow and deep, and pulled back just far enough to finish the thought. "I stop keeping score. You stop being careful. And whatever Priya's telling people..."

She reached down and found Fen's belt buckle, and the grin that broke across her face was pure, reckless mischief.

"...we make sure she's *underselling* it."

Downstairs, somebody turned the music up again. Odile laughed, bright and helpless and not remotely quiet, and pulled Fen in.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: There isn't room to do this properly and we don't let that stop us. Enough clothes come off to be a problem if anyone knocks.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
It turned out that the guest bathroom had been designed by someone who had never once considered this particular use case.

Odile's elbow found the towel rail first. Then the back of her head found the light switch, and for three seconds they were in total darkness, which she found so funny that she had to stop entirely and lean her whole weight on Fen, wheezing, while she groped along the wall behind her.

"Hang on. Hang on, I've got it, I've..." The light flickered back on. She blinked up at Fen, hair mussed, dress slipping off one shoulder, the strap hanging loose at her elbow. "Right. Where were we. Oh, *yes*."

Her dress was mostly around her waist now, and Fen's shirt was somewhere on the floor, possibly in the bathtub. Odile had lost track of it the moment it stopped being between them. She had one hand braced on the edge of the sink and the other clutching at Fen's shoulder, and the mirror behind her had fogged at the edges where her back kept pressing into it.

The seashell soaps rattled in their dish with every movement. Odile did not even glance at them. She was past caring about the soaps.

She had also completely stopped keeping score.

She tried, at first, to be quiet. It lasted about as long as her dignity had. She bit her lip, then the heel of her own hand, then Fen's shoulder, and none of it worked. Every time she thought she had it under control, Fen did something that undid it, and a sound escaped her that was nowhere near subtle, low and helpless and absolutely audible over whatever song was playing downstairs.

"You're," she gasped, "doing that on *purpose*."

The shampoo bottle went next. It toppled off the edge of the bath with a hollow plastic *thonk* and rolled across the tiles. Odile made a noise halfway between a laugh and a moan, and it came out so ridiculous that she laughed harder, forehead pressed to Fen's, breath coming ragged and uneven.

"We're going to have to write them a card," she managed. "*Sorry about your bathroom. Lovely party. Your towels are very absorbent.*"

Her fingers dug into Fen's back. Her laughter broke off halfway through and didn't come back. For a long, unsteady stretch she didn't say anything at all. She clung on with her eyes squeezed shut and her mouth open against Fen's neck. The music thudded up through the floorboards and her pulse thudded to match it, and her ankle was hooked so tightly around Fen's leg that it was a wonder either of them was still standing.

Then there was a knock at the door.

Two sharp raps, and then silence.

Odile's eyes flew open. For one suspended second neither of them moved. The only sound in the bathroom was her breathing, fast and shallow, and the distant, oblivious bassline.

"Just a *minute!*" she called out, in a voice that was pitched about an octave too high, cracked in the middle, and could not have sounded more like exactly what it was.

Whoever was outside didn't answer. But the laughter that drifted through the door as they walked away, not bothering to hide it, was unmistakably Priya's.

Odile dropped her face into Fen's shoulder and made a long, anguished, muffled sound of pure mortification. Her whole body shook with it. She didn't let go of them for a second.

"I'm never leaving this room," she said into their skin. "We live here now. This is our home. We'll raise the seashells as our own."

She lifted her head at last. Her face was pink to the ears and her mascara had smudged at the corners, and she looked more thoroughly delighted than she had all night. She kissed Fen once, hard, and her voice dropped back into that warm, dark register as she pulled them close again.

"...She said a *minute*," Odile whispered. "I didn't say *which* minute."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I can't help laughing, low and breathless. "She's going to be waiting outside with a timer." My hand finds hers against the door, lacing our fingers together. "We should probably make this one count."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile squeezed their fingers so hard her knuckles went white.

"A *timer*," she breathed, and the laugh that followed was shaky and thin, running out of air halfway through. "Oh, she absolutely would. She'd bring a stopwatch. She'd *announce the results*."

But she didn't let go of Fen's hand, and she didn't look at the door again. Her other arm wound around their shoulders and pulled them in until her mouth was right against their ear, and whatever she'd meant to say next dissolved into something that wasn't a word at all.

After that, she stopped talking.

It was the quietest she'd been all night, which wasn't very quiet. Her breath came in short, broken pieces against Fen's neck. Her fingers flexed and tightened in theirs, over and over, like she was holding onto the only fixed point in a room that had started to tilt. The seashells chattered in their dish. The mirror fogged. Somewhere far below, the whole party started singing again, the same song as before, and Odile didn't notice it at all.

When she finally went over, she tried valiantly to be discreet about it. She pressed her face into Fen's shoulder and bit down on the curve of it. It helped very slightly. The sound still came out low and long and unmistakable, and for a few seconds afterward she just held on, trembling, her grip on Fen's hand fierce enough to hurt.

Then, slowly, she started to laugh.

It started as a hiccup against Fen's skin and built into a helpless, full-body shake, her forehead dropping against their collarbone.

"Well," she croaked. "*That* one was in the group chat. That one was *definitely* in the group chat."

She lifted her head. Her hair was a disaster. One earring was missing. There was a red mark on Fen's shoulder the exact shape of her teeth, and she looked at it, winced, and pressed an apologetic kiss to it, then another, then a third, just to be thorough.

"Sorry," she whispered, not sorry at all. "Occupational hazard."

For a moment she simply leaned there against the door and breathed, their fingers still laced together, her thumb moving in slow, absent circles over Fen's knuckles. The flush on her cheeks had spread down her throat. She looked soft and wrecked and entirely, stupidly happy.

Then reality arrived.

Odile looked around the bathroom and saw it all at once: the hand towel on the floor, the shampoo bottle under the sink, the fogged mirror, the seashell soaps knocked into a sad little heap. Fen's shirt was draped over the edge of the bathtub like a surrender flag. Her own phone was still buzzing faintly in the folded towels.

"Oh my god," she said. "It looks like a crime scene. It looks like a *raccoon* got in."

She disentangled herself with great reluctance, hauled her dress back up over both shoulders, and got the strap back in place on the second try. She went for the shampoo bottle first and set it on the edge of the bath, label facing outward, as if that were the thing that would give them away. She rescued the towel and hung it back on its ring, then stood back and squinted at it. It hung slightly crooked. She adjusted it. It was still crooked. She gave up.

Then she picked up the phone, turned it over, and looked at the screen.

Her face went through about five expressions in two seconds.

"Twenty-three messages," she reported faintly. "*Twenty-three.* There *is* a group chat. It's called..." She stopped. She pressed her lips together. Her shoulders started to shake again. "It's called *'Bathroom Update 🚨'*. Priya's been doing *commentary*."

She turned the screen toward Fen so they could see it, then snatched it back before they could read more than a line, clutching it to her chest.

"No. No, I can't. I'll die." She tossed Fen's shirt at them with her free hand, grinning. "Get dressed. We're going down there, and we're going to be *extremely dignified* about this."

She turned to the mirror, wiped a clear patch in the fog with the side of her fist, and tried to fix her hair with her fingers. It made no difference whatsoever. Her lipstick was entirely gone. She considered her reflection for a long moment, sighed, and reached for Fen's hand again.

"Okay," she said, standing by the door, one hand on the little brass lock. "Game plan. We walk out like nothing happened. We don't make eye contact with anyone. If Priya says *anything*..." She paused, thinking hard. "...we tell her the soap fell."

She glanced back over her shoulder, eyes bright, mouth already twitching.

"Ready?"

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get my hand between her legs and she bites down on my shoulder to keep quiet, which works for about thirty seconds.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile had got as far as turning the lock halfway back when Fen's hand slid under the hem of her dress, and her whole carefully constructed game plan went straight out of her head.

"Oh, you *absolute*..." she started, and didn't finish, because the rest of the sentence turned into a sharp little intake of breath.

She let go of the lock. It clicked back into place under her fingers, more by luck than intention. The phone was still clutched in her other hand, and for a wild moment she had no idea what to do with it, so she simply pressed it flat against the door beside her head like she was holding the whole house shut.

Then she turned her face into Fen's shoulder and bit down, on the other side this time, where there wasn't a mark yet. She was nothing if not fair.

It worked. For a while she was genuinely, impressively silent. Her breath came hot and uneven through her nose. Her free hand found Fen's hip and gripped hard. Her knees had gone unreliable, and she leaned back against the door to keep herself upright, eyes squeezed shut, jaw locked, the very picture of someone determined to win a game she'd already publicly forfeited.

The phone buzzed against the wood.

Odile flinched, lost her grip on it entirely, and it slid down the door and landed on the bathmat with a soft, undignified *flump*. She didn't even look. Her teeth loosened on Fen's shoulder, her mouth fell open against their skin, and the sound that came out of her was low and cracked and carried a lot farther than she'd have liked.

"*Dammit*," she gasped, half laughing, half something else entirely. "Thirty seconds. I had it for thirty whole..."

That was as far as she got. Her head thumped back against the door. Her fingers slid up into Fen's hair and held on, and whatever dignity she'd planned to take downstairs dissolved completely. She wasn't laughing now. She was saying Fen's name, quietly at first and then not quietly at all, in a voice that had given up any pretence of discretion.

Below them the party sang on, blissfully unaware. Or at least mostly unaware.

When it was over she sagged against the door, boneless, forehead resting on Fen's, and stayed there for a long moment with her eyes closed. Then one of them opened, bright and slightly dazed.

"That," she said hoarsely, "was *cheating*. I was at the *door*. I had a *game plan*."

On the bathmat, the phone buzzed again. And again.

Odile looked down at it. She looked back up at Fen. The grin crept across her face slowly, wrecked and radiant and utterly without shame.

"Leave it," she whispered. "Let Priya wonder." She kissed them, soft and lingering, her hand still tangled in their hair. "We're definitely going to need another minute now."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I pull back just enough to look at her, breathless and grinning. "Your game plan sucked anyway." I nudge her phone with my foot. "How many messages now?"

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile gasped in outrage, or tried to. It came out mostly as a wheeze, because she hadn't quite got her breath back yet.

"My game plan was *flawless*," she said. "It was sabotaged. By a known saboteur. Who has a documented history of sabotage." She poked Fen in the chest with one finger, then left the finger there, because Fen's chest was warm and she was still leaning on them fairly heavily.

She looked down at the phone on the bathmat. It lit up again as Fen nudged it, cheerfully face-up now, the screen glowing like an accusation.

"Don't," she warned it.

It buzzed.

Odile sighed the sigh of a woman facing her fate, bent down to retrieve it (holding the edge of the sink for support, because her knees had not yet been consulted about any of this), and squinted at the screen.

"Thirty-one," she reported. Then she scrolled, and her face did something complicated. "Oh no. Oh, no, it's worse. People have *joined*. Marcus has joined. Marcus doesn't even *like* group chats." She scrolled further, lips moving as she read. "Priya says, and I quote, 'update: they said just a minute, it has been eleven minutes.' And then Dev said 'rookie error, never give a time estimate.' And then..."

She stopped. She pressed the back of her hand to her mouth.

"...And then *Sam* said, and this is *Sam*, whose *bathroom* this *is*: 'if anyone touches my seashells I'm calling the police.'"

Odile stared at the dish on the counter. The seashells stared back, in their sad little collapsed heap.

Very slowly, very carefully, as if defusing a bomb, she reached over and rearranged them one by one, nudging each into a neat row, until they looked more or less exactly as they had when she'd walked in. She stepped back and considered them. She adjusted the last one a millimetre to the left.

"There," she whispered. "We were never here."

The phone buzzed again in her hand. She glanced at it and her shoulders began to shake.

"Priya just posted a *countdown*. She's at the bottom of the stairs. She says she's giving us 'until the end of this song, out of respect.'" Odile listened. The bassline downstairs was building toward something that sounded suspiciously like a final chorus. "That's not very long. That's really not very long at all."

She held the phone up between them like evidence, screen glowing, her hair still a catastrophe and her face still pink to the collarbones, and grinned at Fen with the specific, reckless joy of someone who had absolutely nothing left to lose.

"So," she said. "Option one: we go down now, with *some* dignity, and I lie about the soap." She tilted her head. "Option two: I reply to the group chat."

Her thumb hovered over the keyboard. Her eyebrows went up.

"Your call," she said. "But I'll warn you now, if it's option two, I'm sending a thumbs up."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Stop worrying about the noise," she says, "and get on with it," so I get her leg up over my hip and stop being careful about how much sound either of us is making.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile had made up her mind somewhere between the thumbs-up and Fen's face, and the decision showed.

She pressed send without looking. The little *whoosh* of the message going out was the last thing she paid attention to. The phone went sailing over her shoulder into the bathtub, where it landed on Fen's shirt with a muffled thump and, very faintly, buzzed.

"Stop worrying about the noise," she said, fingers already hooked in Fen's belt loops and pulling, "and get on with it."

When her leg came up over Fen's hip she laughed, one short, startled, delighted bark, and grabbed the edge of the sink behind her to keep her balance. The seashells, so carefully rearranged, jumped in their dish. She didn't even flinch this time.

"Oh, *sorry*, Sam," she gasped, not sorry in the slightest, and then she stopped apologising to anyone.

She had been trying all night, in her own chaotic way, to be quiet. Now she stopped trying, and the difference was immediate and total. Her head fell back against the mirror with a soft knock. Her hand slid from the sink to Fen's shoulder to the back of their neck, gripping hard, pulling them in closer. The sounds she made weren't stifled or bitten back any more. They were loud and uneven and honest, the kind that would have made her go scarlet an hour ago. She laughed in the middle of them, breathless, because it was ridiculous and wonderful and because the song downstairs was climbing and climbing toward its big finish like it was racing them.

"Final chorus," she panted against Fen's mouth. "Oh god, that's the final chorus, she's going to..."

She lost the end of the sentence. Her ankle locked tight behind Fen's thigh. Her other hand found the wall and pressed flat against it, fingers spread, and she said Fen's name in a voice that wasn't remotely suitable for a guest bathroom at a friend's party. Then she said it again, louder, because apparently she'd decided that if she was going to lose, she was going to lose spectacularly.

Downstairs, the whole party hit the last big note together.

So did Odile. Her timing was so perfect that afterward, clinging to Fen with her face buried in their neck and her whole body trembling, she couldn't tell whether the cheer that went up from below was for the song or for her.

The music faded. In the silence that followed, it was very, very quiet.

Then, faint but distinct, from somewhere at the bottom of the stairs, a single slow clap.

Odile lifted her head. Her eyes were wet, her hair was beyond saving, and her mouth was trembling with a laugh she was holding in by sheer force of will.

"Was that," she whispered, "a *standing ovation*?"

The clapping stopped. Footsteps started up the stairs, unhurried and deliberate.

Odile didn't move an inch. She stayed exactly where she was, leg still hooked around Fen, arms still around their neck, and grinned at them like the world's least repentant criminal.

"Well," she breathed. "I did say we should make it worth it."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I lift my head, listening to the approaching footsteps. "We have maybe thirty seconds before she's at the door," I murmur, then kiss her, hard. "Quick. Game plan."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The kiss knocked the last coherent thought clean out of Odile's head, and for one precious second she forgot there was a staircase at all.

Then a floorboard creaked. Step four, the one she'd nearly missed on the way up. She'd know it anywhere now.

"Game plan," she gasped, unhooking her leg from Fen's hip with all the grace of a newborn deer. Her knee buckled. She caught the sink. The seashells rattled in solidarity. "Right. Yes. Game plan. I am a woman of *strategy*."

She yanked the strap of her dress back onto her shoulder, missed, and tried again. Step six creaked.

"Shirt!" She lunged for the bathtub, fished Fen's shirt out from under her own phone, which was still buzzing faintly and now had a damp patch on it, and shoved it into their arms. "Put that on. Inside out is fine. Inside out is *better*. It's a fashion choice. You're very avant-garde."

Step eight. Odile spun toward the mirror, took one look at her hair, and made a small noise of despair. She raked both hands through it. It got worse. She gave up and turned on the tap, full blast, water thundering into the basin.

"Hand washing," she hissed over the noise, pumping soap into her palm with frantic enthusiasm. "We were washing our hands. Very thoroughly. For a very long time. We're extremely hygienic people, Fen, it's a whole *thing* with us."

Step ten. Step eleven. Her lather had reached alarming proportions.

"And if that doesn't work," she went on, voice climbing, "you have a migraine. No. *I* have a migraine. I've been lying on the cool tiles and you've been nursing me back to health. That's why it sounded like..." She paused, considered what exactly it had sounded like, and her face crumpled. "Oh god, nobody's going to believe the migraine."

The footsteps reached the top of the stairs. They came unhurriedly down the hall and stopped directly outside the door.

Odile went rigid, hands full of foam, tap still roaring.

A knock. Three polite little raps this time, almost gentle, which was somehow far more menacing.

"Knock knock," came Priya's voice through the wood, bright and sweet and absolutely, unbearably smug. "Housekeeping. Just checking whether you two need fresh *towels*."

Odile's eyes went enormous. She looked at Fen. She looked at the door. She looked down at the hand towel, still hanging crooked on its ring, and a laugh started building behind her pressed-together lips with the inevitability of a sneeze.

She turned off the tap. In the sudden silence she could hear Priya breathing on the other side, clearly delighted, clearly *waiting*.

Odile rinsed her hands with enormous dignity, dried them on her dress, and squared her shoulders. She put her hand on the little brass lock.

"Final answer," she whispered to Fen, barely moving her lips. "The soap fell. We stick to the soap. Whatever happens, *whatever she says*, the soap fell and we were very upset about it."

She took a breath, lifted her chin, and called through the door in her most gracious hostess voice.

"No thank you, Priya! We're *fine!* Everything's *completely* normal in here!"

Behind her, the phone in the bathtub buzzed one last time, loud against the porcelain.

Odile shut her eyes. "...Okay," she said, very quietly, in a voice that was starting to crack. "On three, we open it. One..."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: Somebody tries the handle and neither of us stops. "Don't," she says, meaning don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
"One..."

That was as far as the count got.

The handle turned against her palm. It caught on the lock with a small metallic *clack*, and at the same moment Fen's hand found her again. Odile's breath left her all at once. Her forehead dropped against the door, cheek pressed to the painted wood, and the rest of the countdown stayed stuck in her throat.

"*Don't*," she whispered, fierce and urgent. Fen didn't stop, and she hadn't wanted them to, and they both knew it.

The handle jiggled again, testing. Priya was an inch of wood away, and Odile could feel the vibration of it against her own ribs. She bit down hard on her lower lip. Her free hand scrabbled for purchase and found Fen's wrist, not pulling it away but pressing it closer, holding it exactly where it was.

"Odile?" Priya called, sing-song. "You've gone awfully quiet. Blink twice if you're being held hostage."

Odile made a sound that was not a blink.

It came out of her low and ragged, half a laugh and half a moan, muffled against the door and not muffled nearly enough. On the other side there was a pause. Then a gasp of pure, scandalised glee.

"Oh, you are *not*," Priya said. "You are *not*. Right. I'm leaving. I'm leaving *immediately*, I'm going downstairs, and I am telling *everyone*."

Her footsteps retreated at speed, accompanied by helpless cackling, and thundered down the stairs. Every creak came back up in reverse. Step eleven. Step eight. Step four.

Odile didn't hear most of them. Her whole world had narrowed to the cool door under her cheek, the heat of Fen at her back, and the slow, relentless rhythm of their fingers. Her hips moved to meet it without her permission. The brass lock rattled faintly in its housing with every shift of her weight, and she found that unbearably funny and unbearably good in equal measure, so that she laughed and gasped and couldn't untangle one from the other.

"She's *telling everyone*," she panted, delighted and wrecked. "Fen. Fen, she's going to tell *Sam*..."

Her voice broke on the name. Her knees went. She'd have slid down the door entirely if Fen hadn't been holding her up, and she let them. She let her whole weight go back into them, head tipped against their shoulder, throat bared, eyes squeezed shut, and stopped pretending that there was any part of her left that cared about being quiet.

It built fast this time, sharp and bright. She said Fen's name, and then something that wasn't a word at all. Her nails dug crescents into their wrist. For a long, shuddering moment she forgot the bathroom, the party, the group chat and the seashells, and there was only this. The sound she made when she broke was loud enough to rattle the lock again, and she didn't care. She had nothing left to hide.

Downstairs, faintly, a whole room erupted into cheering.

Odile hung there against Fen, trembling, gasping, and started to giggle. It was weak and hiccupping at first and then helpless, her whole body shaking with it.

"That was for *us*," she wheezed. "That cheer. That was *definitely* for us."

She turned in Fen's arms at last, slumping back against the door, and looked up at them through the wreckage of her hair. Her face was blotchy pink from forehead to collarbone. Her mascara had given up entirely. She had never looked happier in her life.

"I'm going to have to move to a different country," she said. "Change my name. Grow a beard."

In the bathtub, the phone lit up and began to buzz continuously, one message after another, like a tiny alarm going off.

Odile didn't even look at it. She hooked a finger into the collar of Fen's inside-out shirt and tugged them down for a kiss, slow and sweet and tasting of salt.

"Two," she murmured against their mouth, picking the count up right where she'd dropped it, eyes glinting.

She didn't say three. She just waited, grinning, one hand resting on the little brass lock, to see what Fen would do.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I kiss her back, slow and deep, before pulling away just enough to murmur, "One." My hand finds the lock and turns it with a soft click. "Ready?"

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The lock turned with the same small, significant click it had made an hour ago. It sounded completely different now. It sounded like a verdict.

Odile stared at it. Then she stared at Fen.

"You said *one*," she whispered, scandalised. "You skipped *two*. I *said* two. That's not how countdowns *work*, Fen, there are *rules*..."

But she was already moving. She lunged for the bathtub, fished out the phone (still buzzing, now slightly damp, the screen a solid waterfall of notifications), and shoved it into her pocket without looking. She spun back to the counter and gave the seashells one final nudge, a benediction. She yanked the crooked towel straight. It fell off the ring. She hung it back up, crooked, and left it.

Then she stood in front of the door, took Fen's hand, laced their fingers together tight, and breathed out through her nose like a diver on the high board.

"Ready," she said. "Extremely dignified. Soap fell. Go."

She opened the door.

The hallway was empty. The fig-and-cedar candle still flickered on its little table. The wedding photos still lined the walls, the couple still mid-laugh under their fairy lights, and Odile couldn't look them in the eye.

Something sat on the floor just outside the threshold.

It was a hand towel, fresh and fluffy and folded into a perfect square. On top of it, clearly torn from the back of a takeaway menu, lay a note in Priya's loopy handwriting:

*For after. You're welcome. 10/10, would eavesdrop again. — Housekeeping xx*

Odile made a sound like a kettle reaching the boil. She bent, picked up the towel, and clutched it to her chest with both hands, note and all, like a bouquet.

"I'm keeping this," she said faintly. "I'm having it *framed*."

They made it to the top of the stairs. Odile squared her shoulders, tucked the towel under one arm, and started down with enormous poise, chin high, one hand trailing elegantly along the banister.

Step four creaked.

Below them, the music was still going, but the conversation stopped. It didn't stop all at once. It rippled outward from the bottom of the stairs, one cluster of people at a time, heads turning, glasses pausing halfway to mouths, until the whole living room had gone quiet except for the song. Someone near the kitchen was very obviously holding up a phone.

Priya stood dead centre at the foot of the stairs, arms folded, beaming like a proud parent at a graduation.

Sam stood beside her, arms also folded, not beaming.

Odile stopped on the second-to-last step. For a long moment nobody said anything at all.

"The soap," Odile announced clearly, to the room at large, "fell."

Priya's face crumpled. Somebody in the back snorted wine out of their nose. Dev started a slow clap, and it spread, and within seconds the whole party was applauding, whistling, somebody banging a spoon on a saucepan. Marcus, who didn't even *like* group chats, raised his glass solemnly in salute.

Odile turned the colour of a stop sign. Then, because there was truly nothing left to lose, she let go of Fen's hand just long enough to sweep into a deep, theatrical curtsy on the stairs, the fresh towel held out to one side like a train.

The cheering doubled.

She straightened up, took Fen's hand again, and leaned in close enough to murmur under the noise, her voice shaking with suppressed laughter.

"Sam's looking at me. Sam is looking *directly* at me." She didn't turn her head. "Don't make eye contact. If she asks about the seashells, you *handle it*. I've done my part. I *curtsied*."

Her thumb stroked once across Fen's knuckles, warm and a little unsteady, and the glint in her eye said she wouldn't have traded a second of it.

"Also," she added, even more quietly, "we are *never* living this down, and I've never been so happy in my life."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I pull her in for a quick kiss right there on the stairs, the whole party watching. "Worth it," I say against her mouth, then raise my voice just enough for Sam to hear. "We'll buy you new soap."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The kiss landed right in the middle of the applause, and the room lost its mind.

Someone whooped. The saucepan-spoon person found a second, louder saucepan. Odile, who had just curtsied in front of thirty people and had apparently thought that was the most mortifying thing that could happen to her, discovered that it was not. She went from stop-sign red to something closer to a fire engine, and she kissed Fen back anyway, one hand fisted in their inside-out collar, because she had never once in her life known when to quit.

Then Fen raised their voice. Odile heard the words *new soap*, and every drop of blood in her body tried to leave through her feet.

Sam unfolded her arms very slowly.

The room went quiet again, the way it does when everyone collectively senses a boss fight. Priya pressed both hands over her mouth. Dev stopped clapping mid-clap, palms an inch apart.

"New soap," Sam repeated flatly.

"*Decorative* soap," Odile blurted, before she could stop herself. "Seashell-shaped. Artisanal. We'll find the *exact* ones. We'll go to..." She had no idea where anyone bought soap shaped like seashells. "...the *coast*."

Sam looked at her for a long, long moment. Then she looked at Fen. Then, pointedly, at the towel tucked under Odile's arm, and the note still sticking out of its folds in Priya's loopy handwriting.

"Those soaps," Sam said, "were a wedding present from my *grandmother*."

Odile made a small, dying noise.

Priya lost it. She doubled over, clutching Sam's arm for support, and wheezed, "They were *not*, she got them at *TK Maxx*, I was *there*..."

Sam's mouth twitched. She tried to hold it. She truly did. Odile watched the struggle play out across her face with the fellow-feeling of someone who'd been losing that exact battle all night, and when it finally cracked and Sam snorted, one undignified honk, Odile nearly sat down on the stairs out of sheer relief.

"You're *disgusting*," Sam told them both, with great warmth. "Both of you. Get down here. Someone get these idiots a drink."

Somebody did. The music swelled back up. The party closed around them like water, noise and hands and back-slaps and at least three people asking *how many minutes was it actually*. Odile answered every one of them with "the soap fell," in a voice that grew steadily less convincing, until by the fourth time she couldn't get past "the" without laughing.

She ended up wedged into the corner of the sofa with Fen, a glass of wine in one hand and the fresh towel folded neatly in her lap, where she had refused to let anyone take it. Her hair was still a disaster. One earring was still missing. She suspected it was in the bathtub, and she would never, ever be going back for it.

Her phone buzzed in her pocket. She pulled it out, glanced at the screen, and passed it wordlessly to Fen.

The group chat had been renamed. It no longer said *Bathroom Update 🚨*. It now said *The Soap Fell 🧼🐚*, and Sam had pinned a message to the top:

*Seashells are officially retired. Replacements due by Christmas. I will be checking.*

Odile leaned her head against Fen's shoulder, carefully, on the side without teeth marks, and sighed the long, contented sigh of a woman who had lost every game she'd played tonight and had somehow come out ahead anyway.

"Christmas," she murmured. "That gives us a few months to find the coast."

She tilted her face up, eyes bright over the rim of her glass, and a slow, dangerous grin spread across it.

"And their spare room," she added, very quietly, "doesn't have a lock at *all*."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I laugh into my wine, shaking my head. "You're terrible. I love you." My thumb brushes the back of her hand. "But we're buying that soap tomorrow."

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: fingertips slipping underneath to find warm skin

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: Her dress was mostly around her waist now

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: When it was over she sagged against the door

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: Her ankle locked tight behind Fen

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: the slow, relentless rhythm of their fingers

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The party had reached the stage where nobody would notice two people missing, which Odile pointed out approximately four seconds before doing something about it.

"The bathroom upstairs has a lock," she said, into Fen's ear, over the music.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Does it work?" I ask, already moving toward the stairs.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile caught Fen's hand on the way up and didn't let go of it.

The upstairs hall was dim and comparatively quiet, the party reduced to a low thump under the floorboards. She tried the bathroom door, found it empty, and pulled Fen in after her. The lock turned with a small, definite click that made her mouth twitch.

"Works," she said, already backing Fen against the door, her voice lower than it had been on the stairs and not nearly as controlled as she wanted it to be. Her hands settled at Fen's waist. "So. We should probably be very quiet."

She said it like a person who had already decided she was going to fail at that.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: ( OOC: Don't write my actions )

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's mouth found the corner of Fen's jaw, then the spot just under it, and she made a small, satisfied sound against the skin there that she clearly hadn't meant to let out.

She went still for half a second, listening — the music downstairs, the lock, nothing else — and then laughed once, quiet and a little wrecked, into Fen's neck.

"Okay," she whispered, which was not an apology. Her hands slid under the hem of Fen's shirt, warm and unhurried, thumbs tracing the line of skin just above the waistband. "That one doesn't count. That was a test."

She kissed Fen properly then, slower than the hallway had suggested she was capable of, one hand flattening against the door beside Fen's head so the wood took her weight. When she pulled back, her breathing was already worse than it should have been for how little they'd done.

"Tell me if you hear anyone," she said, and her fingers hooked, very lightly, in Fen's waistband. "I'm going to be busy failing the rest of the test."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get the door shut and her against it, and downstairs somebody turns the music up, which helps.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's back met the door and she made a sound that the music only mostly covered, half laugh and half something less polite.

"Oh, that's cheating," she said, low, her hands already in Fen's shirt again like the interruption had been an insult. The bass came up through the floor and she used it, rolling her hips once, unhurried, testing how much the door would give. It didn't. Her mouth curved. "Good. Stay there."

She kissed Fen like she had time and none of it, one thigh sliding between Fen's, her free hand braced flat on the wood beside Fen's shoulder so she wouldn't knock anything off the shelf and ruin the bit. When she broke the kiss she was breathing against Fen's mouth, worse than before, and she didn't bother pretending otherwise.

"Music helps," she whispered, and then, because she was incapable of leaving a good idea alone, she dragged her teeth lightly along Fen's jaw and let the next sound out on purpose — quiet, but not quiet enough, and entirely pleased with itself. "Doesn't help enough. Your problem now."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I laugh, breathless, and slide my hands under her shirt, splaying my fingers across her ribs. "You're a menace." I kiss her again, hard enough to taste the cheap party beer on her lips.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile made a noise into the kiss that she would have denied later, low and rough, and the cheap beer taste didn't slow her down at all. Her ribs jumped under Fen's hands. She pressed into them instead of away, like she wanted the span of those fingers mapped and kept.

"Menace is generous," she said when she got her mouth back, the words landing crooked against Fen's. Her own hands had gone still under Fen's shirt for half a second, distracted, and then they remembered what they were doing and slid higher, palms warm, unhurried on purpose. "I was going for subtle."

She wasn't. The music thumped under the floor and she matched it without meaning to, a slow shift of her hips against Fen's thigh, the door solid at her back. A laugh caught in her throat and came out thinner than she wanted. She bit it off against Fen's lower lip, not quite successfully.

"God," she whispered, and it wasn't a performance. Her forehead tipped to Fen's. One hand left the shirt long enough to check the lock again — a quick, blind fumble, the click of metal under her fingers — and then it was back, worse than before, hooking at the waistband like she'd lost the argument with herself. "If you keep doing that with your hands I'm going to forget the entire point of the lock."

She kissed Fen again before the sentence could turn into anything useful, open and a little messy, and the sound she let out this time was quiet only by accident.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: There isn't room to do this properly and we don't let that stop us. Enough clothes come off to be a problem if anyone knocks.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's laugh came out against Fen's mouth and died there, thin and wrecked, because the clothes had stopped being a joke and started being an obstacle she was losing to in real time.

"This is a terrible idea," she said, which would have landed better if her hands hadn't already committed to it. Fabric bunched, caught, got shoved somewhere it wouldn't trip them. Her bare shoulder met the cold of the door and she hissed, then bit the sound off against Fen's collarbone like that solved anything. It didn't. The music downstairs covered the thump of her head tipping back; it did not cover the breath she let out after.

She went still for one second — lock, hall, nothing — and the stillness cost her. When she moved again it was closer, less clever, one knee braced where it would hold, her forehead pressed to Fen's so she wouldn't have to negotiate the angle out loud. Her hands were not steady. She noticed and didn't fix it.

"If someone knocks," she whispered, and the rest of the sentence fell apart into a sound she hadn't budgeted for, low and honest and much too loud for a locked door at a friend's party. She clapped a hand over her own mouth, eyes bright, shoulders shaking with a laugh she was physically refusing to finish. The hand didn't stay. It went back to Fen like it had better work to do.

"Okay," she breathed, ruined, pleased, already failing the next one. "Okay. Don't — just — stay with me. I'm not going to be quiet and I need you to not let me care."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I drag my hand up her spine, pressing her closer. "Then don't be quiet," I murmur against her ear, my own voice rough. "But I'm not letting go."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's answer was a sound she didn't bother catching this time, low and rough against Fen's ear, and the hand at her spine made it worse in the best way. She pressed into it, into Fen, the cold door at her back and the warm line of Fen's body taking the rest of her weight.

"Good," she managed, and it came out shaky. Her fingers had found skin again and stayed there, gripping, not subtle, not clever. The music thumped under the floorboards and she stopped trying to match it. Her hips moved because they had to, a slow, uneven drag, and the breath she let out after was too loud and she heard it and laughed once, helpless, into the curve of Fen's neck.

"I'm not—" The sentence broke. She bit down lightly at Fen's shoulder to keep the next one in and failed anyway, a thin, wrecked noise that the bass only half-covered. Her free hand fumbled up, found Fen's jaw, held there like she needed the anchor. "God. Okay. Okay."

She kissed Fen, open and a little clumsy, tasting the laugh still caught between them, and when she pulled back her forehead stayed pressed to Fen's. Her breathing was a mess. She didn't apologize for it.

"Don't let go," she whispered, and it wasn't a joke this time, just the truth of it, her voice frayed and pleased and nowhere near quiet. "I've got you. I've— just stay right there."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get my hand between her legs and she bites down on my shoulder to keep quiet, which works for about thirty seconds.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's teeth stayed on Fen's shoulder for as long as she could make them, a desperate, shaking press that did nothing for the sound trying to climb out of her throat. Thirty seconds was generous. The hand between her legs found her already a mess, and the first real stroke pulled a broken noise out of her that she swallowed against skin and then lost anyway, thin and high and nowhere near quiet enough.

Her hips jerked into it before she could stop them. One hand fisted in Fen's shirt at the shoulder; the other slapped flat against the door beside Fen's head and stayed there, knuckles white, like the wood might keep her honest. It didn't. Her forehead dropped to Fen's, breath coming apart in hot little bursts against Fen's mouth, and she laughed once — wrecked, helpless, almost a sob — when the next pass of those fingers made her thighs shake.

"Fuck," she whispered, and it cracked in the middle. She bit her own lip hard enough to hurt and still couldn't kill the sound that followed, low and raw, muffled only because she'd turned her face into Fen's neck. The music thumped under the floor. It wasn't enough. She knew it and rolled her hips into Fen's hand anyway, greedy and unsteady, chasing it. "Don't— don't stop. God, don't stop. I'll be— I'll try—"

She wasn't trying. Her free hand found the back of Fen's neck and held on, and the next breath she let out was Fen's name, barely voiced, already failing the rest of the way.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I feel her come apart against me, and it’s beautiful. I keep her pinned between me and the door, swallowing her ragged gasps. “I’ve got you,” I murmur, my voice rough against her ear.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile came apart against the door and against Fen, and for a few seconds she forgot the party existed at all.

The sound she made wasn't a word. It broke against Fen's mouth, ragged and too loud, and her hips jerked once, hard, before the rest of her went tight and shaking. Her hand fisted in Fen's shirt. Her forehead pressed hard to Fen's. The bass under the floor kept going like it hadn't noticed, and she rode the aftershocks out against Fen's hand with small, helpless movements she couldn't have stopped if someone had knocked.

She tried to swallow the next breath. Failed. A thin, wrecked laugh caught in her throat and came out against Fen's ear instead, wet and unsteady.

"Okay," she managed, and it barely qualified as a word. Her thighs were still trembling. She stayed pinned where Fen had her, bare shoulder cold against the door, and didn't even pretend she was ready to move. One hand found Fen's jaw again, clumsy, holding on. "Okay. I've— God."

Downstairs, somebody laughed at something. The sound of it snapped a little of the room back into focus. Odile went still, listening, breathing too hard, and then she bit her lip and looked at Fen with bright, ruined eyes, mouth curved like she'd just gotten away with something she absolutely hadn't.

"That," she whispered, voice frayed and pleased and nowhere near recovered, "was not quiet." Her thumb traced Fen's lower lip, shaky. "Your turn to be the responsible one. I'm not done with you, and I cannot be trusted with that lock."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Stop worrying about the noise," she says, "and get on with it," so I get her leg up over my hip and stop being careful about how much sound either of us is making.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's breath left her in a rush when her leg came up, the new angle pulling a sound out of her she didn't even try to catch. It cracked against the door, low and wrecked, and the music downstairs did almost nothing for it.

"Oh—" Her head tipped back. One hand scrabbled at Fen's shoulder and held on, the other braced flat on the wood so she wouldn't slide. The cold of the door hit her bare spine and she hissed, then laughed, thin and helpless, because the laugh turned into something else halfway through. Her hips rolled into it without permission. "Fuck. Okay. Okay, that's—"

She bit down on the rest of it and failed. The next sound was Fen's name, barely shaped, too loud for a locked bathroom and she knew it and didn't care. Her thigh tightened where it hooked, pulling Fen closer, greedier, the rhythm already uneven. Downstairs someone shouted over the bass. Odile heard it and pressed her open mouth to Fen's jaw anyway, breathing hard, shaking, the laugh still caught in her throat.

"Don't be careful," she whispered, and it came out ruined, pleased, nowhere near quiet. Her fingers fisted in Fen's hair. "God, don't you dare be careful. I've got you. I've— just—"

The sentence broke on another sound she let the door take, bright-eyed and already gone.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I press her harder against the door, my own control fraying. The noise we're making is reckless and I love it. "That's it," I growl against her skin, feeling her come undone again.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile came undone against the door for the second time with a sound she didn't even try to catch.

It broke out of her rough and open, Fen's name somewhere in it and then nothing that was a word at all, and her whole body went tight around the new angle — thigh locked over Fen's hip, fingers fisted hard in Fen's hair, the cold door taking the slap of her free hand when she couldn't hold still. The bass under the floor didn't cover it. She heard herself and laughed, wrecked and bright and helpless, right through the middle of it.

"Fuck— that's—" Her head knocked back against the wood. She didn't care. Her hips jerked into Fen's and stayed there, chasing the aftershocks in small, greedy rolls she couldn't have stopped, breath coming apart in hot bursts against Fen's mouth. A thin, shaking noise climbed out of her throat and she let it. "God. God, don't— don't stop being like that."

Downstairs, the music dipped for a second between songs. The quiet made the sound of her breathing enormous. Odile froze, forehead pressed to Fen's, eyes wide and ruined, and then the track kicked back in and she dissolved into a laugh that was half a sob, shoulders shaking, still pinned exactly where Fen had her.

"Okay," she whispered, voice frayed to nothing, mouth curved like she'd lost a bet she was thrilled to lose. Her hand found Fen's jaw, clumsy and warm, thumb unsteady on the corner of Fen's mouth. "That one was loud. I don't care. I don't—" She kissed Fen, open and messy and still trembling, and when she pulled back she was already moving again, slower, greedier, nowhere near finished. "Your turn to fall apart. I'm not letting go either."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: Somebody tries the handle and neither of us stops. "Don't," she says, meaning don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile went rigid for half a heartbeat when the handle turned — a short, useless rattle against the lock — and the sound of it went straight through her, hot and stupid and nowhere near enough to make her stop.

"Occupied," she called, and it came out wrecked, too thin, cracking in the middle because Fen hadn't stopped and she hadn't asked them to. Her thigh stayed hooked. Her hips rolled into the next thrust like the door didn't exist. "Don't," she said again, lower, into Fen's mouth this time, meaning it. "Don't you dare."

Whoever it was tried the handle once more. The lock held. Odile heard a muffled, annoyed sound from the hall and then footsteps going, and the relief hit her so hard she laughed, bright and broken, right as Fen drove into her again and the laugh turned into a moan she didn't even try to swallow.

"Fuck— they heard me," she whispered, and she sounded thrilled about it, voice shaking, forehead knocking lightly against Fen's. Her hand fisted in Fen's hair. The cold door bit her spine every time she got pushed back into it, and she used that, braced, and met the next stroke instead of riding it out. The angle was clumsy and perfect. She was wet enough that the sound of it was obscene in the small room, a soft, slick rhythm under the bass, and she heard it and clenched around Fen and made it worse on purpose.

"Right there," she got out, and then she lost the rest of the sentence. Her free hand slid down between them, found herself, and she didn't have the patience to be shy about it — two fingers, tight circles, matching Fen, greedy and uneven. The first pass pulled a high, thin sound out of her that the music did nothing for. She bit Fen's shoulder, failed to keep the next one in, and let it go against skin: Fen's name, then a curse, then nothing but breath.

"I'm gonna— God, I'm—" Her thigh trembled where it locked over Fen's hip. She chased it, hips snapping, fingers slipping, the door thumping once under her shoulder hard enough that she knew, distantly, that anyone still in the hall would have heard that too. She didn't care. The second crest hit sharper than the first, meaner, and she came with her mouth open against Fen's neck, a raw, shaking sound she couldn't have killed if the whole party had been standing outside. Her whole body locked, pulsing around Fen, thighs shaking, the hand between her legs stuttering and then pressing hard as the aftershocks rolled through her in hot, helpless waves.

She didn't go soft. She stayed pinned there, breathing like she'd run, and when she could move her hand again she dragged it up Fen's chest, possessive, still trembling.

"Your turn," she said, hoarse, mouth curved, eyes bright and ruined. She rolled her hips, slow and deliberate, still clenched, still not quiet. "Come on. I want them to hear you too. Don't hold it. I've got the door. I've got you. Fall apart."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I groan into her shoulder, my hips stuttering as her words push me over the edge. The sound I make is raw and unguarded—let 'em hear. My fingers dig into her hip, holding her against the door as I shudder through it. "Fuck, Odile."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile felt it when Fen went — the stutter of those hips, the fingers digging into her hip, the raw sound of her name pressed into her shoulder — and the noise she made in answer was low and wrecked and entirely too pleased.

"There," she breathed, holding Fen through it, one hand still fisted in hair, the other braced on the door so neither of them slid. She rolled her hips once, slow, taking the last of it, and bit her own lip against a laugh that came out anyway, thin and shaking, into the curve of Fen's neck. "God. That was— they definitely heard that."

The bass kicked back in downstairs. Somewhere in the hall a floorboard creaked and moved on. Odile stayed pinned where she was, bare shoulder cold against the wood, thighs still trembling, breathing like she'd sprinted. She didn't let go. Her mouth found Fen's jaw, open and a little clumsy, and she kissed the corner of it like she was checking Fen was still there.

"Okay," she whispered, voice frayed to almost nothing, bright-eyed and ruined and grinning against skin. "Okay. Lock held. We're not dead. I'm—" A helpless little sound cut her off as an aftershock rolled through her and she pressed closer instead of away. "I'm not moving yet. Don't you either."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I let my forehead rest against the door beside her head, breathing hard. My hands slide down to her waist, holding her steady as my own legs feel shaky. "Yeah," I breathe out, a rough laugh escaping. "That lock earned its keep."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile let out a breath that was half a laugh and half the last of the shaking, her forehead still tipped toward Fen's, the door cold at her back and not nearly as interesting as the hands at her waist.

"It did," she said, and it came out frayed, pleased, nowhere near the volume of everything that had come before it. She shifted her weight and immediately regretted it — an aftershock rolled through her, small and mean, and she pressed closer instead of pretending she had legs. "God. Don't look so steady. I'm using you as architecture."

Downstairs the track changed. A voice called someone's name that wasn't either of theirs and got an answer from the kitchen. Odile listened for half a second, then dismissed it, mouth finding the corner of Fen's jaw in a kiss that was more check-in than anything else. Her thumb traced an absent, unsteady line at Fen's hip.

"Five more minutes," she whispered, bright-eyed and ruined and grinning against skin like she'd won something. "Then we put the clothes back on in the wrong order and walk out like we were looking for towels. If anyone asks, the lock sticks." She kissed Fen again, slower, the laugh still caught in it. "It doesn't. But they don't need to know that."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I laugh softly, my breath still uneven. "We can blame the towels, but my hair's a mess and you look..." I trail off, my thumb brushing her cheek. "Well, you look like we've been looking for towels really, really hard."
